def assemble(
    self,
    mesh: Mesh,
    operator: Operator,
    *,
    cell_type: CellType,
    n_dofs_per_node: int,
) -> MechanicalContribution:
    """Assemble prescribed displacements. ``operator`` is not used.

    Args:
        mesh: Tatva mesh the condition is applied to.
        operator: Ignored.
        cell_type: Cell shape of ``mesh``.
        n_dofs_per_node: Degrees of freedom stored at each node.

    Returns:
        ``fixed_dofs`` and ``fixed_values``. ``external_force`` stays ``None``.

    """
    _ = operator

    fixed_dofs: np.ndarray = self.dofs(
        mesh,
        cell_type=cell_type,
        n_dofs_per_node=n_dofs_per_node,
    )

    fixed_values: Array = jnp.full(
        fixed_dofs.shape,
        self.value,
    )

    return MechanicalContribution(
        fixed_dofs=fixed_dofs,
        fixed_values=fixed_values,
    )

def __init__(
    self,
    components: tuple[Component, ...] = ("x", "y", "z"),
) -> None:
    """Store the displacement components this condition acts on.

    Args:
        components: ``"x"``, ``"y"``, and ``"z"``, in any order.
            Default: all three.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``components`` is empty or contains another name.

    """
    if not components:
        raise ValueError("At least one component is required.")

    invalid = set(components) - {"x", "y", "z"}
    if invalid:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown components: {sorted(invalid)}.")

    self.components = components

class Generator:
    """Base for mesh generators that can draw the last mesh they built."""

    def __init__(self):
        """Create a generator with no mesh stored yet."""
        self._mesh: MeshFEMBase | None = None

    def _points_and_tetrahedra(
        self,
        cells: tuple[int, int, int],
        /,
    ) -> tuple[NDArray[np.float64], NDArray[np.int32]]:
        raise NotImplementedError

    def draw(
        self,
        cells: tuple[int, int, int] | None = None,
        *,
        backend: Backend = "pyvista",
        ax=None,
        plotter=None,
        wireframe: bool = True,
        show_edges: bool = False,
        show: bool = True,
        save: bool = False,
        save_location: str | Path | None = None,
        save_name: str | None = "mesh",
        save_format: str = "pdf",
        dpi: int = 300,
    ):
        """Plot the stored tetrahedral mesh, or build a preview mesh.

        ``cells=None`` draws the mesh from the last ``generate`` call. Passing
        ``cells``, or calling ``draw`` before ``generate``, builds a temporary mesh
        with those cell counts. The default preview is ``(12, 6, 4)`` cells in
        ``x``, ``y``, and ``z``. The temporary mesh is not stored.

        Args:
            cells: Number of cells along ``x``, ``y``, and ``z``. Default: the
                stored mesh, or ``(12, 6, 4)`` when none is stored.
            backend: ``"matplotlib"`` or ``"pyvista"``. Default: ``"pyvista"``.
            ax: Existing matplotlib axes. A new figure is created when omitted.
            plotter: Existing PyVista plotter. A new plotter is created when omitted.
            wireframe: Draw the mesh as a wireframe. Default: ``True``.
            show_edges: Draw element edges. Default: ``False``.
            show: Display the figure before returning. Default: ``True``.
            save: Write the figure to disk. Default: ``False``.
            save_location: Directory for the saved figure. Default: the working
                directory.
            save_name: File name without the extension. Default: ``"mesh"``.
            save_format: File extension. Default: ``"pdf"``.
            dpi: Resolution used when saving a matplotlib figure. Default: ``300``.

        Returns:
            The matplotlib axes or the PyVista plotter that holds the plot.

        Raises:
            TypeError: If the stored mesh container does not hold a single mesh.

        """
        if self._mesh is not None and cells is None:
            meshes = self._mesh.meshes
            if not isinstance(meshes, Mesh):
                raise TypeError(f"Expected one mesh, got {type(meshes).__name__}.")
            mesh = meshes
        else:
            cells = (12, 6, 4) if cells is None else cells
            points, tetrahedra = self._points_and_tetrahedra(cells)
            mesh = Mesh(
                jnp.asarray(points),
                elements=jnp.asarray(tetrahedra),
            )

        return plot_mesh(
            mesh,
            cell_type="tetra",
            backend=backend,
            ax=ax,
            plotter=plotter,
            show_edges=show_edges,
            wireframe=wireframe,
            lighting=False,
            show=show,
            save=save,
            save_location=save_location,
            save_name=save_name,
            save_format=save_format,
            dpi=dpi,
        )

class Dogbone(Generator):
    """A dogbone volume meshed as a warped box.

    The starting box has the grip width and the specimen thickness. Nodes are
    then moved in ``y`` to form the grips, cosine shoulders, and gauge, and in
    ``z`` to add a cosine weld cap. The bottom of the specimen is shifted to
    ``z = 0``.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        length: float,
        grip_width: float,
        grip_length: float,
        gauge_width: float,
        gauge_length: float,
        thickness: float,
        weld_width: float,
        weld_height: float,
        weld_center: float | None = None,
    ):
        """Store a validated dogbone specification.

        The arguments are checked by ``DogboneSpec``. ``weld_center=None`` becomes
        the midpoint of ``length``.

        Args:
            length: Total length along ``x``, in metres.
            grip_width: Full width of each grip.
            grip_length: Length of one grip, measured from the nearest end.
            gauge_width: Full width of the gauge section.
            gauge_length: Length of the gauge section.
            thickness: Specimen thickness before the weld cap is added.
            weld_width: Width of the weld cap along ``x``. ``0`` omits the weld.
            weld_height: Extra height of the weld cap. ``0`` omits the weld.
            weld_center: Center of the weld along ``x``. Default: the midpoint.

        Raises:
            InputError: If the lengths do not leave room for the shoulders, if
                ``gauge_width`` exceeds ``grip_width``, or if ``weld_center`` lies
                past ``length``.

        """
        super().__init__()

        # doubles the work in the .from_spec() classmethod, but ensures validation.
        spec = DogboneSpec(
            length=length,
            grip_width=grip_width,
            grip_length=grip_length,
            gauge_width=gauge_width,
            gauge_length=gauge_length,
            thickness=thickness,
            weld_width=weld_width,
            weld_height=weld_height,
            weld_center=weld_center,
        )

        self.length = spec.length
        self.grip_width = spec.grip_width
        self.grip_length = spec.grip_length
        self.gauge_width = spec.gauge_width
        self.gauge_length = spec.gauge_length
        self.thickness = spec.thickness
        self.weld_width = spec.weld_width
        self.weld_height = spec.weld_height
        weld_center = spec.weld_center
        if weld_center is None:
            weld_center = spec.length * 0.5
        self.weld_center = weld_center

    @classmethod
    def from_spec(cls, spec: DogboneSpec) -> Dogbone:
        """Build a dogbone from a validated specification.

        Args:
            spec: Specimen dimensions. ``weld_center`` may be ``None``.

        Returns:
            A ``Dogbone`` with those dimensions.

        """
        return cls(**attrs.asdict(spec))

    def _x_edges(
        self,
        n_cells: int,
        /,
        weld_refinement: int = 1,
        *,
        offset: float = 0.0,
    ) -> NDArray[np.float64]:
        if weld_refinement < 1:
            msg = f"'weld_refinement' must be >= 1, got {weld_refinement}."
            config.LOGGER.error(msg)
            raise InputError(msg)

        if offset < 0.0:
            msg = f"'offset' must be >= 0, got {offset}."
            config.LOGGER.error(msg)
            raise InputError(msg)

        edges: np.ndarray = np.linspace(0.0, self.length, n_cells + 1)

        if weld_refinement == 1 or self.weld_height <= 0.0 or self.weld_width <= 0.0:
            return edges

        half_width = 0.5 * self.weld_width
        weld_start = max(0.0, self.weld_center - half_width - offset)
        weld_end = min(self.length, self.weld_center + half_width + offset)

        cell_width = self.length / n_cells
        SNAP_TOLERANCE = 0.05 * cell_width

        # in cases where the closest cell edge is very close, don't add more cells.
        # instead, move the closest cell to the weld edge.
        for weld_edge in (weld_start, weld_end):
            nearest = np.argmin(np.abs(edges - weld_edge))

            if abs(edges[nearest] - weld_edge) <= SNAP_TOLERANCE:
                edges[nearest] = weld_edge
            else:
                edges = np.sort(np.append(edges, weld_edge))

        refined_edges = [edges[0]]

        # split cells in the weld region
        for left, right in pairwise(edges):
            if left >= weld_start and right <= weld_end:
                sub_edges = np.linspace(left, right, weld_refinement + 1)
                refined_edges.extend(sub_edges[1:])
            else:
                refined_edges.append(right)

        return np.asarray(refined_edges, dtype=np.float64)

    def _width_at_x(self, x: NDArray[np.floating] | float) -> NDArray[np.float64]:
        """Return the specimen width at each position along its length.

        The profile is the grip width near each end, the gauge width in the
        middle, and a cosine blend across the two shoulders.

        Args:
            x: Position along the specimen, in metres. A scalar or an array.

        Returns:
            Width at each ``x``, as ``float64``. A scalar input returns a
            zero-dimensional array.

        """
        x: np.ndarray = np.asarray(x, dtype=np.float64)
        is_scalar = x.ndim == 0
        x = np.atleast_1d(x)

        distance_from_end = np.minimum(x, self.length - x)

        widths: np.ndarray = np.empty_like(x)

        shoulder_length = 0.5 * (self.length - 2.0 * self.grip_length - self.gauge_length)

        in_grip = distance_from_end <= self.grip_length
        in_gauge = distance_from_end >= self.grip_length + shoulder_length
        in_shoulder = ~(in_grip | in_gauge)

        widths[in_grip] = self.grip_width
        widths[in_gauge] = self.gauge_width

        if np.any(in_shoulder):
            shoulder_position = (
                distance_from_end[in_shoulder] - self.grip_length
            ) / shoulder_length

            interpolation = 0.5 * (1.0 - np.cos(np.pi * shoulder_position))

            widths[in_shoulder] = (
                self.grip_width + (self.gauge_width - self.grip_width) * interpolation
            )

        if is_scalar:
            return np.asarray(widths[0], dtype=np.float64)

        return widths

    def _weld_height_at_x(
        self,
        x: NDArray[np.floating] | float,
    ) -> NDArray[np.float64]:
        """Return the weld-cap height at each x-coordinate."""
        x: np.ndarray = np.asarray(x, dtype=np.float64)
        is_scalar = x.ndim == 0
        x = np.atleast_1d(x)

        heights: np.ndarray = np.zeros_like(x)
        if self.weld_height <= 0.0 or self.weld_width <= 0.0:
            return np.asarray(heights[0], dtype=np.float64) if is_scalar else heights

        half_width = 0.5 * self.weld_width
        normalized_position = (x - self.weld_center) / half_width
        inside_weld = np.abs(normalized_position) < 1.0

        heights[inside_weld] = (
            self.weld_height * 0.5 * (1.0 + np.cos(np.pi * normalized_position[inside_weld]))
        )

        if is_scalar:
            return np.asarray(heights[0], dtype=np.float64)

        return heights

    def _warp_points(self, points: NDArray[np.floating]) -> NDArray[np.float64]:
        X, Y, Z = 0, 1, 2

        points: np.ndarray = np.asarray(points, dtype=np.float64)

        widths = self._width_at_x(points[:, X])
        weld_heights = self._weld_height_at_x(points[:, X])

        y_mid = 0.5 * self.grip_width
        z_mid = 0.5 * self.thickness

        warped = points.copy()

        width_scale = widths / self.grip_width
        warped[:, Y] = y_mid + (points[:, Y] - y_mid) * width_scale

        height_scale = 1.0 + 2.0 * weld_heights / self.thickness

        # expands the weld symmetrically
        warped[:, Z] = z_mid + (points[:, Z] - z_mid) * height_scale

        # shifts the Z-coordinates such that the minimum is zero
        warped[:, Z] -= warped[:, Z].min()

        return warped

    def _points_and_tetrahedra(
        self,
        cells: tuple[int, int, int],
        /,
        weld_refinement: int = 1,
        *,
        offset: float = 0.0,
    ) -> tuple[NDArray[np.float64], NDArray[np.int32]]:
        box = BoxMesh(
            length=self.length,
            width=self.grip_width,
            height=self.thickness,
        )

        # exists to add additional points at the weld.
        xs = self._x_edges(cells[0], weld_refinement, offset=offset)

        # noinspection PyProtectedMember
        points, tetrahedra = box._points_and_tetrahedra(cells, xs=xs)

        points = self._warp_points(points)

        _assert_positive_tetrahedra(points, tetrahedra)
        return points, tetrahedra

    def generate(
        self,
        /,
        cells: tuple[int, int, int],
        weld_refinement: int = 1,
        *,
        offset: float = 0.0,
    ) -> MeshFEMBase:
        """Build a tetrahedral dogbone and store it.

        ``cells`` is ``(n_x, n_y, n_z)`` on the starting box. ``weld_refinement``
        splits cells that cover the weld into that many pieces along ``x``.
        ``offset`` widens the refined interval past each side of the weld.

        Args:
            cells: Number of cells along ``x``, ``y``, and ``z`` before weld
                refinement. Each count must be at least ``1``.
            weld_refinement: Number of cells placed across the weld along ``x``.
                Default: ``1``, which does not refine.
            offset: Extra length, in metres, refined on each side of the weld.
                Default: ``0``.

        Returns:
            The ``MeshFEMBase`` holding the tetrahedra.

        Raises:
            InputError: If ``weld_refinement`` is below ``1`` or ``offset`` is
                negative.
            ValueError: If a cell count is below ``1``, or if the warped mesh
                contains an inverted tetrahedron.

        """
        points, tetrahedra = self._points_and_tetrahedra(
            cells,
            weld_refinement,
            offset=offset,
        )

        self._mesh = MeshFEMBase(points, tetrahedra)
        return self._mesh

def draw(
    self,
    cells: tuple[int, int, int] | None = None,
    *,
    backend: Backend = "pyvista",
    ax=None,
    plotter=None,
    wireframe: bool = True,
    show_edges: bool = False,
    show: bool = True,
    save: bool = False,
    save_location: str | Path | None = None,
    save_name: str | None = "mesh",
    save_format: str = "pdf",
    dpi: int = 300,
):
    """Plot the stored tetrahedral mesh, or build a preview mesh.

    ``cells=None`` draws the mesh from the last ``generate`` call. Passing
    ``cells``, or calling ``draw`` before ``generate``, builds a temporary mesh
    with those cell counts. The default preview is ``(12, 6, 4)`` cells in
    ``x``, ``y``, and ``z``. The temporary mesh is not stored.

    Args:
        cells: Number of cells along ``x``, ``y``, and ``z``. Default: the
            stored mesh, or ``(12, 6, 4)`` when none is stored.
        backend: ``"matplotlib"`` or ``"pyvista"``. Default: ``"pyvista"``.
        ax: Existing matplotlib axes. A new figure is created when omitted.
        plotter: Existing PyVista plotter. A new plotter is created when omitted.
        wireframe: Draw the mesh as a wireframe. Default: ``True``.
        show_edges: Draw element edges. Default: ``False``.
        show: Display the figure before returning. Default: ``True``.
        save: Write the figure to disk. Default: ``False``.
        save_location: Directory for the saved figure. Default: the working
            directory.
        save_name: File name without the extension. Default: ``"mesh"``.
        save_format: File extension. Default: ``"pdf"``.
        dpi: Resolution used when saving a matplotlib figure. Default: ``300``.

    Returns:
        The matplotlib axes or the PyVista plotter that holds the plot.

    Raises:
        TypeError: If the stored mesh container does not hold a single mesh.

    """
    if self._mesh is not None and cells is None:
        meshes = self._mesh.meshes
        if not isinstance(meshes, Mesh):
            raise TypeError(f"Expected one mesh, got {type(meshes).__name__}.")
        mesh = meshes
    else:
        cells = (12, 6, 4) if cells is None else cells
        points, tetrahedra = self._points_and_tetrahedra(cells)
        mesh = Mesh(
            jnp.asarray(points),
            elements=jnp.asarray(tetrahedra),
        )

    return plot_mesh(
        mesh,
        cell_type="tetra",
        backend=backend,
        ax=ax,
        plotter=plotter,
        show_edges=show_edges,
        wireframe=wireframe,
        lighting=False,
        show=show,
        save=save,
        save_location=save_location,
        save_name=save_name,
        save_format=save_format,
        dpi=dpi,
    )

@frozen
class DogboneSpec:
    """Dimensions of a dogbone specimen, including an optional weld cap.

    All lengths are in meters. ``length`` must leave room for two grips, two
    shoulders, and the gauge: it has to be greater than
    ``2 * grip_length + gauge_length``. ``gauge_width`` cannot exceed
    ``grip_width``. A weld width or height of ``0`` omits the weld.
    ``weld_center=None`` is stored as the midpoint of ``length``.
    """

    length: float = attrs.field(validator=attrs.validators.gt(0))
    grip_width: float = attrs.field(validator=attrs.validators.gt(0))
    grip_length: float = attrs.field(validator=attrs.validators.gt(0))

    gauge_width: float = attrs.field(validator=attrs.validators.gt(0))
    gauge_length: float = attrs.field(validator=attrs.validators.gt(0))

    thickness: float = attrs.field(validator=attrs.validators.gt(0))

    # a weld_width and weld_height of zero results in no weld.
    weld_width: float = attrs.field(validator=attrs.validators.ge(0))
    weld_height: float = attrs.field(validator=attrs.validators.ge(0))
    weld_center: float | None = attrs.field(
        default=None,
        validator=attrs.validators.optional(attrs.validators.ge(0)),
    )

    UNITS: ClassVar[Mapping[str, str]] = {
        "length": "m",
        "grip_width": "m",
        "grip_length": "m",
        "gauge_width": "m",
        "gauge_length": "m",
        "thickness": "m",
        "weld_width": "m",
        "weld_height": "m",
        "weld_center": "m",
    }

    def __attrs_post_init__(self):
        """Check the specimen proportions and fill in a missing weld center.

        Raises:
            InputError: If ``length`` does not leave room for the shoulders, if
                ``gauge_width`` exceeds ``grip_width``, or if ``weld_center`` lies
                past ``length``.

        """
        required_length = 2 * self.grip_length + self.gauge_length
        if self.length <= required_length:
            # length must be more than required_length to leave room for shoulders.
            msg = (
                f"'length' must be > 2 * 'grip_length' + 'gauge_length' "
                f"({required_length}), got {self.length}."
            )
            config.LOGGER.error(msg)
            raise InputError(msg)

        if self.gauge_width > self.grip_width:
            msg = (
                f"'gauge_width' must be smaller than or equal to 'grip_width', "
                f"got {self.gauge_width} > {self.grip_width}."
            )
            config.LOGGER.error(msg)
            raise InputError(msg)

        if self.weld_center is None:
            object.__setattr__(self, "weld_center", self.length * 0.5)
        elif self.weld_center > self.length:
            msg = f"'weld_center' must be <= 'length', got {self.weld_center} > {self.length}."
            config.LOGGER.error(msg)
            raise InputError(msg)

    def to_string(self, *, indent: int = 0) -> str:
        """Return a string of the dogbone dimensions and their units.

        ``weld_center=None`` is printed as the midpoint of ``length``.

        Args:
            indent: Indentation level. Each level is two spaces. Default: ``0``.

        Returns:
            The formatted specification.

        Examples:
            >>> from pinnjax.fem.generation import DogboneSpec
            >>> print(
            ...     DogboneSpec(
            ...         length=0.1,
            ...         grip_width=0.02,
            ...         grip_length=0.02,
            ...         gauge_width=0.01,
            ...         gauge_length=0.04,
            ...         thickness=0.004,
            ...         weld_width=0.01,
            ...         weld_height=0.001,
            ...     )
            ... )
            DogboneSpec:
              length: 0.1 m
              grip_width: 0.02 m
              grip_length: 0.02 m
              gauge_width: 0.01 m
              gauge_length: 0.04 m
              thickness: 0.004 m
              weld_width: 0.01 m
              weld_height: 0.001 m
              weld_center: 0.05 m

        """
        return _print_attrs_class(self, indent=indent)

    def __str__(self) -> str:  # noqa: D105

def __attrs_post_init__(self):
    """Check the specimen proportions and fill in a missing weld center.

    Raises:
        InputError: If ``length`` does not leave room for the shoulders, if
            ``gauge_width`` exceeds ``grip_width``, or if ``weld_center`` lies
            past ``length``.

    """
    required_length = 2 * self.grip_length + self.gauge_length
    if self.length <= required_length:
        # length must be more than required_length to leave room for shoulders.
        msg = (
            f"'length' must be > 2 * 'grip_length' + 'gauge_length' "
            f"({required_length}), got {self.length}."
        )
        config.LOGGER.error(msg)
        raise InputError(msg)

    if self.gauge_width > self.grip_width:
        msg = (
            f"'gauge_width' must be smaller than or equal to 'grip_width', "
            f"got {self.gauge_width} > {self.grip_width}."
        )
        config.LOGGER.error(msg)
        raise InputError(msg)

    if self.weld_center is None:
        object.__setattr__(self, "weld_center", self.length * 0.5)
    elif self.weld_center > self.length:
        msg = f"'weld_center' must be <= 'length', got {self.weld_center} > {self.length}."
        config.LOGGER.error(msg)
        raise InputError(msg)

def plot_mesh(
    mesh: Mesh,
    *,
    cell_type: CellType,
    backend: Backend = "matplotlib",
    values=None,
    data_location: DataLocation | None = None,
    surface_elements=None,
    label: str = "values",
    title: str | None = None,
    ax=None,
    plotter=None,
    dimensionality: Literal["3D", "2D"] = "3D",
    plane: Plane = "xy",
    cmap: str = DEFAULT_CMAP,
    norm=None,
    boundaries: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    show_edges: bool = False,
    lighting: bool | None = None,
    wireframe: bool = False,
    show: bool = True,
    save: bool = False,
    save_location: str | Path | None = None,
    save_name: str | None = "mesh",
    save_format: str = "pdf",
    dpi: int = 300,
):
    """Plot a Tatva mesh and an optional scalar field on its exterior.

    The mesh is converted to a surface and drawn with Matplotlib or PyVista.
    Point values are stored on the nodes. Cell values are stored on the volume
    cells, and each exterior face then shows its parent cell. When
    ``surface_elements`` is given, the field is drawn only on those faces and
    the rest of the exterior is drawn in the default surface color.

    A 3D Matplotlib plot uses flat face colors. Point values are averaged onto
    each face. A 2D Matplotlib plot with point values uses Gouraud shading, and
    quads are split into two triangles for that path. PyVista keeps the point
    or cell data on the extracted surface.

    Matplotlib adds a colorbar only when it created the figure. PyVista adds
    its own scalar bar whenever values are present. A wireframe is drawn with
    no face color.

    Args:
        mesh: Tatva mesh to draw.
        cell_type: Cell shape of ``mesh``. One of ``"triangle"``, ``"quad"``,
            ``"tetra"``, or ``"hexahedron"``.
        backend: ``"matplotlib"`` or ``"pyvista"``. The check is
            case-insensitive. Default: ``"matplotlib"``.
        values: Scalar field. One value per node when ``data_location`` is
            ``"point"``, or one value per volume cell when it is ``"cell"``.
            Omit it to draw the geometry only.
        data_location: ``"point"`` or ``"cell"``. Required when ``values`` is
            given.
        surface_elements: Exterior faces that receive ``values``. Each face is
            a sequence of node indices. Winding order does not matter. Omit it
            to color the whole exterior.
        label: Name of the scalar field, used for the colorbar. Default:
            ``"values"``.
        title: Figure title. Omit it to leave the title unset.
        ax: Matplotlib axes to draw on. A new figure is created when omitted.
            Used when ``backend`` is ``"matplotlib"``. A 3D plot requires 3D
            axes.
        plotter: PyVista plotter to draw on. A new plotter is created when
            omitted. Used when ``backend`` is ``"pyvista"``.
        dimensionality: ``"3D"``, or ``"2D"`` to project onto ``plane``.
            Default: ``"3D"``.
        plane: Projection plane for a 2D plot. One of ``"xy"``, ``"xz"``, or
            ``"yz"``. Default: ``"xy"``.
        cmap: Colormap name. Default: ``"managua"``.
        norm: Matplotlib normalization. When given, ``boundaries`` is not used.
            For PyVista, ``norm.vmin`` and ``norm.vmax`` set the color limits
            when both are present.
        boundaries: Levels for a Matplotlib ``BoundaryNorm``. For PyVista, the
            first and last entries set the color limits.
        show_edges: Draw element edges. Default: ``False``.
        lighting: PyVista lighting flag. ``None`` leaves the plotter default.
            Used when ``backend`` is ``"pyvista"``.
        wireframe: Draw edges without filled faces. Default: ``False``.
        show: Display the figure before returning. Default: ``True``. When
            this is ``False`` and Matplotlib created the figure, that figure
            is closed.
        save: Write the figure to disk. Default: ``False``.
        save_location: Directory for the saved figure. The working directory
            is used when omitted.
        save_name: File name. The extension is added from ``save_format`` when
            it is missing. Default: ``"mesh"``.
        save_format: File extension. Default: ``"pdf"``.
        dpi: Resolution used when saving. Default: ``300``.

    Returns:
        The Matplotlib axes, or the PyVista plotter.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``backend`` or ``dimensionality`` is unknown, if
            ``values`` is given without ``"point"`` or ``"cell"``, if
            ``values`` has the wrong length, if a face in ``surface_elements``
            is not an exterior face, or if a Matplotlib surface mixes face
            sizes.

    """
    surface, coloured_surface = _prepare_surface(
        mesh,
        cell_type,
        values=values,
        data_location=data_location,
        label=label,
        surface_elements=surface_elements,
    )

    kwargs = {
        "surface": surface,
        "coloured_surface": coloured_surface,
        "values_exist": values is not None,
        "label": label,
        "title": title,
        "dimensionality": dimensionality,
        "plane": plane,
        "cmap": cmap,
        "norm": norm,
        "boundaries": boundaries,
        "show_edges": show_edges,
        "wireframe": wireframe,
        "show": show,
        "save": save,
        "save_location": save_location,
        "save_name": save_name,
        "save_format": save_format,
        "dpi": dpi,
    }

    match backend.lower():
        case "matplotlib":
            return _plot_matplotlib(
                ax=ax,
                data_location=data_location,
                **kwargs,
            )

        case "pyvista":
            return _plot_pyvista(
                plotter=plotter,
                lighting=lighting,
                **kwargs,
            )

        case _:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown plotting backend: {backend!r}")

def plot_mechanical_conditions(
    mesh: Mesh,
    conditions: MechanicalCondition | list[MechanicalCondition],
    *,
    cell_type: CellType,
    show_edges: bool = False,
    show: bool = True,
    save: bool = False,
    save_location: str | Path | None = None,
    save_name: str | None = "mechanical",
    save_format: str = "pdf",
    dpi: int = 300,
):
    """Draw each mechanical condition on a translucent copy of the mesh.

    Node conditions are spheres. Element conditions are colored patches. The
    legend uses the class name, so a ``Clamp`` is distinct from a ``Dirichlet``.

    Args:
        mesh: Tatva mesh to draw.
        conditions: One condition, or a list of them.
        cell_type: Cell shape of ``mesh``.
        show_edges: Draw element edges. Default: ``False``.
        show: Display the plotter before returning. Default: ``True``.
        save: Write the figure to disk. Default: ``False``.
        save_location: Directory for the saved figure.
        save_name: File name passed to the plot saver.
        save_format: File extension. Default: ``"pdf"``.
        dpi: Resolution used when saving. Default: ``300``.

    Returns:
        The PyVista plotter.

    """
    surface, _ = _prepare_surface(
        mesh,
        cell_type,
    )

    # plot light-grey mesh: # TODO: expand to work for matplotlib (as per fem.plot)
    plotter = pv.Plotter(off_screen=not show)
    plotter.add_mesh(
        surface,
        color="lightgray",
        opacity=0.25,
        show_edges=show_edges,
    )

    if not isinstance(conditions, list):
        conditions = [conditions]

    coords: np.ndarray = np.asarray(mesh.coords)
    legend_labels: set[str] = set()
    for condition in conditions:
        label = type(condition).__name__
        legend_label = label if label not in legend_labels else None

        color = CONDITION_COLORS.get(
            type(condition),
            CONDITION_COLORS[MechanicalCondition],
        )

        select = condition.elements(mesh, cell_type=cell_type)

        match condition.APPLICATION:
            case "element":
                patch = _select_surface_elements(surface, select)

                plotter.add_mesh(
                    patch,
                    color=color,
                    show_edges=show_edges,
                    lighting=False,
                    label=legend_label,
                )

            case "node":
                points: np.ndarray = coords[np.asarray(select)]

                plotter.add_points(
                    points,
                    color=color,
                    point_size=10,
                    render_points_as_spheres=True,
                    label=legend_label,
                )

        legend_labels.add(label)

    legend = cast(Any, plotter).add_legend(  # cast avoids ty error.
        loc="lower right",
        face="rectangle",
        font_family="courier",
    )

    legend.LockBorderOff()
    legend.GetEntryTextProperty().SetFontSize(11)
    cast(Any, plotter).add_axes(interactive=None)  # cast avoids ty error.

    if save:
        from pinnjax.plot import save_plot

        save_plot(
            plotter,
            save_location=save_location,
            save_name=save_name,
            save_format=save_format,
            dpi=dpi,
        )

    if show:
        plotter.show()
    return plotter

    save_format: str = "pdf",
    dpi: int = 300,
):
    """Color each exterior face of a mesh by its side name.

    Faces whose axis does not exist on this mesh are skipped. A 2D mesh does
    not draw ``"-z"`` or ``"+z"``.

    Args:
        mesh: Tatva mesh to draw.
        cell_type: Cell shape of ``mesh``.
        show_edges: Draw element edges. Default: ``False``.
        show: Display the plotter before returning. Default: ``True``.
        save: Write the figure to disk. Default: ``False``.
        save_location: Directory for the saved figure.
        save_name: File name passed to the plot saver.
        save_format: File extension. Default: ``"pdf"``.
        dpi: Resolution used when saving. Default: ``300``.

    Returns:
        The PyVista plotter.

    """
    surface, _ = _prepare_surface(mesh, cell_type)

    plotter = pv.Plotter(off_screen=not show)

    dim = mesh.coords.shape[1]

    for side, (axis, _) in SIDE_AXIS_SIGN.items():
        if axis >= dim:
            continue

        elements = select_boundary(
            mesh,
            cell_type=cell_type,
            application="element",
            location=None,
            side=side,
        )

        patch = _select_surface_elements(surface, elements)

        plotter.add_mesh(
            patch,
            color=SIDE_COLORS[side],
            show_edges=show_edges,
            label=side,
            lighting=False,
        )

    legend = cast(Any, plotter).add_legend(  # cast avoids ty error.
        loc="lower right",
        face="rectangle",
        font_family="courier",
    )
    legend.LockBorderOff()
    legend.GetEntryTextProperty().SetFontSize(11)

    cast(Any, plotter).add_axes(  # cast avoids ty error.
        interactive=None,
        x_color="k",
        y_color="k",
        z_color="k",
    )

    if save:
        from pinnjax.plot import save_plot

        save_plot(
            plotter,
            save_location=save_location,
            save_name=save_name,
            save_format=save_format,
            dpi=dpi,
        )

    if show:
        plotter.show()

    return plotter

class FEMBase(ABC):
    """Base class for solvers that operate on one or more Tatva meshes.

    This class deliberately knows nothing about where the mesh came from or
    which physics is solved on it.
    """

    CELL_TYPE: CellType

    def __init__(self):
        """Create a solver with no mesh stored yet."""
        self.meshes: Mesh | list[Mesh] | None = None

    def boundary_geometry(
        self,
        mesh: Mesh,
    ) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
        """Return the exterior boundary of one mesh of this solver's cell type.

        Args:
            mesh: Tatva mesh to query. It is not read from ``self.meshes``.

        Returns:
            Boundary connectivity and unit outward normals.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If ``CELL_TYPE`` has no boundary definition, or if a
                boundary face has a zero normal.

        """
        return boundary_geometry(mesh, self.CELL_TYPE)

    def plot(
        self,
        *,
        backend: Backend = "matplotlib",
        ax=None,
        plotter=None,
        mesh: list[Mesh] | Mesh | None = None,
        index: int | None = None,
        values=None,
        data_location: Literal["point", "cell"] | None = None,
        surface_elements=None,
        label: str = "values",
        dimensionality: Literal["3D", "2D"] = "3D",
        plane: Plane = "xy",
        cmap: str = "managua",
        show_edges: bool = False,
        lighting: bool | None = None,
        title: str | None = None,
        show: bool = True,
        save: bool = False,
        save_location: str | Path | None = None,
        save_name: str | None = "mesh.pdf",
        save_format: str = "pdf",
        dpi: int = 300,
    ):
        """Plot one mesh, with no knowledge of where it came from.

        ``mesh=None`` uses ``self.meshes``. ``index`` selects an entry when that
        value is a list. ``values`` are colored on the nodes or the cells according
        to ``data_location``.

        Args:
            backend: ``"matplotlib"`` or ``"pyvista"``. Default: ``"matplotlib"``.
            ax: Existing matplotlib axes. A new figure is created when omitted.
            plotter: Existing PyVista plotter. A new plotter is created when omitted.
            mesh: Mesh to draw. Default: ``self.meshes``.
            index: Entry to draw when ``mesh`` is a list. Default: the first entry.
            values: Scalar field to color. The mesh is drawn uncolored when omitted.
            data_location: ``"point"`` or ``"cell"``. Required when ``values`` is
                set and the plotter cannot infer it.
            surface_elements: Optional face connectivity used instead of the mesh
                cells. Each row is one face.
            label: Color-bar label. Default: ``"values"``.
            dimensionality: ``"3D"`` or a ``"2D"`` projection. Default: ``"3D"``.
            plane: Projection plane when ``dimensionality`` is ``"2D"``. One of
                ``"xy"``, ``"xz"``, or ``"yz"``. Default: ``"xy"``.
            cmap: Matplotlib colormap name. Default: ``"managua"``.
            show_edges: Draw element edges. Default: ``False``.
            lighting: Enable PyVista lighting. Matplotlib ignores this.
            title: Figure title. Omitted when ``None``.
            show: Display the figure before returning. Default: ``True``.
            save: Write the figure to disk. Default: ``False``.
            save_location: Directory for the saved figure. Default: the working
                directory.
            save_name: File name, including the extension. Default: ``"mesh.pdf"``.
            save_format: File extension. Default: ``"pdf"``.
            dpi: Resolution used when saving a matplotlib figure. Default: ``300``.

        Returns:
            The matplotlib axes or the PyVista plotter that holds the plot.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If no mesh was passed and ``self.meshes`` is empty.
            TypeError: If ``mesh`` is neither a ``Mesh`` nor a list of meshes.

        """
        if mesh is None:
            mesh = self.meshes
            if mesh is None:
                raise ValueError(
                    "Either 'mesh' must be provided, or 'self.meshes' must exist.",
                )

        idx = 0 if index is None else int(index)

        if isinstance(mesh, list):
            mesh = mesh[idx]
        elif not isinstance(mesh, Mesh):
            raise TypeError(f"Unexpected mesh type: {type(mesh).__name__}")

        return plot_tatva_mesh(
            mesh,
            cell_type=self.CELL_TYPE,
            backend=backend,
            values=values,
            data_location=data_location,
            surface_elements=surface_elements,
            label=label,
            title=title,
            ax=ax,
            plotter=plotter,
            dimensionality=dimensionality,
            plane=plane,
            cmap=cmap,
            show_edges=show_edges,
            lighting=lighting,
            show=show,
            save=save,
            save_location=save_location,
            save_name=save_name,
            save_format=save_format,
            dpi=dpi,
        )

Bases: FEMBase, ABC

A triangular surface mesh that can be replaced by a tetrahedral volume.

CELL_TYPE is "triangle" until tetrahedralize runs, then "tetra". Tetrahedralization converts the stored coordinates from millimetres to metres.

Source code in pinnjax/fem/fem.py 
class MeshFEMBase(FEMBase, ABC):
    """A triangular surface mesh that can be replaced by a tetrahedral volume.

    ``CELL_TYPE`` is ``"triangle"`` until ``tetrahedralize`` runs, then
    ``"tetra"``. Tetrahedralization converts the stored coordinates from
    millimetres to metres.
    """

    # TODO: This shouldn't be capable of holding multiple meshes,
    #  but that seems counter to how the naming works. But, I'm not sure.
    def __init__(
        self,
        points: ArrayLike,
        elements: ArrayLike,
    ):
        """Store a surface or a tetrahedral volume.

        Three nodes per element make a triangular surface. Four nodes per element
        make a tetrahedral volume, and the exterior faces and outward normals are
        cached for later boundary queries.

        Args:
            points: Node coordinates, shape ``(N, 3)``. Stored as ``float32``.
            elements: Connectivity, shape ``(M, 3)`` or ``(M, 4)``.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If ``points`` is not ``(N, 3)``, or if ``elements`` is
                neither ``(M, 3)`` nor ``(M, 4)``.

        """
        super().__init__()

        points: np.ndarray = np.asarray(points, dtype=np.float32)
        elements: np.ndarray = np.asarray(elements, dtype=np.int32)

        if points.ndim != 2 or points.shape[1] != 3:
            raise ValueError(f"Expected points with shape (N, 3), got {points.shape}.")

        if elements.ndim != 2 or elements.shape[1] not in (3, 4):
            raise ValueError(
                "Expected triangular surface faces with shape (M, 3) or "
                f"tetrahedral elements with shape (M, 4), got {elements.shape}.",
            )

        self.boundary_faces: np.ndarray | None = None
        self.boundary_normals: np.ndarray | None = None
        self._surface_points: np.ndarray | None = None
        self._surface_faces: np.ndarray | None = None

        if elements.shape[1] == 3:
            self._set_surface_mesh(points, elements)
        else:
            self._set_tetrahedral_mesh(points, elements)

    @property
    def tetrahedralized(self) -> bool:
        """Report whether the stored mesh is a tetrahedral volume.

        Returns:
            ``True`` when ``CELL_TYPE`` is ``"tetra"``.

        """
        return self.CELL_TYPE == "tetra"

    def _set_surface_mesh(
        self,
        points: np.ndarray,
        faces: np.ndarray,
    ) -> None:
        self.CELL_TYPE = "triangle"
        self._surface_points = np.asarray(points, dtype=np.float32).copy()
        self._surface_faces = np.asarray(faces, dtype=np.int32).copy()
        self.boundary_faces = None
        self.boundary_normals = None
        self.meshes = Mesh(
            jnp.asarray(self._surface_points),
            elements=jnp.asarray(self._surface_faces),
        )

    def _set_tetrahedral_mesh(
        self,
        points: np.ndarray,
        elements: np.ndarray,
    ) -> None:
        self.CELL_TYPE = "tetra"
        points = np.asarray(points, dtype=np.float32)
        elements = np.asarray(elements, dtype=np.int32)
        self.meshes = Mesh(
            jnp.asarray(points),
            elements=jnp.asarray(elements),
        )
        self.boundary_faces, self.boundary_normals = _boundary_geometry_from_arrays(
            points,
            elements,
            "tetra",
        )

    @staticmethod
    def _load_points_and_faces(
        file: str | Path,
    ) -> tuple[NDArray, NDArray]:
        file = Path(file)
        file_type = file.suffix.lower().removeprefix(".")

        if file_type not in get_args(FileType):
            raise ValueError(f"Invalid File Type. Got '{file_type}'.")

        match file_type:
            case "stl" | "ply":
                mesh = trimesh.load_mesh(file)

                points = np.asarray(
                    mesh.vertices,
                    dtype=np.float32,
                )
                faces = np.asarray(
                    mesh.faces,
                    dtype=np.int32,
                )

            case "h5" | "hdf5":
                with h5py.File(file, "r") as f:
                    points = np.asarray(
                        f["points"][:],
                        dtype=np.float32,
                    )
                    faces = np.asarray(
                        f["faces"][:],
                        dtype=np.int32,
                    )

            case "npz":
                with np.load(str(file)) as data:
                    points = np.asarray(
                        data["points"],
                        dtype=np.float32,
                    )
                    faces = np.asarray(
                        data["faces"],
                        dtype=np.int32,
                    )

        return points, faces

    @classmethod
    def from_file(
        cls,
        file: str | Path,
        *,
        tetrahedralize: bool = True,
        **kwargs,
    ):
        """Load a triangular surface from disk and, by default, tetrahedralize it.

        ``.stl`` and ``.ply`` are read with Trimesh. ``.h5``, ``.hdf5``, and
        ``.npz`` must contain ``points`` and ``faces`` arrays. ``kwargs`` are
        forwarded to ``from_points_and_faces``, including any extra arguments
        required by a subclass constructor.

        Args:
            file: Path of the surface mesh.
            tetrahedralize: Build a tetrahedral volume after loading.
                Default: ``True``.
            **kwargs: Forwarded to ``from_points_and_faces``, including any extra
                arguments required by a subclass constructor.

        Returns:
            A mesh of this class.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If the suffix is not a supported file type, or if the
                loaded arrays are not a triangular surface.

        """
        points, faces = cls._load_points_and_faces(file)

        return cls.from_points_and_faces(
            points,
            faces,
            tetrahedralize=tetrahedralize,
            **kwargs,
        )

    @classmethod
    def from_points_and_faces(
        cls,
        points: ArrayLike,
        faces: ArrayLike,
        *,
        tetrahedralize: bool = True,
        tetrahedralizer: Tetrahedralizer = "gmsh",
        target_size: float | None = None,
        quality: bool = True,
        **kwargs,
    ):
        """Build a mesh from a triangular surface and, by default, tetrahedralize it.

        ``kwargs`` are passed to the class constructor after ``points`` and
        ``faces``. ``MeshFEMBase`` takes no further arguments. A subclass can use
        them for material, conditions, and solver settings.

        Args:
            points: Node coordinates, shape ``(N, 3)``.
            faces: Triangle connectivity, shape ``(M, 3)``.
            tetrahedralize: Replace the surface with a tetrahedral volume.
                Default: ``True``.
            tetrahedralizer: ``"gmsh"`` or ``"tetgen"``. Default: ``"gmsh"``.
            target_size: Target element size passed to Gmsh. Ignored by TetGen.
            quality: Ask TetGen for a quality mesh. Ignored by Gmsh.
                Default: ``True``.
            **kwargs: Passed to the class constructor after ``points`` and
                ``faces``. ``MeshFEMBase`` takes no further arguments. A subclass
                can use them for material, conditions, and solver settings.

        Returns:
            A mesh of this class.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If ``points`` is not ``(N, 3)`` or ``faces`` is not
                ``(M, 3)``.

        """
        points: np.ndarray = np.asarray(points, dtype=np.float32)
        faces: np.ndarray = np.asarray(faces, dtype=np.int32)

        if points.ndim != 2 or points.shape[1] != 3:
            raise ValueError(f"Expected points with shape (N, 3), got {points.shape}.")

        if faces.ndim != 2 or faces.shape[1] != 3:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Expected triangular faces with shape (M, 3), got {faces.shape}.",
            )

        mesh = cls(
            points,
            faces,
            **kwargs,
        )

        if tetrahedralize:
            mesh.tetrahedralize(
                method=tetrahedralizer,
                target_size=target_size,
                quality=quality,
            )

        return mesh

    def tetrahedralize(
        self,
        *,
        method: Tetrahedralizer = "gmsh",
        scale_factor: float | None = None,
        target_size: float | None = None,
        quality: bool = True,
        overwrite: bool = False,
    ):
        """Replace the stored triangular surface with a tetrahedral volume.

        The new node coordinates are the mesher output multiplied by ``1e-3``,
        converting millimetres to metres. A mesh that is already tetrahedral is
        left unchanged unless ``overwrite`` is set. The exterior faces and outward
        normals are cached.

        Args:
            method: ``"gmsh"`` or ``"tetgen"``. Default: ``"gmsh"``.
            target_size: Target element size passed to Gmsh. Ignored by TetGen.
            scale_factor: Scale the mesh by this factor. Default: ``None``.
            quality: Ask TetGen for a quality mesh. Ignored by Gmsh.
                Default: ``True``.
            overwrite: Tetrahedralize again when a volume mesh is already stored.
                Default: ``False``.

        Returns:
            This mesh.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If no triangular surface is stored, or if ``method`` is
                unknown.

        """
        if self.tetrahedralized and not overwrite:
            return self

        if self._surface_points is None or self._surface_faces is None:
            raise ValueError(
                "No triangular surface mesh is available to tetrahedralize.",
            )

        points, elements = self._tetrahedralize(
            self._surface_points,
            self._surface_faces,
            method=method,
            target_size=target_size,
            quality=quality,
        )

        # the mesh is in mm, but the physics happens in m.
        points = points * scale_factor

        self._set_tetrahedral_mesh(points, elements)

        return self

    @staticmethod
    def _tetrahedralize(
        points: ArrayLike,
        faces: ArrayLike,
        *,
        method: Tetrahedralizer = "gmsh",
        target_size: float | None = None,
        quality: bool = True,
    ) -> tuple[NDArray, NDArray]:
        match method:
            case "gmsh":
                return MeshFEMBase._tetrahedralize_gmsh(
                    points,
                    faces,
                    target_size=target_size,
                )

            case "tetgen":
                return MeshFEMBase._tetrahedralize_tetgen(
                    points,
                    faces,
                    quality=quality,
                )

            case _:
                raise ValueError(f"Unknown tetrahedralization method: {method!r}.")

    @staticmethod
    def _tetrahedralize_tetgen(
        points: ArrayLike,
        faces: ArrayLike,
        *,
        quality: bool = True,
    ) -> tuple[NDArray, NDArray]:
        points_array = np.asarray(points, dtype=np.float64)
        faces_array = np.asarray(faces, dtype=np.int32)
        tet = tetgen.TetGen(points_array, faces_array)
        tet.tetrahedralize(quality=quality)

        return (
            np.asarray(tet.node, dtype=np.float32),
            np.asarray(tet.elem, dtype=np.int32),
        )

    @staticmethod
    def _tetrahedralize_gmsh(
        points: ArrayLike,
        faces: ArrayLike,
        *,
        target_size: float | None = None,
    ) -> tuple[NDArray, NDArray]:
        points: np.ndarray = np.asarray(points, dtype=np.float64)
        faces: np.ndarray = np.asarray(faces, dtype=np.int64)

        if target_size is not None and target_size <= 0.0:
            raise ValueError(f"target_size must be positive, got {target_size}.")

        was_initialized = bool(gmsh.isInitialized())

        if not was_initialized:
            gmsh.initialize()

        previous_model = gmsh.model.getCurrent() if was_initialized and gmsh.model.list() else None

        try:
            gmsh.model.add("mesh_fem_tetrahedralization")

            surface_tag = gmsh.model.addDiscreteEntity(2)

            node_tags = np.arange(
                1,
                points.shape[0] + 1,
                dtype=np.int64,
            )

            triangle_type = gmsh.model.mesh.getElementType(
                "Triangle",
                1,
            )

            gmsh.model.mesh.addNodes(
                2,
                surface_tag,
                node_tags,
                points.reshape(-1),
            )

            gmsh.model.mesh.addElementsByType(
                surface_tag,
                triangle_type,
                [],
                (faces + 1).reshape(-1),
            )

            gmsh.model.mesh.reclassifyNodes()

            volume_tag = gmsh.model.addDiscreteEntity(
                3,
                boundary=[surface_tag],
            )

            gmsh.model.mesh.createGeometry([(3, volume_tag)])

            gmsh.option.setNumber(
                "Mesh.MeshOnlyEmpty",
                1,
            )

            gmsh.option.setNumber(
                "Mesh.AngleToleranceFacetOverlap",
                0.01,
            )

            if target_size is not None:
                gmsh.option.setNumber(
                    "Mesh.MeshSizeFromPoints",
                    0,
                )
                gmsh.option.setNumber(
                    "Mesh.MeshSizeFromCurvature",
                    0,
                )
                gmsh.option.setNumber(
                    "Mesh.MeshSizeExtendFromBoundary",
                    0,
                )
                gmsh.option.setNumber(
                    "Mesh.MeshSizeMin",
                    target_size,
                )
                gmsh.option.setNumber(
                    "Mesh.MeshSizeMax",
                    target_size,
                )

            gmsh.model.mesh.generate(3)

            node_tags, coords, _ = gmsh.model.mesh.getNodes()

            tetra_type = gmsh.model.mesh.getElementType(
                "Tetrahedron",
                1,
            )

            _, tetra_node_tags = gmsh.model.mesh.getElementsByType(
                tetra_type,
            )

            points_out = np.reshape(
                np.asarray(
                    coords,
                    dtype=np.float32,
                ),
                shape=(-1, 3),
            )

            node_tags: np.ndarray = np.asarray(
                node_tags,
                dtype=np.int64,
            )

            tetra_node_tags: np.ndarray = np.asarray(
                tetra_node_tags,
                dtype=np.int64,
            )

            node_indices: np.ndarray = np.empty(
                node_tags.max() + 1,
                dtype=np.int64,
            )
            node_indices[node_tags] = np.arange(node_tags.size)

            elements_out = node_indices[tetra_node_tags].reshape(-1, 4).astype(np.int32)

            return points_out, elements_out

        finally:
            if was_initialized:
                gmsh.model.remove()

                if previous_model is not None:
                    gmsh.model.setCurrent(previous_model)
            else:
                gmsh.finalize()

    @staticmethod
    def _extract_boundary_faces(
        points: ArrayLike,
        elements: ArrayLike,
    ) -> NDArray:
        boundary_faces, _ = _boundary_geometry_from_arrays(
            points,
            elements,
            "tetra",
        )
        return boundary_faces

    def boundary_geometry(
        self,
        mesh: Mesh,
    ) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
        """Return the exterior boundary of a mesh.

        The cached faces and normals are returned when ``mesh`` is the stored
        tetrahedral volume. Any other mesh is computed by ``FEMBase``.

        Args:
            mesh: Tatva mesh to query.

        Returns:
            Boundary connectivity and unit outward normals.

        """
        if (
            mesh is self.meshes
            and self.tetrahedralized
            and self.boundary_faces is not None
            and self.boundary_normals is not None
        ):
            return self.boundary_faces, self.boundary_normals

        return super().boundary_geometry(mesh)

def __init__(
    self,
    points: ArrayLike,
    elements: ArrayLike,
):
    """Store a surface or a tetrahedral volume.

    Three nodes per element make a triangular surface. Four nodes per element
    make a tetrahedral volume, and the exterior faces and outward normals are
    cached for later boundary queries.

    Args:
        points: Node coordinates, shape ``(N, 3)``. Stored as ``float32``.
        elements: Connectivity, shape ``(M, 3)`` or ``(M, 4)``.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``points`` is not ``(N, 3)``, or if ``elements`` is
            neither ``(M, 3)`` nor ``(M, 4)``.

    """
    super().__init__()

    points: np.ndarray = np.asarray(points, dtype=np.float32)
    elements: np.ndarray = np.asarray(elements, dtype=np.int32)

    if points.ndim != 2 or points.shape[1] != 3:
        raise ValueError(f"Expected points with shape (N, 3), got {points.shape}.")

    if elements.ndim != 2 or elements.shape[1] not in (3, 4):
        raise ValueError(
            "Expected triangular surface faces with shape (M, 3) or "
            f"tetrahedral elements with shape (M, 4), got {elements.shape}.",
        )

    self.boundary_faces: np.ndarray | None = None
    self.boundary_normals: np.ndarray | None = None
    self._surface_points: np.ndarray | None = None
    self._surface_faces: np.ndarray | None = None

    if elements.shape[1] == 3:
        self._set_surface_mesh(points, elements)
    else:
        self._set_tetrahedral_mesh(points, elements)

def from_file(
    cls,

    **kwargs,
):
    """Load a triangular surface from disk and, by default, tetrahedralize it.

    ``.stl`` and ``.ply`` are read with Trimesh. ``.h5``, ``.hdf5``, and
    ``.npz`` must contain ``points`` and ``faces`` arrays. ``kwargs`` are
    forwarded to ``from_points_and_faces``, including any extra arguments
    required by a subclass constructor.

            arguments required by a subclass constructor.

    Raises:

            loaded arrays are not a triangular surface.

    points, faces = cls._load_points_and_faces(file)

        points,
        faces,
        tetrahedralize=tetrahedralize,

@classmethod
def from_points_and_faces(
    cls,
    points: ArrayLike,
    faces: ArrayLike,
    *,
    tetrahedralize: bool = True,
    tetrahedralizer: Tetrahedralizer = "gmsh",
    target_size: float | None = None,
    quality: bool = True,
    **kwargs,
):
    """Build a mesh from a triangular surface and, by default, tetrahedralize it.

    ``kwargs`` are passed to the class constructor after ``points`` and
    ``faces``. ``MeshFEMBase`` takes no further arguments. A subclass can use
    them for material, conditions, and solver settings.

    Args:
        points: Node coordinates, shape ``(N, 3)``.
        faces: Triangle connectivity, shape ``(M, 3)``.
        tetrahedralize: Replace the surface with a tetrahedral volume.
            Default: ``True``.
        tetrahedralizer: ``"gmsh"`` or ``"tetgen"``. Default: ``"gmsh"``.
        target_size: Target element size passed to Gmsh. Ignored by TetGen.
        quality: Ask TetGen for a quality mesh. Ignored by Gmsh.
            Default: ``True``.
        **kwargs: Passed to the class constructor after ``points`` and
            ``faces``. ``MeshFEMBase`` takes no further arguments. A subclass
            can use them for material, conditions, and solver settings.

    Returns:
        A mesh of this class.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``points`` is not ``(N, 3)`` or ``faces`` is not
            ``(M, 3)``.

    """
    points: np.ndarray = np.asarray(points, dtype=np.float32)
    faces: np.ndarray = np.asarray(faces, dtype=np.int32)

    if points.ndim != 2 or points.shape[1] != 3:
        raise ValueError(f"Expected points with shape (N, 3), got {points.shape}.")

    if faces.ndim != 2 or faces.shape[1] != 3:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Expected triangular faces with shape (M, 3), got {faces.shape}.",
        )

    mesh = cls(
        points,
        faces,
        **kwargs,
    )

    if tetrahedralize:
        mesh.tetrahedralize(
            method=tetrahedralizer,
            target_size=target_size,
            quality=quality,
        )

    return mesh

def tetrahedralize(
    self,
    *,
    method: Tetrahedralizer = "gmsh",
    scale_factor: float | None = None,
    target_size: float | None = None,
    quality: bool = True,
    overwrite: bool = False,
):
    """Replace the stored triangular surface with a tetrahedral volume.

    The new node coordinates are the mesher output multiplied by ``1e-3``,
    converting millimetres to metres. A mesh that is already tetrahedral is
    left unchanged unless ``overwrite`` is set. The exterior faces and outward
    normals are cached.

    Args:
        method: ``"gmsh"`` or ``"tetgen"``. Default: ``"gmsh"``.
        target_size: Target element size passed to Gmsh. Ignored by TetGen.
        scale_factor: Scale the mesh by this factor. Default: ``None``.
        quality: Ask TetGen for a quality mesh. Ignored by Gmsh.
            Default: ``True``.
        overwrite: Tetrahedralize again when a volume mesh is already stored.
            Default: ``False``.

    Returns:
        This mesh.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If no triangular surface is stored, or if ``method`` is
            unknown.

    """
    if self.tetrahedralized and not overwrite:
        return self

    if self._surface_points is None or self._surface_faces is None:
        raise ValueError(
            "No triangular surface mesh is available to tetrahedralize.",
        )

    points, elements = self._tetrahedralize(
        self._surface_points,
        self._surface_faces,
        method=method,
        target_size=target_size,
        quality=quality,
    )

    # the mesh is in mm, but the physics happens in m.
    points = points * scale_factor

    self._set_tetrahedral_mesh(points, elements)

    return self

class HeightMapFEMBase(FEMBase, ABC):
    """Base for FEM solvers whose meshes are generated from height maps.

    A missing thickness produces a triangular surface mesh.
    A supplied
    ``thickness`` extrudes the same height map into a layered hexahedral mesh.
    """

    height_channel: int = 0
    mask_channel: int | None = None
    channel_count: int | None = None

    grid_node_indices: np.ndarray | list[np.ndarray] | None

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        lx: float,
        ly: float,
        thickness: float | None = None,
        height_channel: int = 0,
        mask_channel: int | None = None,
        channel_count: int | None = None,
        height_scale: float = 1.0,
        thickness_steps: int = 4,
        surface_grading: float = 1.0,
    ):
        """Store the height-map domain. No mesh is built until ``generate_meshes``.

        ``thickness=None`` selects a triangular surface. A numeric ``thickness``
        selects a layered hexahedral solid and requires ``thickness_steps >= 2``
        and ``surface_grading >= 1``. ``surface_grading=1`` spaces the layers
        uniformly. Larger values pack layers toward the scanned surface.

        Args:
            lx: In-plane length of the height map along ``x``.
            ly: In-plane length of the height map along ``y``.
            thickness: Solid thickness below the scan. ``None`` builds a membrane.
                Default: ``None``.
            height_channel: Scan-image channel read as height. Default: ``0``.
            mask_channel: Optional scan channel used as a mask. Default: ``None``.
            channel_count: Number of channels in each scan image. Inferred when
                omitted.
            height_scale: Multiplier applied to the height channel. Default: ``1``.
            thickness_steps: Node layers through the solid, including both
                surfaces. Default: ``4``.
            surface_grading: Layer clustering toward the scanned surface.
                Default: ``1``.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If a solid mesh is requested with fewer than two thickness
                steps, or with ``surface_grading`` below ``1``.

        """
        super().__init__()

        self.lx = float(lx)
        self.ly = float(ly)
        self.thickness = None if thickness is None else float(thickness)
        self.CELL_TYPE: CellType = cast(
            "CellType",
            "triangle" if self.thickness is None else "hexahedron",
        )

        self.height_channel = int(height_channel)
        self.mask_channel = mask_channel
        self.channel_count = channel_count
        self.height_scale = float(height_scale)

        self.thickness_steps = int(thickness_steps)
        self.surface_grading = float(surface_grading)

        if self.thickness is not None:
            if self.thickness_steps < 2:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"thickness_steps must be at least 2, got {thickness_steps}.",
                )

            if self.surface_grading < 1.0:
                raise ValueError(
                    "surface_grading must be at least 1.0 (1.0 = uniform layers), "
                    f"got {surface_grading}.",
                )

        self.grid_node_indices = None
        self._scan_images = None

    @property
    def layer_profile(self) -> np.ndarray:
        """Return the normalized height of each solid-mesh node layer.

        Values run from ``0`` at the substrate to ``1`` at the scanned surface.
        ``surface_grading=1`` spaces them uniformly. Larger values keep more layers
        near ``1``.

        Returns:
            Array of shape ``(thickness_steps,)``.

        """
        s = np.linspace(0.0, 1.0, self.thickness_steps)

        if self.surface_grading == 1.0:
            return s

        return 1.0 - (1.0 - s) ** self.surface_grading

    def _height_batch(self, images: Array) -> Array:
        heights = height_maps_from_scan(
            images,
            self.height_channel,
            self.channel_count,
        )
        return jnp.asarray(heights) * self.height_scale

    def _generate_mesh(self, image: Array):
        image = jnp.asarray(image)
        if image.ndim != 2:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Expected a (H, W) height map, got shape {tuple(image.shape)}.",
            )

        h, w = image.shape
        x = jnp.linspace(0.0, self.lx, w)
        y = jnp.linspace(0.0, self.ly, h)

        if self.thickness is None:
            yy, xx = jnp.meshgrid(y, x, indexing="ij")

            nodes = jnp.stack(
                [
                    xx,
                    yy,
                    image,
                ],
                axis=-1,
            ).reshape(-1, 3)

            grid_node_indices = np.arange(
                h * w,
                dtype=np.int32,
            ).reshape(h, w)

            elements = []
            for iy in range(h - 1):
                for ix in range(w - 1):
                    n00 = grid_node_indices[iy, ix]
                    n10 = grid_node_indices[iy, ix + 1]
                    n01 = grid_node_indices[iy + 1, ix]
                    n11 = grid_node_indices[iy + 1, ix + 1]

                    elements.append([n00, n10, n11])
                    elements.append([n00, n11, n01])

            elements = jnp.asarray(np.asarray(elements, dtype=np.int32))
            return Mesh(nodes, elements=elements), grid_node_indices

        steps = self.thickness_steps
        eta = jnp.asarray(self.layer_profile)

        yy, xx, ee = jnp.meshgrid(
            y,
            x,
            eta,
            indexing="ij",
        )

        zz = ee * (self.thickness + image[..., None])

        nodes = jnp.stack(
            [
                xx,
                yy,
                zz,
            ],
            axis=-1,
        ).reshape(-1, 3)

        grid_node_indices = np.arange(
            h * w * steps,
            dtype=np.int32,
        ).reshape(h, w, steps)

        elements = []
        for iy in range(h - 1):
            for ix in range(w - 1):
                for iz in range(steps - 1):
                    n000 = grid_node_indices[iy, ix, iz]
                    n100 = grid_node_indices[iy, ix + 1, iz]
                    n110 = grid_node_indices[iy + 1, ix + 1, iz]
                    n010 = grid_node_indices[iy + 1, ix, iz]

                    n001 = grid_node_indices[iy, ix, iz + 1]
                    n101 = grid_node_indices[iy, ix + 1, iz + 1]
                    n111 = grid_node_indices[iy + 1, ix + 1, iz + 1]
                    n011 = grid_node_indices[iy + 1, ix, iz + 1]

                    elements.append(
                        [
                            n000,
                            n100,
                            n110,
                            n010,
                            n001,
                            n101,
                            n111,
                            n011,
                        ],
                    )

        elements = jnp.asarray(np.asarray(elements, dtype=np.int32))
        return Mesh(nodes, elements=elements), grid_node_indices

    def generate_meshes(self, images: Array):
        """Build one Tatva mesh for each height map and store the pixel-to-node map.

        A single ``(H, W)`` map is stored as one mesh. A batch is stored as a list.
        Accepted layouts are ``(H, W)``, ``(N, H, W)``, ``(C, H, W)``, and
        ``(N, C, H, W)``. The height channel is multiplied by ``height_scale``.

        A membrane uses the height as ``z`` and splits each pixel quad into two
        triangles. A solid extrudes that surface through ``thickness`` into
        hexahedra. ``grid_node_indices`` records which node came from which pixel,
        with shape ``(H, W)`` or ``(H, W, thickness_steps)``.

        Args:
            images: One height map or a batch of scan images.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If ``images`` is not one of the accepted layouts, or if a
                single map is not two-dimensional after the height channel is read.

        """
        self._scan_images = scan_images_nchw(
            images,
            self.height_channel,
            self.channel_count,
        )
        images = jnp.asarray(self._height_batch(images))

        match images.ndim:
            case 2:
                self.meshes, self.grid_node_indices = self._generate_mesh(images)

            case 3:
                meshes, grid_node_indices = [], []

                for image in images:
                    mesh, grid_indices = self._generate_mesh(image)

                    meshes.append(mesh)
                    grid_node_indices.append(grid_indices)

                self.meshes = meshes
                self.grid_node_indices = grid_node_indices

            case _:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Invalid image shape {tuple(images.shape)}. "
                    "Pass (H, W), (N, H, W), (C, H, W) or (N, C, H, W).",
                )

    def _plot_channel(self, channel: int | None) -> int:
        if channel is not None:
            return int(channel)
        return int(self.height_channel)

    def _node_values_for_plot(self, *, index: int, channel: int, n_nodes: int):
        return scan_channel_node_values(
            scan_images=self._scan_images,
            grid_node_indices=self.grid_node_indices,
            index=index,
            channel=channel,
            n_nodes=n_nodes,
        )

    def _channel_label(self, channel: int) -> str:
        if channel == self.height_channel:
            return "relative height [mm]"
        if channel == self.mask_channel:
            return "material mask"
        return f"channel {channel}"

    def _height_map_surface_elements(self, index: int = 0) -> np.ndarray | None:
        grid = (
            self.grid_node_indices[index]
            if isinstance(self.grid_node_indices, list)
            else self.grid_node_indices
        )

        if grid is None:
            return None

        grid: np.ndarray = np.asarray(grid)
        if grid.ndim == 2:
            return None

        if grid.ndim != 3:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Expected grid_node_indices with 2 or 3 dimensions, got {grid.ndim}.",
            )

        surface = grid[..., -1]

        return np.reshape(
            np.stack(
                [
                    surface[:-1, :-1],
                    surface[:-1, 1:],
                    surface[1:, 1:],
                    surface[1:, :-1],
                ],
                axis=-1,
            ),
            (-1, 4),
        )

    def plot(
        self,
        *,
        backend: Backend = "matplotlib",
        ax=None,
        plotter=None,
        mesh: list[Mesh] | Mesh | None = None,
        index: int | None = None,
        values=None,
        data_location: Literal["point", "cell"] | None = None,
        surface_elements=None,
        label: str = "values",
        channel: int | None = None,
        dimensionality: Literal["3D", "2D"] = "3D",
        plane: Plane = "xy",
        cmap: str = "managua",
        show_edges: bool = False,
        lighting: bool | None = None,
        title: str | None = None,
        show: bool = True,
        save: bool = False,
        save_location: str | Path | None = None,
        save_name: str | None = "stress.pdf",
        save_format: str = "pdf",
        dpi: int = 300,
    ):
        """Plot one height-map mesh, using the scan when no field is given.

        ``values=None`` samples ``channel`` onto the scanned surface. The default
        channel is the height channel. If no scan is stored, the node's ``z``
        coordinate is used instead. The drawn faces are the top surface of the
        mesh unless ``surface_elements`` is passed.

        Args:
            backend: ``"matplotlib"`` or ``"pyvista"``. Default: ``"matplotlib"``.
            ax: Existing matplotlib axes. A new figure is created when omitted.
            plotter: Existing PyVista plotter. A new plotter is created when omitted.
            mesh: Mesh to draw. Default: ``self.meshes``.
            index: Crop to draw when several height maps were meshed.
                Default: the first crop.
            values: Scalar field to color. A scan channel is used when omitted.
            data_location: ``"point"`` or ``"cell"``. A scan-derived field is
                plotted on the points.
            surface_elements: Faces to draw. Default: the scanned surface.
            label: Color-bar label. A scan channel replaces this with its own label.
            channel: Scan channel used when ``values`` is omitted. Default: the
                height channel.
            dimensionality: ``"3D"`` or a ``"2D"`` projection. Default: ``"3D"``.
            plane: Projection plane when ``dimensionality`` is ``"2D"``. One of
                ``"xy"``, ``"xz"``, or ``"yz"``. Default: ``"xy"``.
            cmap: Matplotlib colormap name. Default: ``"managua"``.
            show_edges: Draw element edges. Default: ``False``.
            lighting: Enable PyVista lighting. Matplotlib ignores this.
            title: Figure title. Omitted when ``None``.
            show: Display the figure before returning. Default: ``True``.
            save: Write the figure to disk. Default: ``False``.
            save_location: Directory for the saved figure. Default: the working
                directory.
            save_name: File name, including the extension.
                Default: ``"stress.pdf"``.
            save_format: File extension. Default: ``"pdf"``.
            dpi: Resolution used when saving a matplotlib figure. Default: ``300``.

        Returns:
            The matplotlib axes or the PyVista plotter that holds the plot.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If no mesh was passed and ``self.meshes`` is empty, or if
                ``channel`` is outside the stored scan.
            TypeError: If ``mesh`` is neither a ``Mesh`` nor a list of meshes.

        """
        if mesh is None:
            mesh = self.meshes
            if mesh is None:
                raise ValueError(
                    "Either 'mesh' must be provided, or 'self.meshes' must exist.",
                )

        idx = 0 if index is None else int(index)

        if isinstance(mesh, list):
            mesh = mesh[idx]
        elif not isinstance(mesh, Mesh):
            raise TypeError(f"Unexpected mesh type: {type(mesh).__name__}")

        if values is None:
            channel = self._plot_channel(channel)
            label = self._channel_label(channel)

            values = self._node_values_for_plot(
                index=idx,
                channel=channel,
                n_nodes=mesh.coords.shape[0],
            )

            if values is None:
                values = np.asarray(mesh.coords)[:, 2]

            data_location: Literal["point", "cell"] = "point"

        if surface_elements is None:
            surface_elements = self._height_map_surface_elements(idx)

        return super().plot(
            backend=backend,
            ax=ax,
            plotter=plotter,
            mesh=mesh,
            index=idx,
            values=values,
            data_location=data_location,
            surface_elements=surface_elements,
            label=label,
            dimensionality=dimensionality,
            plane=plane,
            cmap=cmap,
            show_edges=show_edges,
            lighting=lighting,
            title=title,
            show=show,
            save=save,
            save_location=save_location,
            save_name=save_name,
            save_format=save_format,
            dpi=dpi,
        )
