class Shape(ABC):
    """Primitive Base Class for which all Shapes derive.

    Attributes:
        spatial_dims: number of spatial dimensions.
        dims: total number of dimensions, including temporal.
        times: Optional [`pinnjax.Time`][pinnjax.Time] object.
        samples: Array of collocation points.
            Populated after calling `sample()` on a single shape.
            A ``ComplexShape`` keeps the points on its children.
        n_points: Number of collocation points.
        residual_function: Assigned [`pinnjax.Residual`][pinnjax.Residual] object.
        loss_function: Assigned [`pinnjax.Loss`][pinnjax.Loss] object.
        loss_val: Most recently calculated loss using assigned
            [`pinnjax.Loss`][pinnjax.Loss] object.
        origin: Reference point of the shape, when a subclass defines one.
        shapes: Child shapes. ``None`` until a subclass assigns a list.

    """

    spatial_dims: int = 0
    dims: int = 0
    times: Time | float | None = None
    samples: Array | None = None
    n_points: int = 0
    residual_function: Residual | None = None
    loss_function: Loss | None = None
    loss_val: Array | None = None
    origin: Array | None = None

    residual_functions: tuple[Residual, ...] | None = None
    loss_functions: tuple[Loss, ...] | None = None

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        """Set ``shapes`` to ``None``.

        Subclasses replace it with the child shapes they contain.
        """
        self.shapes = None

    def bounds(self) -> tuple[Array, Array]:
        """Return (min, max) arrays for sampling.

        Raises:
            NotImplementedError: Always.

        """
        config.LOGGER.error("Not implemented.")
        raise NotImplementedError

    def transform(self, unit_samples: Array) -> Array:
        """Map unit-cube samples to uniform samples in the shape.

        Raises:
            NotImplementedError: Always.

        """
        config.LOGGER.error("Not implemented.")
        raise NotImplementedError

    def sample(
        self,
        method: SamplingMethod,
        sampling_values: float | Sequence[float | int] | None = None,
        *,
        overwrite: bool = False,
        descriptor_count: int = 32,
    ) -> tuple[Array, int]:
        """Store collocation points on this shape.

        ``sampling_values`` is one number. ``None`` uses ``1000``. A list is
        rejected here. [`ComplexShape.sample`][pinnjax.geometry.complex.ComplexShape.sample]
        accepts one number per child. When points are already stored and
        ``overwrite`` is false, those points are returned unchanged.

        ``descriptor_count`` is used by
        [`OperatorGeometry.sample`][pinnjax.geometry.operator.OperatorGeometry.sample] and ignored
        here.

        Args:
            method: Sampler that draws the points.
            sampling_values: One sampling size. ``None`` uses the Sampler default.
            overwrite: Replace points that were already stored.
            descriptor_count: Descriptor sample count for an operator geometry.

        Returns:
            samples: Collocation points stored on ``samples``.
            n_points: Number of those points.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If ``sampling_values`` is a sequence.

        """
        del descriptor_count
        if sampling_values is not None and not isinstance(sampling_values, (float, int)):
            msg = "A Shape takes one sampling value. Pass a list to ComplexShape.sample."
            config.LOGGER.error(msg)
            raise ValueError(msg)

        if not overwrite and self.samples is not None and self.n_points > 0:
            return self.samples, self.n_points

        self.samples = jnp.asarray(
            method(self, sampling_values),
            dtype=config.get_dtype(),
        )
        self.n_points = len(self.samples)

        return self.samples, self.n_points

    def estimate_nsamples(self, value: float) -> int:
        """Determine the equivalent number of samples given a uniform-grid sampling.

        Args:
            value: Distance between points in a uniform-grid sample of the same Shape.

        Raises:
            NotImplementedError: Always.

        """
        config.LOGGER.error("Not implemented.")
        raise NotImplementedError

    def grid_shape(self, value: float) -> tuple[int, ...]:
        """Return point counts along each active axis of a uniform sampling grid."""
        config.LOGGER.error("Not implemented.")
        raise NotImplementedError

    def measure(self) -> Array:
        """Return the geometric measure of this shape.

        A line returns its length, a surface its area, and a volume its volume.
        A point returns zero.

        Returns:
            The measure as a scalar array.

        Raises:
            NotImplementedError: Always, unless a subclass overrides this method.

        """
        msg = "Not implemented."
        config.LOGGER.error(msg)

        raise NotImplementedError

    def normal(self) -> Array:
        """Compute the normal vector.

        Raises:
            NotImplementedError: Always.

        """
        config.LOGGER.error("Not implemented.")
        raise NotImplementedError

    def set_residual(self, residual: Residual) -> None:
        """Bind the [`pinnjax.Residual`][pinnjax.Residual] object to this Shape.

        Args:
            residual: A [`pinnjax.Residual`][pinnjax.Residual] object.

        """
        bind = getattr(residual, "bind", None)
        if bind is None:
            self.residual_function = residual
        else:
            self.residual_function = cast("Callable[[Shape], Residual]", bind)(self)

    def has_residual(self) -> bool:
        """Check if a [`pinnjax.Residual`][pinnjax.Residual] has already been bound.

        Returns:
            bool: Whether the Shape has a [`pinnjax.Residual`][pinnjax.Residual].

        """
        return self.residual_function is not None

    def residuals(self, ops: DifferentialOperators) -> Array:
        """Calculate the residual values for all collocation points.

        Evaluation uses the bound [`pinnjax.Residual`][pinnjax.Residual].

        Args:
            ops: A [`DifferentialOperators`][pinnjax.DifferentialOperators] object.


        Returns:
            residuals: Array of residual values for each collocation point.

        Raises:
            InputError: If no collocation points have been generated for this Shape.
            InputError: If no [`pinnjax.Residual`][pinnjax.Residual]
                has been bound to this Shape.

        """
        samples = self.samples
        if samples is None:
            msg = "There are no samples associated with this shape. Call .sample() first."
            config.LOGGER.error(msg)
            raise config.InputError(msg)
        residual_function = self.residual_function
        if residual_function is None:
            msg = (
                "There is no residual function associated with this shape. "
                "Call .set_residual() first."
            )
            config.LOGGER.error(msg)
            raise config.InputError(msg)
        return residual_function(samples, ops)

    def set_loss(self, loss_function: Loss) -> None:
        """Assign a [`pinnjax.Loss`][pinnjax.Loss] object to this Shape.

        Args:
            loss_function: A [`pinnjax.Loss`][pinnjax.Loss] object.

        """
        self.loss_function = loss_function

    def has_loss(self) -> bool:
        """Check if a [`pinnjax.Loss`][pinnjax.Loss] has already been bound.

        Returns:
            bool: Whether the Shape has a [`pinnjax.Loss`][pinnjax.Loss].

        """
        return self.loss_function is not None

    def loss(self, residuals: Array) -> Array:
        """Calculate the loss for all collocation points.

        Evaluation uses the bound [`pinnjax.Loss`][pinnjax.Loss].

        Args:
            residuals: Array of residual values for each collocation point.

        Returns:
            The loss for ``residuals``.

        Raises:
            InputError: If no [`pinnjax.Loss`][pinnjax.Loss] has been bound
                to this Shape.

        """
        loss_function = self.loss_function
        if loss_function is None:
            msg = "There is no loss function associated with this shape. Call .set_loss first."
            config.LOGGER.error(msg)
            raise config.InputError(msg)

        self.loss_val = loss_function(residuals)
        return self.loss_val

    def residual_and_losses(
        self,
        model: NeuralNetwork,
        ops: DifferentialOperators,
    ) -> Array | tuple[Array, Array, Array]:
        """Calculate the loss and residuals. Return the loss."""
        residuals = self.residuals(ops)
        return self.loss(residuals)

    @abstractmethod
    def draw(
        self,
        *,
        show_normals: bool = False,
        normal_scale: float = 1.0,
        fig: Figure | None = None,
        ax: Axes | None = None,
        show: bool = True,
    ) -> tuple[Figure, Axes]:
        """Plot this shape.

        Args:
            show_normals: Draw the outward normal. Default: ``False``.
            normal_scale: Length multiplier for the drawn normal. Default: ``1``.
            fig: Existing figure. A new figure is created when omitted.
            ax: Existing axes. New axes are created when omitted.
            show: Display the figure before returning. Default: ``True``.

        Returns:
            The figure and axes used for the plot.

        Raises:
            NotImplementedError: Always, unless a subclass overrides this method.

        """
        config.LOGGER.error("Not implemented.")
        raise NotImplementedError

def sample(
    self,
    method: SamplingMethod,
    sampling_values: float | Sequence[float | int] | None = None,
    *,
    overwrite: bool = False,
    descriptor_count: int = 32,
) -> tuple[Array, int]:
    """Store collocation points on this shape.

    ``sampling_values`` is one number. ``None`` uses ``1000``. A list is
    rejected here. [`ComplexShape.sample`][pinnjax.geometry.complex.ComplexShape.sample]
    accepts one number per child. When points are already stored and
    ``overwrite`` is false, those points are returned unchanged.

    ``descriptor_count`` is used by
    [`OperatorGeometry.sample`][pinnjax.geometry.operator.OperatorGeometry.sample] and ignored
    here.

    Args:
        method: Sampler that draws the points.
        sampling_values: One sampling size. ``None`` uses the Sampler default.
        overwrite: Replace points that were already stored.
        descriptor_count: Descriptor sample count for an operator geometry.

    Returns:
        samples: Collocation points stored on ``samples``.
        n_points: Number of those points.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``sampling_values`` is a sequence.

    """
    del descriptor_count
    if sampling_values is not None and not isinstance(sampling_values, (float, int)):
        msg = "A Shape takes one sampling value. Pass a list to ComplexShape.sample."
        config.LOGGER.error(msg)
        raise ValueError(msg)

    if not overwrite and self.samples is not None and self.n_points > 0:
        return self.samples, self.n_points

    self.samples = jnp.asarray(
        method(self, sampling_values),
        dtype=config.get_dtype(),
    )
    self.n_points = len(self.samples)

    return self.samples, self.n_points

class Dot(Shape):
    """One point, with an optional time instant or time range.

    Attributes:
        a: Point coordinates. A float becomes a one-element array.
        times: Time range, or ``None`` when the point has one instant or no time.

    """

    times: Time | None

    def __init__(
        self,
        a: float
        | tuple[float]
        | tuple[float, float]
        | tuple[float, float, float]
        | tuple[float, ...]
        | Array,
        times: Time | float | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Store the point and the optional time.

        A float ``times`` is one instant and does not set ``times``. A
        [`Time`][pinnjax.Time] value is a range. Either one adds a time axis to ``dims``.

        Args:
            a: Point coordinates. A float, a coordinate tuple, or an array.
            times: One instant, a time range, or no time. Default: no time.

        """
        super().__init__()
        self.a = jnp.atleast_1d(jnp.asarray(a, dtype=config.get_dtype()))
        self.spatial_dims = self.a.size
        self.dims = self.a.size

        if isinstance(times, (int, float)):
            # Single time instant
            self.single_time = float(times)
            self.times = None
            self.dims += 1
        elif isinstance(times, Time):
            # Time range
            self.single_time = None
            self.times = times
            self.tmin = times.min
            self.tmax = times.max
            self.tstep = times.step
            self.dims += 1
        else:
            # No time dimension
            self.single_time = None
            self.times = None

    def estimate_nsamples(self, value: float) -> int:
        """Return how many samples a time range needs.

        ``value`` is accepted so this method matches [`Shape.estimate_nsamples`][pinnjax.geometry.base.Shape.estimate_nsamples].
        A point does not use it. A point with no time range returns ``1``. A time
        range returns its duration divided by its step, rounded.

        Args:
            value: Unused spacing.

        Returns:
            The sample count.

        """
        # 1 is not enough samples.
        if self.times is None:
            return 1
        return int(jnp.round(self.times.range() / self.tstep))

    def grid_shape(self, value: float) -> tuple[int, ...]:  # noqa: D102
        del value

        if self.times is not None:
            n_time = int(jnp.round((self.tmax - self.tmin) / self.tstep))
            return (n_time,)

        return ()

    def measure(self) -> Array:
        """Return zero.

        Returns:
            A scalar zero array.

        """
        return jnp.asarray(0.0, dtype=config.get_dtype())

    def bounds(self) -> tuple[Array, Array]:
        """Return the point as both the lower and upper bound.

        A time instant or a time range is appended as the last coordinate.

        Returns:
            The lower and upper bounds.

        """
        lower = jnp.asarray(self.a, dtype=config.get_dtype())
        upper = jnp.asarray(self.a, dtype=config.get_dtype())

        if self.single_time is not None:
            time = jnp.asarray([self.single_time], dtype=config.get_dtype())
            lower = jnp.concatenate([lower, time])
            upper = jnp.concatenate([upper, time])

        elif self.times is not None:
            lower = jnp.concatenate(
                [lower, jnp.asarray([self.tmin], dtype=config.get_dtype())],
            )
            upper = jnp.concatenate(
                [upper, jnp.asarray([self.tmax], dtype=config.get_dtype())],
            )

        return lower, upper

    def normal(self) -> Array:
        """Return the sign of a one-dimensional point.

        A coordinate close to ``-1`` or ``1`` returns that exact value. Any other
        coordinate returns its sign.

        Returns:
            A one-element normal.

        Raises:
            NotImplementedError: If the point is not one-dimensional.

        """
        if self.a.shape[0] != 1:
            msg = "Dot.normal() only implemented for 1D"
            config.LOGGER.error(msg)
            raise NotImplementedError(msg)

        x = float(self.a[0])
        if jnp.isclose(x, -1.0):
            return jnp.array([-1.0])
        if jnp.isclose(x, 1.0):
            return jnp.array([1.0])
        return jnp.sign(jnp.array([x], dtype=config.get_dtype()))

    def transform(self, unit_samples: Array) -> Array:
        """Repeat the point for each unit-cube sample.

        With a time range, the last column of ``unit_samples`` maps onto that range
        and one row is returned per sample. A single instant, or no time, returns one
        row containing the point.

        Args:
            unit_samples: Unit-cube coordinates. A time range requires a row per sample.

        Returns:
            The point, with time appended when this dot has a time axis.

        """
        spatial = self.a

        if self.single_time is not None:
            point = jnp.concatenate([spatial, jnp.array([self.single_time])])
        elif self.times is not None:
            t_param = unit_samples[:, -1]
            time = self.tmin + t_param * (self.tmax - self.tmin)
            return jnp.concatenate(
                [jnp.tile(spatial, (unit_samples.shape[0], 1)), time[:, None]],
                axis=1,
            )
        else:
            point = spatial

        return point[jnp.newaxis, :]

    def draw(
        self,
        *,
        show_normals: bool = False,
        normal_scale: float = 1.0,
        fig: Figure | None = None,
        ax: Axes | None = None,
        show: bool = True,
    ) -> tuple[Figure, Axes]:
        """Draw the point.

        Two coordinates use a 2D axes. Any other size requires an existing 3D axes.
        ``show_normals`` and ``normal_scale`` are accepted and not used.

        Args:
            show_normals: Ignored. Default: ``False``.
            normal_scale: Ignored. Default: ``1``.
            fig: Figure to draw on. Default: a new figure in the 2D case.
            ax: Axes to draw on. Default: new 2D axes when the point has two coordinates.
            show: Display the figure before returning it. Default: ``True``.

        Returns:
            The Matplotlib figure and axes.

        Raises:
            TypeError: If the point is not two-dimensional and ``ax`` is not a 3D axes.

        """
        if self.a.size == TWO_DIMENSIONAL:  # 2D line
            if fig is None or ax is None:
                fig, ax = plt.subplots()

            ax.scatter(
                *self.a,
                s=50,
            )

            ax.set_xlabel("X")
            ax.set_ylabel("Y")
            ax.grid(True)
            ax.set_aspect("equal")

            if show:
                plt.show()

        else:  # 3D line
            if not isinstance(ax, Axes3D):
                raise TypeError("A 3D plot requires a 3D axes.")

            if fig is None or ax is None:
                fig = plt.figure()
                ax = fig.add_subplot(111, projection="3d")

            ax.scatter(
                *self.a,
                s=50,
            )

            ax.set_xlabel("X")
            ax.set_ylabel("Y")
            ax.set_zlabel("Z")

            if show:
                plt.show()

        return fig, ax

def __init__(
    self,
    a: float
    | tuple[float]
    | tuple[float, float]
    | tuple[float, float, float]
    | tuple[float, ...]
    | Array,
    times: Time | float | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Store the point and the optional time.

    A float ``times`` is one instant and does not set ``times``. A
    [`Time`][pinnjax.Time] value is a range. Either one adds a time axis to ``dims``.

    Args:
        a: Point coordinates. A float, a coordinate tuple, or an array.
        times: One instant, a time range, or no time. Default: no time.

    """
    super().__init__()
    self.a = jnp.atleast_1d(jnp.asarray(a, dtype=config.get_dtype()))
    self.spatial_dims = self.a.size
    self.dims = self.a.size

    if isinstance(times, (int, float)):
        # Single time instant
        self.single_time = float(times)
        self.times = None
        self.dims += 1
    elif isinstance(times, Time):
        # Time range
        self.single_time = None
        self.times = times
        self.tmin = times.min
        self.tmax = times.max
        self.tstep = times.step
        self.dims += 1
    else:
        # No time dimension
        self.single_time = None
        self.times = None

def estimate_nsamples(self, value: float) -> int:
    """Return how many samples a time range needs.

    ``value`` is accepted so this method matches [`Shape.estimate_nsamples`][pinnjax.geometry.base.Shape.estimate_nsamples].
    A point does not use it. A point with no time range returns ``1``. A time
    range returns its duration divided by its step, rounded.

    Args:
        value: Unused spacing.

    Returns:
        The sample count.

    """
    # 1 is not enough samples.
    if self.times is None:
        return 1
    return int(jnp.round(self.times.range() / self.tstep))

def sample(
    self,
    method: SamplingMethod,
    sampling_values: float | Sequence[float | int] | None = None,
    *,
    overwrite: bool = False,
    descriptor_count: int = 32,
) -> tuple[Array, int]:
    """Store collocation points on this shape.

    ``sampling_values`` is one number. ``None`` uses ``1000``. A list is
    rejected here. [`ComplexShape.sample`][pinnjax.geometry.complex.ComplexShape.sample]
    accepts one number per child. When points are already stored and
    ``overwrite`` is false, those points are returned unchanged.

    ``descriptor_count`` is used by
    [`OperatorGeometry.sample`][pinnjax.geometry.operator.OperatorGeometry.sample] and ignored
    here.

    Args:
        method: Sampler that draws the points.
        sampling_values: One sampling size. ``None`` uses the Sampler default.
        overwrite: Replace points that were already stored.
        descriptor_count: Descriptor sample count for an operator geometry.

    Returns:
        samples: Collocation points stored on ``samples``.
        n_points: Number of those points.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``sampling_values`` is a sequence.

    """
    del descriptor_count
    if sampling_values is not None and not isinstance(sampling_values, (float, int)):
        msg = "A Shape takes one sampling value. Pass a list to ComplexShape.sample."
        config.LOGGER.error(msg)
        raise ValueError(msg)

    if not overwrite and self.samples is not None and self.n_points > 0:
        return self.samples, self.n_points

    self.samples = jnp.asarray(
        method(self, sampling_values),
        dtype=config.get_dtype(),
    )
    self.n_points = len(self.samples)

    return self.samples, self.n_points

class Line(Shape):
    """A straight segment from ``origin`` to ``end``, with an optional time axis.

    Attributes:
        origin: Start of the segment.
        end: End of the segment.
        times: Time range, or ``None`` when the segment has one instant or no time.

    """

    origin: Array
    end: Array
    _normal_override: Array | None = None

    def __init__(
        self,
        origin: float
        | tuple[float]
        | tuple[float, float]
        | tuple[float, float, float]
        | tuple[float, ...]
        | Array,
        end: float
        | tuple[float]
        | tuple[float, float]
        | tuple[float, float, float]
        | tuple[float, ...]
        | Array,
        times: Time | float | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Store the endpoints and the optional time.

        A float ``times`` is one instant and does not set ``times``. A
        [`Time`][pinnjax.Time] value is a range. Either one adds a time axis to ``dims``.

        Args:
            origin: Start of the segment. A float, a coordinate tuple, or an array.
            end: End of the segment, in the same form as ``origin``.
            times: One instant, a time range, or no time. Default: no time.

        """
        super().__init__()
        self.origin = jnp.atleast_1d(
            jnp.array(origin, dtype=config.get_dtype()),
        )  # Ensure proper dtype
        self.end = jnp.atleast_1d(jnp.array(end, dtype=config.get_dtype()))
        self.spatial_dims = self.origin.size
        self.dims = self.origin.size

        # Handle different time specifications
        if isinstance(times, (int, float)):
            # Single time instant
            self.single_time = float(times)
            self.times = None
            self.dims += 1
        elif isinstance(times, Time):
            # Time range
            self.single_time = None
            self.times = times
            self.tmin = times.min
            self.tmax = times.max
            self.tstep = times.step
            self.dims += 1
        else:
            # No time dimension
            self.single_time = None
            self.times = None

    def measure(self) -> Array:
        """Return the distance from ``origin`` to ``end``.

        Returns:
            The length as a scalar array.

        """
        return jnp.linalg.norm(self.end - self.origin)

    def normal(self) -> Array:
        """Return a unit normal in the plane of a two-dimensional segment.

        The direction is the segment rotated 90 degrees counterclockwise. A stored
        ``_normal_override`` is returned instead when one is set. A segment of length
        zero returns ``[0, 1]``.

        Returns:
            The unit normal.

        Raises:
            NotImplementedError: If the segment is not two-dimensional.

        """
        if self._normal_override is not None:
            return self._normal_override

        if self.origin.shape[0] == TWO_DIMENSIONAL:
            direction = self.end - self.origin
            # Perpendicular in 2D: rotate 90 degrees counterclockwise
            normal_2d = jnp.array(
                [-direction[1], direction[0]],
                dtype=config.get_dtype(),
            )
            norm_magnitude = jnp.linalg.norm(normal_2d)
            return jnp.where(
                norm_magnitude > 1e-12,
                normal_2d / norm_magnitude,
                jnp.array([0.0, 1.0], dtype=config.get_dtype()),
            )  # Fallback
        msg = "Normal for 3D lines not implemented."
        config.LOGGER.error("Normal for 3D lines not implemented.")
        raise NotImplementedError(msg)

    def bounds(self) -> tuple[Array, Array]:
        """Return the box around the two endpoints.

        A time instant or a time range is appended as the last coordinate.

        Returns:
            The lower and upper bounds.

        """
        lower = jnp.minimum(self.origin, self.end)
        upper = jnp.maximum(self.origin, self.end)

        if self.single_time is not None:
            # Single time point
            lower = jnp.concatenate([lower, jnp.array([self.single_time])])
            upper = jnp.concatenate([upper, jnp.array([self.single_time])])
        elif self.times is not None:
            # Time range
            lower = jnp.concatenate([lower, jnp.array([self.tmin])])
            upper = jnp.concatenate([upper, jnp.array([self.tmax])])

        return lower, upper

    def transform(self, unit_samples: Array) -> Array:
        """Map the first unit coordinate along the segment.

        ``0`` is ``origin`` and ``1`` is ``end``. A single instant is appended to every
        point. A time range uses the second unit coordinate.

        Args:
            unit_samples: Unit-cube coordinates, shaped ``(..., dims)``.

        Returns:
            Points on the segment, with time appended when this line has a time axis.

        """
        # unit_samples shape (..., 1) for spatial parameter
        t_param = unit_samples[..., 0:1]  # Parameter along line [0,1]

        # Interpolate along line: a + t*(b-a)
        spatial = self.origin + t_param * (self.end - self.origin)

        if self.single_time is not None:
            # Add constant time dimension
            time = jnp.full((*unit_samples.shape[:-1], 1), self.single_time)
            return jnp.concatenate([spatial, time], axis=-1)
        if self.times is not None:
            # Add time range
            t_time = unit_samples[..., 1:2]  # Time parameter [0,1]
            time = self.tmin + t_time * (self.tmax - self.tmin)
            return jnp.concatenate([spatial, time], axis=-1)
        return spatial

    def estimate_nsamples(self, value: float = 0.1) -> int:
        """Return a grid count from the segment length divided by ``value``.

        Thus, the ```value`` represents the discrete resolution.

        A time range multiplies that count by the number of time steps. One instant
        does not.

        Args:
            value: Spacing along the segment. Default: ``0.1``.

        Returns:
            The sample count, rounded.

        """
        length = jnp.linalg.norm(self.end - self.origin)
        n_space = jnp.round(length / value)

        if self.single_time is not None:
            # Single time instant - only spatial samples needed
            return int(n_space)
        if self.times is not None:
            # Time range - multiply by time samples
            n_time = jnp.round((self.tmax - self.tmin) / self.tstep)
            return int(n_space * n_time)
        return int(n_space)

    def grid_shape(self, value: float) -> tuple[int, ...]:  # noqa: D102
        length = jnp.linalg.norm(self.end - self.origin)
        n_space = int(jnp.round(length / value))

        if self.times is not None:
            n_time = int(jnp.round((self.tmax - self.tmin) / self.tstep))
            return n_space, n_time

        return (n_space,)

    def draw(
        self,
        *,
        show_normals: bool = False,
        normal_scale: float = 1.0,
        fig: Figure | None = None,
        ax: Axes | None = None,
        show: bool = True,
    ) -> tuple[Figure, Axes]:
        """Draw the segment.

        One coordinate is drawn on the horizontal axis at height zero. Two coordinates
        are drawn in the plane, with an arrow when ``show_normals`` is true. Three
        coordinates require an existing 3D axes.

        Args:
            show_normals: Draw the normal in the two-dimensional case. Default: ``False``.
            normal_scale: Length multiplier for that arrow. Default: ``1``.
            fig: Figure to draw on. Default: a new figure in the 1D and 2D cases.
            ax: Axes to draw on. Default: new 2D axes when the segment is not three-dimensional.
            show: Display the figure before returning it. Default: ``True``.

        Returns:
            The Matplotlib figure and axes.

        Raises:
            TypeError: If the segment is three-dimensional and ``ax`` is not a 3D axes.
            pinnjax.InputError: If the segment is not one, two, or three-dimensional.

        """
        if self.origin.size == 1:
            if fig is None or ax is None:
                fig, ax = plt.subplots()

            ax.plot([self.origin, self.end], [0, 0], "b-", linewidth=2)
            ax.plot([self.origin, self.end], [0, 0], "bo", markersize=5)

        elif self.origin.size == TWO_DIMENSIONAL:  # 2D line
            if fig is None or ax is None:
                fig, ax = plt.subplots()

            ax.plot(
                [self.origin[0], self.end[0]],
                [self.origin[1], self.end[1]],
                "b-",
                linewidth=2,
            )
            ax.plot(
                [self.origin[0], self.end[0]],
                [self.origin[1], self.end[1]],
                "bo",
                markersize=5,
            )

            if show_normals:
                midpoint = (self.origin + self.end) / 2
                n = self.normal() * normal_scale
                ax.arrow(
                    float(midpoint[0]),
                    float(midpoint[1]),
                    float(n[0]),
                    float(n[1]),
                    head_width=0.1,
                    head_length=0.1,
                    fc="red",
                    ec="red",
                )

            ax.set_xlabel("X")
            ax.set_ylabel("Y")
            ax.grid(True)
            ax.set_aspect("equal")

            if show:
                plt.show()

        elif self.origin.size == THREE_DIMENSIONAL:  # 3D line
            if not isinstance(ax, Axes3D):
                raise TypeError("A 3D plot requires a 3D axes.")

            if fig is None or ax is None:
                fig = plt.figure()
                ax = fig.add_subplot(111, projection="3d")

            ax.plot(
                [self.origin[0], self.end[0]],
                [self.origin[1], self.end[1]],
                [self.origin[2], self.end[2]],
                "b-",
                linewidth=2,
            )
            ax.scatter(
                [self.origin[0], self.end[0]],
                [self.origin[1], self.end[1]],
                [self.origin[2], self.end[2]],
                c="blue",
                s=50,
            )

            ax.set_xlabel("X")
            ax.set_ylabel("Y")
            ax.set_zlabel("Z")

        else:
            msg = "Unsupported dimension size."
            config.LOGGER.error(msg)
            raise config.InputError(msg)

        if show:
            plt.show()

        return fig, ax

def __init__(
    self,
    origin: float
    | tuple[float]
    | tuple[float, float]
    | tuple[float, float, float]
    | tuple[float, ...]
    | Array,
    end: float
    | tuple[float]
    | tuple[float, float]
    | tuple[float, float, float]
    | tuple[float, ...]
    | Array,
    times: Time | float | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Store the endpoints and the optional time.

    A float ``times`` is one instant and does not set ``times``. A
    [`Time`][pinnjax.Time] value is a range. Either one adds a time axis to ``dims``.

    Args:
        origin: Start of the segment. A float, a coordinate tuple, or an array.
        end: End of the segment, in the same form as ``origin``.
        times: One instant, a time range, or no time. Default: no time.

    """
    super().__init__()
    self.origin = jnp.atleast_1d(
        jnp.array(origin, dtype=config.get_dtype()),
    )  # Ensure proper dtype
    self.end = jnp.atleast_1d(jnp.array(end, dtype=config.get_dtype()))
    self.spatial_dims = self.origin.size
    self.dims = self.origin.size

    # Handle different time specifications
    if isinstance(times, (int, float)):
        # Single time instant
        self.single_time = float(times)
        self.times = None
        self.dims += 1
    elif isinstance(times, Time):
        # Time range
        self.single_time = None
        self.times = times
        self.tmin = times.min
        self.tmax = times.max
        self.tstep = times.step
        self.dims += 1
    else:
        # No time dimension
        self.single_time = None
        self.times = None

def normal(self) -> Array:
    """Return a unit normal in the plane of a two-dimensional segment.

    The direction is the segment rotated 90 degrees counterclockwise. A stored
    ``_normal_override`` is returned instead when one is set. A segment of length
    zero returns ``[0, 1]``.

    Returns:
        The unit normal.

    Raises:
        NotImplementedError: If the segment is not two-dimensional.

    """
    if self._normal_override is not None:
        return self._normal_override

    if self.origin.shape[0] == TWO_DIMENSIONAL:
        direction = self.end - self.origin
        # Perpendicular in 2D: rotate 90 degrees counterclockwise
        normal_2d = jnp.array(
            [-direction[1], direction[0]],
            dtype=config.get_dtype(),
        )
        norm_magnitude = jnp.linalg.norm(normal_2d)
        return jnp.where(
            norm_magnitude > 1e-12,
            normal_2d / norm_magnitude,
            jnp.array([0.0, 1.0], dtype=config.get_dtype()),
        )  # Fallback
    msg = "Normal for 3D lines not implemented."
    config.LOGGER.error("Normal for 3D lines not implemented.")
    raise NotImplementedError(msg)

def residuals(self, ops: DifferentialOperators) -> Array:
    """Calculate the residual values for all collocation points.

    Evaluation uses the bound [`pinnjax.Residual`][pinnjax.Residual].

    Args:
        ops: A [`DifferentialOperators`][pinnjax.DifferentialOperators] object.


    Returns:
        residuals: Array of residual values for each collocation point.

    Raises:
        InputError: If no collocation points have been generated for this Shape.
        InputError: If no [`pinnjax.Residual`][pinnjax.Residual]
            has been bound to this Shape.

    """
    samples = self.samples
    if samples is None:
        msg = "There are no samples associated with this shape. Call .sample() first."
        config.LOGGER.error(msg)
        raise config.InputError(msg)
    residual_function = self.residual_function
    if residual_function is None:
        msg = (
            "There is no residual function associated with this shape. "
            "Call .set_residual() first."
        )
        config.LOGGER.error(msg)
        raise config.InputError(msg)
    return residual_function(samples, ops)

def sample(
    self,
    method: SamplingMethod,
    sampling_values: float | Sequence[float | int] | None = None,
    *,
    overwrite: bool = False,
    descriptor_count: int = 32,
) -> tuple[Array, int]:
    """Store collocation points on this shape.

    ``sampling_values`` is one number. ``None`` uses ``1000``. A list is
    rejected here. [`ComplexShape.sample`][pinnjax.geometry.complex.ComplexShape.sample]
    accepts one number per child. When points are already stored and
    ``overwrite`` is false, those points are returned unchanged.

    ``descriptor_count`` is used by
    [`OperatorGeometry.sample`][pinnjax.geometry.operator.OperatorGeometry.sample] and ignored
    here.

    Args:
        method: Sampler that draws the points.
        sampling_values: One sampling size. ``None`` uses the Sampler default.
        overwrite: Replace points that were already stored.
        descriptor_count: Descriptor sample count for an operator geometry.

    Returns:
        samples: Collocation points stored on ``samples``.
        n_points: Number of those points.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``sampling_values`` is a sequence.

    """
    del descriptor_count
    if sampling_values is not None and not isinstance(sampling_values, (float, int)):
        msg = "A Shape takes one sampling value. Pass a list to ComplexShape.sample."
        config.LOGGER.error(msg)
        raise ValueError(msg)

    if not overwrite and self.samples is not None and self.n_points > 0:
        return self.samples, self.n_points

    self.samples = jnp.asarray(
        method(self, sampling_values),
        dtype=config.get_dtype(),
    )
    self.n_points = len(self.samples)

    return self.samples, self.n_points

def transform(self, unit_samples: Array) -> Array:
    """Map the first unit coordinate along the segment.

    ``0`` is ``origin`` and ``1`` is ``end``. A single instant is appended to every
    point. A time range uses the second unit coordinate.

    Args:
        unit_samples: Unit-cube coordinates, shaped ``(..., dims)``.

    Returns:
        Points on the segment, with time appended when this line has a time axis.

    """
    # unit_samples shape (..., 1) for spatial parameter
    t_param = unit_samples[..., 0:1]  # Parameter along line [0,1]

    # Interpolate along line: a + t*(b-a)
    spatial = self.origin + t_param * (self.end - self.origin)

    if self.single_time is not None:
        # Add constant time dimension
        time = jnp.full((*unit_samples.shape[:-1], 1), self.single_time)
        return jnp.concatenate([spatial, time], axis=-1)
    if self.times is not None:
        # Add time range
        t_time = unit_samples[..., 1:2]  # Time parameter [0,1]
        time = self.tmin + t_time * (self.tmax - self.tmin)
        return jnp.concatenate([spatial, time], axis=-1)
    return spatial

class Triangle(Shape):
    """A triangle through three vertices, with an optional time axis.

    Attributes:
        a: First vertex.
        b: Second vertex.
        c: Third vertex.
        times: Time range, or ``None`` when the triangle has one instant or no time.

    """

    # TODO(@mjryande): Ensure functionality with an example.
    def __init__(
        self,
        a: tuple[float, ...] | Array,
        b: tuple[float, ...] | Array,
        c: tuple[float, ...] | Array,
        times: Time | float | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Store the three vertices and the optional time.

        The vertices must share one shape, and each must be two or three coordinates.
        A float ``times`` is one instant. A [`Time`][pinnjax.Time] value is a range.
        Either one adds a time axis to ``dims``.

        Args:
            a: First vertex.
            b: Second vertex.
            c: Third vertex.
            times: One instant, a time range, or no time. Default: no time.

        Raises:
            pinnjax.InputError: If the vertices differ in shape, or a vertex is not two
                or three-dimensional.

        """
        super().__init__()

        self.a = jnp.asarray(a, dtype=config.get_dtype())
        self.b = jnp.asarray(b, dtype=config.get_dtype())
        self.c = jnp.asarray(c, dtype=config.get_dtype())

        if self.a.shape != self.b.shape or self.a.shape != self.c.shape:
            msg = "Triangle vertices a, b, and c must have the same dimension."
            config.LOGGER.error(msg)
            raise config.InputError(msg)

        if self.a.ndim != 1 or self.a.size not in {
            TWO_DIMENSIONAL,
            THREE_DIMENSIONAL,
        }:
            msg = "Triangle vertices must be 2D or 3D coordinates."
            config.LOGGER.error(msg)
            raise config.InputError(msg)

        self.spatial_dims = self.a.size
        self.dims = self.spatial_dims

        if isinstance(times, (int, float)):
            self.single_time = float(times)
            self.times = None
            self.dims += 1
        elif isinstance(times, Time):
            self.single_time = None
            self.times = times
            self.tmin = times.min
            self.tmax = times.max
            self.tstep = times.step
            self.dims += 1
        else:
            self.single_time = None
            self.times = None

    def bounds(self) -> tuple[Array, Array]:
        """Return the box around the three vertices.

        A time instant or a time range is appended as the last coordinate.

        Returns:
            The lower and upper bounds.

        """
        lower = jnp.minimum(jnp.minimum(self.a, self.b), self.c)
        upper = jnp.maximum(jnp.maximum(self.a, self.b), self.c)

        if self.single_time is not None:
            # Single time point
            lower = jnp.concatenate([lower, jnp.array([self.single_time])])
            upper = jnp.concatenate([upper, jnp.array([self.single_time])])
        elif self.times is not None:
            # Time range
            lower = jnp.concatenate([lower, jnp.array([self.tmin])])
            upper = jnp.concatenate([upper, jnp.array([self.tmax])])

        return lower, upper

    def transform(self, unit_samples: Array) -> Array:
        """Map unit-square coordinates onto the triangle.

        The first two columns are barycentric parameters. A single instant is appended
        to every point. A time range uses the last column.

        Args:
            unit_samples: Unit-cube coordinates, with one row per sample.

        Returns:
            Points on the triangle, with time appended when this triangle has a time axis.

        """
        if self.single_time is not None:
            # Single time instant case
            u_space = unit_samples[:, :2]
            b0, b1, b2 = _sample_triangle_barycentric(u_space)

            spatial = b0[:, None] * self.a + b1[:, None] * self.b + b2[:, None] * self.c
            time = jnp.full((spatial.shape[0], 1), self.single_time)
            return jnp.concatenate([spatial, time], axis=1)
        if self.times is not None:
            # Time range case
            u_space = unit_samples[:, :2]
            u_time = unit_samples[:, -1]  # Use -1 for time, always last!
            b0, b1, b2 = _sample_triangle_barycentric(u_space)

            spatial = b0[:, None] * self.a + b1[:, None] * self.b + b2[:, None] * self.c
            time = self.tmin + u_time * (self.tmax - self.tmin)
            return jnp.concatenate([spatial, time[:, None]], axis=1)
        # No time dimension
        b0, b1, b2 = _sample_triangle_barycentric(unit_samples)
        return b0[:, None] * self.a + b1[:, None] * self.b + b2[:, None] * self.c

    def estimate_nsamples(self, value: float = 0.1) -> int:
        """Return a grid count from the triangle area divided by ``value`` squared.

        Thus, ``value`` represents the discrete resolution.

        A time range multiplies that count by the number of time steps. One instant
        does not.

        Args:
            value: Spacing used to turn the area into a count. Default: ``0.1``.

        Returns:
            The sample count, rounded.

        """
        area = 0.5 * jnp.linalg.norm(jnp.cross(self.b - self.a, self.c - self.a))
        n_space = jnp.round(area / value**2)

        if self.single_time is not None:
            # Single time instant - only spatial samples needed
            return int(n_space)
        if self.times is not None:
            # Time range - multiply by time samples
            n_time = jnp.round((self.tmax - self.tmin) / self.tstep)
            return int(n_space * n_time)
        return int(n_space)

    def grid_shape(self, value: float) -> tuple[int, ...]:  # noqa: D102
        area = 0.5 * jnp.linalg.norm(jnp.cross(self.b - self.a, self.c - self.a))
        n_space = max(int(jnp.round(area / value**2)), 1)
        n_side = max(int(jnp.round(jnp.sqrt(n_space))), 1)

        if self.times is not None:
            n_time = max(int(jnp.round((self.tmax - self.tmin) / self.tstep)), 1)
            return n_side, n_side, n_time

        return n_side, n_side

    def normal(self) -> Array:
        """Return the unit normal from the cross product of two edges.

        A two-dimensional triangle is padded with a zero third coordinate before the
        cross product.

        Returns:
            The unit normal.

        """
        va, vb, vc = _as3(self.a), _as3(self.b), _as3(self.c)
        n = jnp.cross(vb - va, vc - va)
        return n / jnp.linalg.norm(n)

    def measure(self) -> Array:
        """Return the area of the triangle.

        Returns:
            The area as a scalar array.

        Raises:
            pinnjax.InputError: If the triangle is not two or three dimensional.

        """
        u = self.b - self.a
        v = self.c - self.a

        if self.spatial_dims == TWO_DIMENSIONAL:
            area = 0.5 * jnp.abs(u[0] * v[1] - u[1] * v[0])
        elif self.spatial_dims == THREE_DIMENSIONAL:
            area = 0.5 * jnp.linalg.norm(jnp.cross(u, v))
        else:
            msg = "Triangle.measure() only supports 2D or 3D triangles."
            config.LOGGER.error(msg)
            raise config.InputError(msg)

        return jnp.asarray(area, dtype=config.get_dtype())

    def draw(
        self,
        *,
        show_normals: bool = False,
        normal_scale: float = 1.0,
        fig: Figure | None = None,
        ax: Axes | None = None,
        show: bool = True,
    ) -> tuple[Figure, Axes]:
        """Draw the triangle in two or three dimensions.

        Args:
            show_normals: Draw the normal arrow for a 3D triangle. Default: ``False``.
            normal_scale: Length multiplier for the normal arrow. Default: ``1``.
            fig: Figure to draw on. A new figure is created when omitted.
            ax: Existing axes. New axes are created when omitted.
            show: Display the figure before returning it. Default: ``True``.

        Returns:
            The Matplotlib figure and axes.

        Raises:
            TypeError: If the supplied axes does not match the triangle dimension.

        """
        if self.spatial_dims == TWO_DIMENSIONAL:
            if ax is None:
                if fig is None:
                    fig = plt.figure()
                ax = fig.add_subplot(111)
            elif isinstance(ax, Axes3D):
                raise TypeError("A 2D triangle requires a 2D axes.")

            if fig is None:
                fig = ax.get_figure(root=True)

            pts = jnp.stack([self.a, self.b, self.c, self.a])
            ax.plot(pts[:, 0], pts[:, 1], color="black", marker="o")

            if show_normals:
                config.LOGGER.warning("Cannot display an out-of-plane normal on a 2D axes.")

            ax.set_xlabel("X")
            ax.set_ylabel("Y")
            ax.set_aspect("equal", adjustable="box")

        elif self.spatial_dims == THREE_DIMENSIONAL:
            if ax is None:
                if fig is None:
                    fig = plt.figure()
                ax = fig.add_subplot(111, projection="3d")

            if not isinstance(ax, Axes3D):
                raise TypeError("A 3D triangle requires a 3D axes.")

            if fig is None:
                fig = ax.get_figure(root=True)

            pts = jnp.stack([self.a, self.b, self.c, self.a])
            ax.plot(pts[:, 0], pts[:, 1], pts[:, 2], color="black", marker="o")

            if show_normals:
                centroid = (self.a + self.b + self.c) / 3.0
                n = self.normal() * normal_scale
                ax.quiver(
                    centroid[0],
                    centroid[1],
                    centroid[2],
                    n[0],
                    n[1],
                    n[2],
                    color="blue",
                    linewidth=2,
                )

            ax.set_xlabel("X")
            ax.set_ylabel("Y")
            ax.set_zlabel("Z")
            ax.set_box_aspect([1.0, 1.0, 1.0])

        else:
            raise TypeError(f"Cannot draw a {self.spatial_dims}D triangle.")

        if show:
            plt.show()

        return cast(Figure, ax.get_figure(root=True)), ax

def loss(self, residuals: Array) -> Array:
    """Calculate the loss for all collocation points.

    v = self.c - self.a

    if self.spatial_dims == TWO_DIMENSIONAL:
        area = 0.5 * jnp.abs(u[0] * v[1] - u[1] * v[0])
    elif self.spatial_dims == THREE_DIMENSIONAL:
        area = 0.5 * jnp.linalg.norm(jnp.cross(u, v))
    else:
        msg = "Triangle.measure() only supports 2D or 3D triangles."
        config.LOGGER.error(msg)
        raise config.InputError(msg)

    return jnp.asarray(area, dtype=config.get_dtype())

def normal(self) -> Array:
    """Return the unit normal from the cross product of two edges.

    A two-dimensional triangle is padded with a zero third coordinate before the
    cross product.

    Returns:
        The unit normal.

    """
    va, vb, vc = _as3(self.a), _as3(self.b), _as3(self.c)
    n = jnp.cross(vb - va, vc - va)
    return n / jnp.linalg.norm(n)

    """Calculate the residual values for all collocation points.

            has been bound to this Shape.

    samples = self.samples
    if samples is None:
        msg = "There are no samples associated with this shape. Call .sample() first."

        config.LOGGER.error(msg)

    return residual_function(samples, ops)

def sample(
    self,
    method: SamplingMethod,
    sampling_values: float | Sequence[float | int] | None = None,
    *,
    overwrite: bool = False,
    descriptor_count: int = 32,
) -> tuple[Array, int]:
    """Store collocation points on this shape.

    ``sampling_values`` is one number. ``None`` uses ``1000``. A list is
    rejected here. [`ComplexShape.sample`][pinnjax.geometry.complex.ComplexShape.sample]
    accepts one number per child. When points are already stored and
    ``overwrite`` is false, those points are returned unchanged.

    ``descriptor_count`` is used by
    [`OperatorGeometry.sample`][pinnjax.geometry.operator.OperatorGeometry.sample] and ignored
    here.

    Args:
        method: Sampler that draws the points.
        sampling_values: One sampling size. ``None`` uses the Sampler default.
        overwrite: Replace points that were already stored.
        descriptor_count: Descriptor sample count for an operator geometry.

    Returns:
        samples: Collocation points stored on ``samples``.
        n_points: Number of those points.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``sampling_values`` is a sequence.

    """
    del descriptor_count
    if sampling_values is not None and not isinstance(sampling_values, (float, int)):
        msg = "A Shape takes one sampling value. Pass a list to ComplexShape.sample."
        config.LOGGER.error(msg)
        raise ValueError(msg)

    if not overwrite and self.samples is not None and self.n_points > 0:
        return self.samples, self.n_points

    self.samples = jnp.asarray(
        method(self, sampling_values),
        dtype=config.get_dtype(),
    )
    self.n_points = len(self.samples)

    return self.samples, self.n_points

def transform(self, unit_samples: Array) -> Array:
    """Map unit-square coordinates onto the triangle.

    The first two columns are barycentric parameters. A single instant is appended
    to every point. A time range uses the last column.

    Args:
        unit_samples: Unit-cube coordinates, with one row per sample.

    Returns:
        Points on the triangle, with time appended when this triangle has a time axis.

    """
    if self.single_time is not None:
        # Single time instant case
        u_space = unit_samples[:, :2]
        b0, b1, b2 = _sample_triangle_barycentric(u_space)

        spatial = b0[:, None] * self.a + b1[:, None] * self.b + b2[:, None] * self.c
        time = jnp.full((spatial.shape[0], 1), self.single_time)
        return jnp.concatenate([spatial, time], axis=1)
    if self.times is not None:
        # Time range case
        u_space = unit_samples[:, :2]
        u_time = unit_samples[:, -1]  # Use -1 for time, always last!
        b0, b1, b2 = _sample_triangle_barycentric(u_space)

        spatial = b0[:, None] * self.a + b1[:, None] * self.b + b2[:, None] * self.c
        time = self.tmin + u_time * (self.tmax - self.tmin)
        return jnp.concatenate([spatial, time[:, None]], axis=1)
    # No time dimension
    b0, b1, b2 = _sample_triangle_barycentric(unit_samples)
    return b0[:, None] * self.a + b1[:, None] * self.b + b2[:, None] * self.c

class Rectangle(Shape):
    """A parallelogram spanned by two edges from ``origin``.

    Attributes:
        origin: Corner where the two edges meet.
        edge1: First edge.
        edge2: Second edge.
        times: Time range, or ``None`` when the rectangle has one instant or no time.

    """

    origin: Array
    edge1: Array
    edge2: Array
    times: Time | None
    _outward_normal: Array | None = None
    _normal_override: Array | None = None

    def __init__(
        self,
        origin: tuple[float, ...] | Array,
        edge1: tuple[float, ...] | Array,
        edge2: tuple[float, ...] | Array,
        times: Time | float | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Store the corner, the two edges, and the optional time.

        A float ``times`` is one instant and does not set ``times``. A
        [`Time`][pinnjax.Time] value is a range. Either one adds a time axis to ``dims``.

        Args:
            origin: Corner where the two edges meet.
            edge1: First edge, in the same dimension as ``origin``.
            edge2: Second edge, in the same dimension as ``origin``.
            times: One instant, a time range, or no time. Default: no time.

        """
        super().__init__()
        self.origin = jnp.array(origin)
        self.edge1 = jnp.array(edge1)
        self.edge2 = jnp.array(edge2)
        self.spatial_dims = self.origin.size
        self.dims = self.origin.size

        # Handle different time specifications
        if isinstance(times, (int, float)):
            # Single time instant
            self.single_time = float(times)
            self.times = None
            self.dims += 1
        elif isinstance(times, Time):
            # Time range
            self.single_time = None
            self.times = times
            self.tmin = times.min
            self.tmax = times.max
            self.tstep = times.step
            self.dims += 1
        else:
            # No time dimension
            self.single_time = None
            self.times = None

    def measure(self) -> Array:
        """Return the area of the parallelogram spanned by the two edges.

        Returns:
            The area as a scalar array.

        """
        return jnp.linalg.norm(jnp.cross(self.edge1, self.edge2))

    def bounds(self) -> tuple[Array, Array]:
        """Return the box around the four corners.

        A time instant or a time range is appended as the last coordinate.

        Returns:
            The lower and upper bounds.

        """
        corners = jnp.stack(
            [
                self.origin,
                self.origin + self.edge1,
                self.origin + self.edge2,
                self.origin + self.edge1 + self.edge2,
            ],
        )
        lower = jnp.min(corners, axis=0)
        upper = jnp.max(corners, axis=0)

        if self.single_time is not None:
            # Single time point
            lower = jnp.concatenate([lower, jnp.array([self.single_time])])
            upper = jnp.concatenate([upper, jnp.array([self.single_time])])
        elif self.times is not None:
            # Time range
            lower = jnp.concatenate([lower, jnp.array([self.tmin])])
            upper = jnp.concatenate([upper, jnp.array([self.tmax])])

        return lower, upper

    def transform(self, unit_samples: Array) -> Array:
        """Map the first two unit coordinates along the two edges.

        A single instant is appended to every point. A time range uses the third unit
        coordinate.

        Args:
            unit_samples: Unit-cube coordinates, shaped ``(..., dims)``.

        Returns:
            Points on the parallelogram, with time appended when this rectangle has a
            time axis.

        """
        # Spatial transformation
        pt = self.origin + unit_samples[..., 0:1] * self.edge1 + unit_samples[..., 1:2] * self.edge2

        if self.single_time is not None:
            # Add constant time dimension
            t = jnp.full((*unit_samples.shape[:-1], 1), self.single_time)
            pt = jnp.concatenate([pt, t], axis=-1)
        elif self.times is not None:
            # Add time range
            t = self.tmin + unit_samples[..., 2:3] * (self.tmax - self.tmin)
            pt = jnp.concatenate([pt, t], axis=-1)

        return pt

    def estimate_nsamples(self, value: float) -> int:
        """Return a grid count from the two edge lengths.

        Each edge contributes at least two points, from its length divided by
        ``value``. The two counts are multiplied. A time range multiplies again by its
        step count, also at least two. One instant does not.

        Args:
            value: Spacing along each edge.

        Returns:
            The sample count.

        """
        len1 = jnp.linalg.norm(self.edge1)
        len2 = jnp.linalg.norm(self.edge2)
        n_space = jnp.maximum(int(jnp.round(len1 / value)), 2) * jnp.maximum(
            int(jnp.round(len2 / value)),
            2,
        )

        if self.single_time is not None:
            # Single time instant - only spatial samples needed
            return int(n_space)
        if self.times is not None:
            # Time range - multiply by time samples
            n_time = jnp.maximum(jnp.round((self.tmax - self.tmin) / self.tstep), 2)
            return int(n_space * n_time)
        return int(n_space)

    def grid_shape(self, value: float) -> tuple[int, ...]:  # noqa: D102
        n1 = max(int(jnp.round(jnp.linalg.norm(self.edge1) / value)), 2)
        n2 = max(int(jnp.round(jnp.linalg.norm(self.edge2) / value)), 2)

        if self.times is not None:
            n_time = max(int(jnp.round((self.tmax - self.tmin) / self.tstep)), 2)
            return n1, n2, n_time

        return n1, n2

    def normal(self) -> Array:
        """Return the unit normal from the cross product of the two edges.

        A stored ``_normal_override`` is returned instead when one is set. A
        two-dimensional edge is padded with a zero third coordinate before the cross
        product.

        Returns:
            The unit normal.

        """
        if self._normal_override is not None:
            return self._normal_override
        e1, e2 = _as3(self.edge1), _as3(self.edge2)
        n = jnp.cross(e1, e2)
        return n / jnp.linalg.norm(n)

    def draw(
        self,
        *,
        show_normals: bool = False,
        normal_scale: float = 1.0,
        fig: Figure | None = None,
        ax: Axes | None = None,
        show: bool = True,
    ) -> tuple[Figure, Axes]:
        """Draw the rectangle in two or three dimensions.

        Args:
            show_normals: Draw the normal arrow for a 3D rectangle. Default: ``False``.
            normal_scale: Length multiplier for the normal arrow. Default: ``1``.
            fig: Figure to draw on. A new figure is created when omitted.
            ax: Existing axes. New axes are created when omitted.
            show: Display the figure before returning it. Default: ``True``.

        Returns:
            The Matplotlib figure and axes.

        Raises:
            TypeError: If the supplied axes does not match the rectangle dimension.

        """
        if self.spatial_dims == TWO_DIMENSIONAL:
            if ax is None:
                if fig is None:
                    fig = plt.figure()
                ax = fig.add_subplot(111)
            elif isinstance(ax, Axes3D):
                raise TypeError("A 2D rectangle requires a 2D axes.")

            v0 = self.origin
            v1 = self.origin + self.edge1
            v2 = self.origin + self.edge1 + self.edge2
            v3 = self.origin + self.edge2

            pts = jnp.stack([v0, v1, v2, v3, v0])
            ax.plot(pts[:, 0], pts[:, 1], color="black", marker="o")

            if show_normals:
                config.LOGGER.warning("Cannot display an out-of-plane normal on a 2D axes.")

            ax.set_xlabel("X")
            ax.set_ylabel("Y")
            ax.set_aspect("equal", adjustable="box")

        elif self.spatial_dims == THREE_DIMENSIONAL:
            if ax is None:
                if fig is None:
                    fig = plt.figure()
                ax = fig.add_subplot(111, projection="3d")

            if not isinstance(ax, Axes3D):
                raise TypeError("A 3D rectangle requires a 3D axes.")

            v0 = self.origin
            v1 = self.origin + self.edge1
            v2 = self.origin + self.edge1 + self.edge2
            v3 = self.origin + self.edge2

            pts = jnp.stack([v0, v1, v2, v3, v0])
            ax.plot(pts[:, 0], pts[:, 1], pts[:, 2], color="black", marker="o")

            if show_normals:
                centroid = (v0 + v1 + v2 + v3) / 4.0
                n = self.normal() * normal_scale
                ax.quiver(
                    centroid[0],
                    centroid[1],
                    centroid[2],
                    n[0],
                    n[1],
                    n[2],
                    color="blue",
                    linewidth=2,
                )

            ax.set_xlabel("X")
            ax.set_ylabel("Y")
            ax.set_zlabel("Z")
            ax.set_box_aspect([1.0, 1.0, 1.0])

        else:
            raise TypeError(f"Cannot draw a {self.spatial_dims}D rectangle.")

        if show:
            plt.show()

        return cast(Figure, ax.get_figure(root=True)), ax

            )

        ax.set_xlabel("X")
        ax.set_ylabel("Y")
        ax.set_zlabel("Z")
        ax.set_box_aspect([1.0, 1.0, 1.0])

    else:
        raise TypeError(f"Cannot draw a {self.spatial_dims}D rectangle.")

    if show:
        plt.show()

    return cast(Figure, ax.get_figure(root=True)), ax

def estimate_nsamples(self, value: float) -> int:
    """Return a grid count from the two edge lengths.

    Each edge contributes at least two points, from its length divided by
    ``value``. The two counts are multiplied. A time range multiplies again by its
    step count, also at least two. One instant does not.

    Args:
        value: Spacing along each edge.

    Returns:
        The sample count.

    """
    len1 = jnp.linalg.norm(self.edge1)
    len2 = jnp.linalg.norm(self.edge2)
    n_space = jnp.maximum(int(jnp.round(len1 / value)), 2) * jnp.maximum(
        int(jnp.round(len2 / value)),
        2,
    )

    if self.single_time is not None:
        # Single time instant - only spatial samples needed
        return int(n_space)
    if self.times is not None:
        # Time range - multiply by time samples
        n_time = jnp.maximum(jnp.round((self.tmax - self.tmin) / self.tstep), 2)
        return int(n_space * n_time)
    return int(n_space)

def normal(self) -> Array:
    """Return the unit normal from the cross product of the two edges.

    A stored ``_normal_override`` is returned instead when one is set. A
    two-dimensional edge is padded with a zero third coordinate before the cross
    product.

    Returns:
        The unit normal.

    """
    if self._normal_override is not None:
        return self._normal_override
    e1, e2 = _as3(self.edge1), _as3(self.edge2)
    n = jnp.cross(e1, e2)
    return n / jnp.linalg.norm(n)

def sample(
    self,
    method: SamplingMethod,
    sampling_values: float | Sequence[float | int] | None = None,
    *,
    overwrite: bool = False,
    descriptor_count: int = 32,
) -> tuple[Array, int]:
    """Store collocation points on this shape.

    ``sampling_values`` is one number. ``None`` uses ``1000``. A list is
    rejected here. [`ComplexShape.sample`][pinnjax.geometry.complex.ComplexShape.sample]
    accepts one number per child. When points are already stored and
    ``overwrite`` is false, those points are returned unchanged.

    ``descriptor_count`` is used by
    [`OperatorGeometry.sample`][pinnjax.geometry.operator.OperatorGeometry.sample] and ignored
    here.

    Args:
        method: Sampler that draws the points.
        sampling_values: One sampling size. ``None`` uses the Sampler default.
        overwrite: Replace points that were already stored.
        descriptor_count: Descriptor sample count for an operator geometry.

    Returns:
        samples: Collocation points stored on ``samples``.
        n_points: Number of those points.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``sampling_values`` is a sequence.

    """
    del descriptor_count
    if sampling_values is not None and not isinstance(sampling_values, (float, int)):
        msg = "A Shape takes one sampling value. Pass a list to ComplexShape.sample."
        config.LOGGER.error(msg)
        raise ValueError(msg)

    if not overwrite and self.samples is not None and self.n_points > 0:
        return self.samples, self.n_points

    self.samples = jnp.asarray(
        method(self, sampling_values),
        dtype=config.get_dtype(),
    )
    self.n_points = len(self.samples)

    return self.samples, self.n_points

def transform(self, unit_samples: Array) -> Array:
    """Map the first two unit coordinates along the two edges.

    A single instant is appended to every point. A time range uses the third unit
    coordinate.

    Args:
        unit_samples: Unit-cube coordinates, shaped ``(..., dims)``.

    Returns:
        Points on the parallelogram, with time appended when this rectangle has a
        time axis.

    """
    # Spatial transformation
    pt = self.origin + unit_samples[..., 0:1] * self.edge1 + unit_samples[..., 1:2] * self.edge2

    if self.single_time is not None:
        # Add constant time dimension
        t = jnp.full((*unit_samples.shape[:-1], 1), self.single_time)
        pt = jnp.concatenate([pt, t], axis=-1)
    elif self.times is not None:
        # Add time range
        t = self.tmin + unit_samples[..., 2:3] * (self.tmax - self.tmin)
        pt = jnp.concatenate([pt, t], axis=-1)

    return pt

class Box(Shape, ABC):
    """A parallelepiped spanned by three edges from ``origin``.

    Attributes:
        origin: Corner where the three edges meet.
        edge1: First edge.
        edge2: Second edge.
        edge3: Third edge.
        times: Time range, or ``None`` when the box has one instant or no time.

    """

    origin: Array
    edge1: Array
    edge2: Array
    edge3: Array
    times: Time | None

    def __init__(
        self,
        origin: tuple[float, float, float] | tuple[float, ...] | Array,
        edge1: tuple[float, float, float] | tuple[float, ...] | Array,
        edge2: tuple[float, float, float] | tuple[float, ...] | Array,
        edge3: tuple[float, float, float] | tuple[float, ...] | Array,
        times: Time | float | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Store the corner, the three edges, and the optional time.

        A float ``times`` is one instant and does not set ``times``. A
        [`Time`][pinnjax.Time] value is a range. Either one adds a time axis to ``dims``.

        Args:
            origin: Corner where the three edges meet.
            edge1: First edge.
            edge2: Second edge.
            edge3: Third edge.
            times: One instant, a time range, or no time. Default: no time.

        """
        super().__init__()
        self.origin = jnp.array(origin)
        self.edge1 = jnp.array(edge1)
        self.edge2 = jnp.array(edge2)
        self.edge3 = jnp.array(edge3)
        self.spatial_dims = self.origin.size
        self.dims = self.origin.size

        # Handle different time specifications
        if isinstance(times, (int, float)):
            # Single time instant
            self.single_time = float(times)
            self.times = None
            self.dims += 1
        elif isinstance(times, Time):
            # Time range
            self.single_time = None
            self.times = times
            self.tmin = times.min
            self.tmax = times.max
            self.tstep = times.step
            self.dims += 1
        else:
            # No time dimension
            self.single_time = None
            self.times = None

    def measure(self) -> Array:
        """Return the volume from the scalar triple product of the three edges.

        Returns:
            The absolute volume as a scalar array.

        """
        return jnp.abs(jnp.dot(self.edge1, jnp.cross(self.edge2, self.edge3)))

    def bounds(self) -> tuple[Array, Array]:
        """Return the box around the eight corners.

        A time instant or a time range is appended as the last coordinate.

        Returns:
            The lower and upper bounds.

        """
        # Compute all 8 corners, then min/max
        corners = jnp.stack(
            [
                self.origin,
                self.origin + self.edge1,
                self.origin + self.edge2,
                self.origin + self.edge3,
                self.origin + self.edge1 + self.edge2,
                self.origin + self.edge1 + self.edge3,
                self.origin + self.edge2 + self.edge3,
                self.origin + self.edge1 + self.edge2 + self.edge3,
            ],
        )
        lower = jnp.min(corners, axis=0)
        upper = jnp.max(corners, axis=0)

        if self.single_time is not None:
            # Single time point
            lower = jnp.concatenate([lower, jnp.array([self.single_time])])
            upper = jnp.concatenate([upper, jnp.array([self.single_time])])
        elif self.times is not None:
            # Time range
            lower = jnp.concatenate([lower, jnp.array([self.tmin])])
            upper = jnp.concatenate([upper, jnp.array([self.tmax])])

        return lower, upper

    def draw(
        self,
        *,
        show_normals: bool = False,
        normal_scale: float = 1.0,
        fig: Figure | None = None,
        ax: Axes | None = None,
        show: bool | None = True,
    ) -> tuple[Figure, Axes]:
        """Draw the box through the oriented-bounding-box domain.

        ``show_normals`` and ``normal_scale`` are accepted and not used.

        Args:
            show_normals: Ignored. Default: ``False``.
            normal_scale: Ignored. Default: ``1``.
            fig: Figure to draw on. Default: a figure created by the domain.
            ax: Axes to draw on. Default: axes created by the domain.
            show: Display the figure before returning it. Default: ``True``.

        Returns:
            The Matplotlib figure and axes.

        """
        domain = SpatialDomain.from_obb(
            self.origin,
            self.edge1,
            self.edge2,
            self.edge3,
            times=self.times,
        )

        fig, ax = domain.draw(show=show, fig=fig, ax=ax)

        return fig, ax

    def transform(self, unit_samples: Array) -> Array:
        """Map the first three unit coordinates along the three edges.

        A single instant is appended to every point. A time range uses the fourth unit
        coordinate.

        Args:
            unit_samples: Unit-cube coordinates, shaped ``(..., dims)``.

        Returns:
            Points in the parallelepiped, with time appended when this box has a time axis.

        """
        # Spatial transformation
        pt = (
            self.origin
            + unit_samples[..., 0:1] * self.edge1
            + unit_samples[..., 1:2] * self.edge2
            + unit_samples[..., 2:3] * self.edge3
        )

        if self.single_time is not None:
            # Add constant time dimension
            t = jnp.full((*unit_samples.shape[:-1], 1), self.single_time)
            pt = jnp.concatenate([pt, t], axis=-1)
        elif self.times is not None:
            # Add time range
            t = self.tmin + unit_samples[..., 3:4] * (self.tmax - self.tmin)
            pt = jnp.concatenate([pt, t], axis=-1)

        return pt

    def estimate_nsamples(self, value: float) -> int:
        """Return a grid count from the three edge lengths.

        Each edge contributes at least two points, from its length divided by
        ``value``. The three counts are multiplied. A time range multiplies again by
        its step count, also at least two. One instant does not.

        Args:
            value: Spacing along each edge.

        Returns:
            The sample count.

        """
        len1, len2, len3 = (
            jnp.linalg.norm(self.edge1),
            jnp.linalg.norm(self.edge2),
            jnp.linalg.norm(self.edge3),
        )
        n_space = (
            jnp.maximum(jnp.round(len1 / value), 2)
            * jnp.maximum(jnp.round(len2 / value), 2)
            * jnp.maximum(jnp.round(len3 / value), 2)
        )

        if self.single_time is not None:
            # Single time instant - only spatial samples needed
            return int(n_space)
        if self.times is not None:
            # Time range - multiply by time samples
            n_time = jnp.maximum(jnp.round((self.tmax - self.tmin) / self.tstep), 2)
            return int(n_space * n_time)
        return int(n_space)

    def grid_shape(self, value: float) -> tuple[int, ...]:  # noqa: D102
        n1 = max(int(jnp.round(jnp.linalg.norm(self.edge1) / value)), 2)
        n2 = max(int(jnp.round(jnp.linalg.norm(self.edge2) / value)), 2)
        n3 = max(int(jnp.round(jnp.linalg.norm(self.edge3) / value)), 2)

        if self.times is not None:
            n_time = max(int(jnp.round((self.tmax - self.tmin) / self.tstep)), 2)
            return n1, n2, n3, n_time

        return n1, n2, n3

    *,
    show_normals: bool = False,
    normal_scale: float = 1.0,
    fig: Figure | None = None,
    ax: Axes | None = None,
    show: bool | None = True,
) -> tuple[Figure, Axes]:
    """Draw the box through the oriented-bounding-box domain.

    ``show_normals`` and ``normal_scale`` are accepted and not used.

    Args:
        show_normals: Ignored. Default: ``False``.
        normal_scale: Ignored. Default: ``1``.
        fig: Figure to draw on. Default: a figure created by the domain.
        ax: Axes to draw on. Default: axes created by the domain.
        show: Display the figure before returning it. Default: ``True``.

    Returns:
        The Matplotlib figure and axes.

    """
    domain = SpatialDomain.from_obb(
        self.origin,
        self.edge1,
        self.edge2,
        self.edge3,
        times=self.times,
    )

    fig, ax = domain.draw(show=show, fig=fig, ax=ax)

    return fig, ax

def estimate_nsamples(self, value: float) -> int:
    """Return a grid count from the three edge lengths.

    Each edge contributes at least two points, from its length divided by
    ``value``. The three counts are multiplied. A time range multiplies again by
    its step count, also at least two. One instant does not.

    Args:
        value: Spacing along each edge.

    Returns:
        The sample count.

    """
    len1, len2, len3 = (
        jnp.linalg.norm(self.edge1),
        jnp.linalg.norm(self.edge2),
        jnp.linalg.norm(self.edge3),
    )
    n_space = (
        jnp.maximum(jnp.round(len1 / value), 2)
        * jnp.maximum(jnp.round(len2 / value), 2)
        * jnp.maximum(jnp.round(len3 / value), 2)
    )

    if self.single_time is not None:
        # Single time instant - only spatial samples needed
        return int(n_space)
    if self.times is not None:
        # Time range - multiply by time samples
        n_time = jnp.maximum(jnp.round((self.tmax - self.tmin) / self.tstep), 2)
        return int(n_space * n_time)
    return int(n_space)

def sample(
    self,
    method: SamplingMethod,
    sampling_values: float | Sequence[float | int] | None = None,
    *,
    overwrite: bool = False,
    descriptor_count: int = 32,
) -> tuple[Array, int]:
    """Store collocation points on this shape.

    ``sampling_values`` is one number. ``None`` uses ``1000``. A list is
    rejected here. [`ComplexShape.sample`][pinnjax.geometry.complex.ComplexShape.sample]
    accepts one number per child. When points are already stored and
    ``overwrite`` is false, those points are returned unchanged.

    ``descriptor_count`` is used by
    [`OperatorGeometry.sample`][pinnjax.geometry.operator.OperatorGeometry.sample] and ignored
    here.

    Args:
        method: Sampler that draws the points.
        sampling_values: One sampling size. ``None`` uses the Sampler default.
        overwrite: Replace points that were already stored.
        descriptor_count: Descriptor sample count for an operator geometry.

    Returns:
        samples: Collocation points stored on ``samples``.
        n_points: Number of those points.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``sampling_values`` is a sequence.

    """
    del descriptor_count
    if sampling_values is not None and not isinstance(sampling_values, (float, int)):
        msg = "A Shape takes one sampling value. Pass a list to ComplexShape.sample."
        config.LOGGER.error(msg)
        raise ValueError(msg)

    if not overwrite and self.samples is not None and self.n_points > 0:
        return self.samples, self.n_points

    self.samples = jnp.asarray(
        method(self, sampling_values),
        dtype=config.get_dtype(),
    )
    self.n_points = len(self.samples)

    return self.samples, self.n_points
