def transform(self, unit_samples: Array) -> Array:
    """Map the first three unit coordinates along the three edges.

    A single instant is appended to every point. A time range uses the fourth unit
    coordinate.

    Args:
        unit_samples: Unit-cube coordinates, shaped ``(..., dims)``.

    Returns:
        Points in the parallelepiped, with time appended when this box has a time axis.

    """
    # Spatial transformation
    pt = (
        self.origin
        + unit_samples[..., 0:1] * self.edge1
        + unit_samples[..., 1:2] * self.edge2
        + unit_samples[..., 2:3] * self.edge3
    )

    if self.single_time is not None:
        # Add constant time dimension
        t = jnp.full((*unit_samples.shape[:-1], 1), self.single_time)
        pt = jnp.concatenate([pt, t], axis=-1)
    elif self.times is not None:
        # Add time range
        t = self.tmin + unit_samples[..., 3:4] * (self.tmax - self.tmin)
        pt = jnp.concatenate([pt, t], axis=-1)

    return pt

class Hypercube(Shape):
    """A box in parameter space, sampled through one marginal per axis.

    ``lower`` and ``upper`` are the bounds used for the domain, the measure, and
    the default uniform marginals. A marginal maps the unit interval to that axis
    during ``transform``. There is no time axis.

    Attributes:
        lower: Lower bound of each axis.
        upper: Upper bound of each axis.
        axis_names: Name of each axis. Default names are ``mu0``, ``mu1``, and so on.
        marginals: Distribution used to map each unit-interval coordinate.
        evaluator: Callable run on the samples after ``sample``, or ``None``.
        evaluated_values: Array returned by the last ``evaluate`` call that stored
            its result, or ``None``.

    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        lower: tuple[float, ...] | list[float] | Array,
        upper: tuple[float, ...] | list[float] | Array,
        *,
        axis_names: tuple[str, ...] | None = None,
        marginals: tuple[MarginalSpec, ...] | None = None,
        evaluator: Callable | Sequence[Callable] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Store the bounds and one marginal per axis.

        Omitted marginals are uniform on each ``[lower, upper]`` interval. Omitted
        axis names are ``mu0``, ``mu1``, and so on.

        Args:
            lower: Lower bound of each axis.
            upper: Upper bound of each axis. Each entry must be strictly greater than
                the matching entry of ``lower``.
            axis_names: One name per axis. Default: ``mu0``, ``mu1``, and so on.
            marginals: One marginal per axis. Default: a uniform distribution on each
                bound interval.
            evaluator: Callable, or a sequence of callables, applied to the samples at
                the end of ``sample``. Default: ``None``.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If the bounds differ in length, an upper bound is not strictly
                greater than the matching lower bound, or a name or marginal sequence
                does not have one entry per axis.

        """
        super().__init__()

        self.lower = jnp.asarray(lower, dtype=config.get_dtype())
        self.upper = jnp.asarray(upper, dtype=config.get_dtype())
        self.evaluator = evaluator
        self.evaluated_values = None

        if self.lower.shape != self.upper.shape:
            raise ValueError(
                f"lower and upper must have the same length, "
                f"got {self.lower.shape} and {self.upper.shape}.",
            )

        if jnp.any(self.upper <= self.lower):
            raise ValueError("Each upper bound must be strictly greater than lower.")

        k = int(self.lower.shape[0])
        self.spatial_dims = k
        self.dims = k
        self.times = None

        if axis_names is None:
            self.axis_names = tuple(f"mu{i}" for i in range(k))
        else:
            if len(axis_names) != k:
                raise ValueError(f"axis_names length must be {k}")
            self.axis_names = tuple(axis_names)

        if marginals is None:
            self.marginals = tuple(
                _uniform_on_interval(
                    (float(self.lower[i]), float(self.upper[i])),
                )
                for i in range(k)
            )
        else:
            if len(marginals) != k:
                raise ValueError(f"marginals length must be {k}, got {len(marginals)}")
            self.marginals = tuple(marginals)

    def draw(
        self,
        *,
        show_normals: bool = False,
        normal_scale: float = 1.0,
        fig: Figure | None = None,
        ax: Axes | None = None,
        show: bool = True,
    ) -> tuple[Figure, Axes]:
        """Draw the hypercube when it has at most three dimensions.

        Args:
            show_normals: Ignored.
            normal_scale: Ignored.
            fig: Figure to draw on. A new figure is created when omitted.
            ax: Existing axes. New axes are created when omitted.
            show: Display the figure before returning it. Default: ``True``.

        Returns:
            The Matplotlib figure and axes.

        Raises:
            TypeError: If the supplied axes does not match the hypercube dimension.

        """
        del show_normals, normal_scale

        if self.dims > THREE_DIMENSIONAL:
            config.LOGGER.warning(
                f"Cannot draw a {self.dims}D Hypercube. Only up to 3D is supported.",
            )
            if ax is None:
                if fig is None:
                    fig = plt.figure()
                ax = fig.add_subplot(111)

            return cast(Figure, ax.get_figure(root=True)), ax

        if self.dims == 1:
            if ax is None:
                if fig is None:
                    fig = plt.figure()
                ax = fig.add_subplot(111)
            elif isinstance(ax, Axes3D):
                raise TypeError("A 1D Hypercube requires a 2D axes.")

            ax.plot(
                [self.lower[0], self.upper[0]],
                [0.0, 0.0],
                color="black",
                marker="o",
            )
            ax.set_xlabel(self.axis_names[0])
            ax.set_yticks([])

        elif self.dims == TWO_DIMENSIONAL:
            if ax is None:
                if fig is None:
                    fig = plt.figure()
                ax = fig.add_subplot(111)
            elif isinstance(ax, Axes3D):
                raise TypeError("A 2D Hypercube requires a 2D axes.")

            x0, y0 = self.lower
            x1, y1 = self.upper
            x = jnp.array([x0, x1, x1, x0, x0])
            y = jnp.array([y0, y0, y1, y1, y0])

            ax.plot(x, y, color="black", marker="o")
            ax.set_xlabel(self.axis_names[0])
            ax.set_ylabel(self.axis_names[1])
            ax.set_aspect("equal", adjustable="box")

        elif self.dims == THREE_DIMENSIONAL:
            if ax is None:
                if fig is None:
                    fig = plt.figure()
                ax = fig.add_subplot(111, projection="3d")

            if not isinstance(ax, Axes3D):
                raise TypeError("A 3D Hypercube requires a 3D axes.")

            x0, y0, z0 = self.lower
            x1, y1, z1 = self.upper

            vertices = jnp.array(
                [
                    [x0, y0, z0],
                    [x1, y0, z0],
                    [x1, y1, z0],
                    [x0, y1, z0],
                    [x0, y0, z1],
                    [x1, y0, z1],
                    [x1, y1, z1],
                    [x0, y1, z1],
                ],
            )

            edges = (
                (0, 1),
                (1, 2),
                (2, 3),
                (3, 0),
                (4, 5),
                (5, 6),
                (6, 7),
                (7, 4),
                (0, 4),
                (1, 5),
                (2, 6),
                (3, 7),
            )

            for i, j in edges:
                edge = vertices[jnp.array([i, j])]
                ax.plot(edge[:, 0], edge[:, 1], edge[:, 2], color="black")

            ax.set_xlabel(self.axis_names[0])
            ax.set_ylabel(self.axis_names[1])
            ax.set_zlabel(self.axis_names[2])
            ax.set_box_aspect([1.0, 1.0, 1.0])

        if show:
            plt.show()

        assert ax is not None
        return cast(Figure, ax.get_figure(root=True)), ax

    @property
    def domain(self) -> Domain:
        """Return the bounds and axis names as a [`Domain`][pinnjax.Domain]."""
        return Domain(
            min=tuple(float(x) for x in self.lower.tolist()),
            max=tuple(float(x) for x in self.upper.tolist()),
            axis_names=self.axis_names,
        )

    def bounds(self) -> tuple[Array, Array]:
        """Return the lower and upper bounds."""
        return self.lower, self.upper

    def transform(self, unit_samples: Array) -> Array:
        """Map unit-cube coordinates onto the marginal for each axis.

        The last axis of ``unit_samples`` is one coordinate per dimension, in ``[0, 1]``.
        An interval marginal maps that coordinate linearly onto its interval. A discrete
        marginal picks a value by cutting ``[0, 1]`` into equal bins. A continuous
        marginal uses its percent-point function.

        Args:
            unit_samples: Coordinates in the unit cube, shaped ``(..., dims)``.

        Returns:
            Points in parameter space, with the same shape as ``unit_samples``.

        """
        u = jnp.asarray(unit_samples, dtype=config.get_dtype())
        u_np = np.asarray(u)

        cols = [_transform_axis(u_np[..., i], self.marginals[i]) for i in range(self.dims)]
        return jnp.asarray(np.stack(cols, axis=-1), dtype=config.get_dtype())

    def measure(self) -> Array:
        """Return the volume of the bounding box.

        This is the product of ``upper - lower``. It does not depend on the marginals.

        Returns:
            The volume as a scalar array.

        """
        return jnp.prod(self.upper - self.lower)

    def estimate_nsamples(self, value: float) -> int:
        """Return how many points a uniform grid at this spacing would contain.

        Each axis uses at least two points. The count on an axis is the edge length
        divided by ``value``, rounded, and the counts are multiplied.

        Args:
            value: Spacing between grid points, in the same units as the bounds.

        Returns:
            The product of the per-axis counts.

        """
        edges = self.upper - self.lower
        per_axis = jnp.maximum(jnp.round(edges / value), 2)
        return int(jnp.prod(per_axis))

    def grid_shape(self, value: float) -> tuple[int, ...]:  # noqa: D102
        edges = self.upper - self.lower
        return tuple(max(int(jnp.round(edge / value)), 2) for edge in edges)

    def sample(
        self,
        method: SamplingMethod,
        sampling_values: float | Sequence[float | int] | None = None,
        *,
        overwrite: bool = False,
        descriptor_count: int = 32,
    ) -> tuple[Array, int]:
        """Draw collocation points, then run ``evaluator`` when one was stored.

        Sampling follows [`Shape.sample`][pinnjax.geometry.base.Shape.sample]. A stored evaluator
        is then applied with ``overwrite=True``, which replaces ``evaluated_values``.
        ``descriptor_count`` is ignored.

        Args:
            method: Sampler used to draw the points.
            sampling_values: Size passed to ``method``. ``None`` uses ``1000``.
            overwrite: Replace points that were already stored.
            descriptor_count: Descriptor sample count for an operator geometry.

        Returns:
            samples: Collocation points stored on this shape.
            n_points: Number of those points.

        """
        del descriptor_count
        self.samples, self.n_points = super().sample(
            method,
            sampling_values,
            overwrite=overwrite,
        )

        if self.evaluator is not None:
            self.evaluated_values = self.evaluate(self.evaluator, overwrite=True)

        return self.samples, self.n_points

    def evaluate(
        self,
        evaluator: SampleEvaluator | Sequence[SampleEvaluator],
        *,
        overwrite: bool = False,
    ) -> Array:
        """Apply one or more callables to the stored samples.

        Each callable is mapped over the sample rows. One callable returns that array.
        Several callables are stacked on a new leading axis. ``overwrite`` stores the
        result on ``evaluated_values``.

        Args:
            evaluator: One callable, or a sequence of callables. Each callable takes one
                sample row and returns an array.
            overwrite: Replace ``evaluated_values`` with the result. Default: ``False``.

        Returns:
            The mapped values, or a stack of those values when more than one callable
            was given.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If ``sample`` has not been called, or the sequence is empty.
            TypeError: If an entry in the sequence is not callable.

        """
        samples = self.samples
        if samples is None:
            raise ValueError("Shape must first be sampled prior to evaluation.")

        if isinstance(evaluator, Sequence):
            evaluators = tuple(evaluator)
        else:
            evaluators = (evaluator,)

        if len(evaluators) == 0:
            raise ValueError("evaluator sequence must contain at least one callable.")

        if not all(callable(fn) for fn in evaluators):
            raise TypeError("All evaluators must be callable.")
        values = [jnp.asarray(jax.vmap(fn)(samples), dtype=config.get_dtype()) for fn in evaluators]

        if len(values) == 1:
            out = values[0]
        else:
            out = jnp.stack(values, axis=0)

        if overwrite:
            self.evaluated_values = out
        return out

    @classmethod
    def from_domain(
        cls,
        domain: Domain,
        evaluator: Callable | Sequence[Callable] | None = None,
        **kwargs,
    ) -> Hypercube:
        """Build a hypercube from the minimum, maximum, and axis names of a domain.

        Args:
            domain: Domain that supplies the bounds and axis names.
            evaluator: Callable, or a sequence of callables, stored for ``sample``.
                Default: ``None``.
            **kwargs: Forwarded to [`Hypercube`][pinnjax.Hypercube]. Use this for ``marginals``.

        Returns:
            A hypercube with those bounds and names.

        """
        return cls(
            lower=jnp.asarray(domain.min),
            upper=jnp.asarray(domain.max),
            axis_names=domain.axis_names,
            evaluator=evaluator,
            **kwargs,
        )

    @classmethod
    def from_intervals(
        cls,
        *intervals: tuple[float, float],
        axis_names: Sequence[str] | None = None,
        evaluator: Callable | Sequence[Callable] | None = None,
    ) -> Hypercube:
        """Build a hypercube with a uniform marginal on each interval.

        Each pair is ``(lower, upper)``. The upper value must be strictly greater than
        the lower value.

        Args:
            *intervals: One ``(lower, upper)`` pair per axis.
            axis_names: One name per axis. Default: ``mu0``, ``mu1``, and so on.
            evaluator: Callable, or a sequence of callables, stored for ``sample``.
                Default: ``None``.

        Returns:
            A hypercube whose bounds are those intervals.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If an interval is empty or reversed, or ``axis_names`` does not
                have one entry per interval.

        """
        specs = [_uniform_on_interval(iv) for iv in intervals]
        return cls.from_distributions(
            *specs,
            axis_names=axis_names,
            evaluator=evaluator,
        )

    @classmethod
    def from_distributions(
        cls,
        *specs: MarginalSpec,
        confidence: float = 0.99,
        axis_names: Sequence[str] | None = None,
        evaluator: Callable | Sequence[Callable] | None = None,
    ) -> Hypercube:
        """Build a hypercube whose bounds come from one marginal per axis.

        An interval marginal uses its own endpoints. A discrete marginal uses the
        smallest and largest value. A continuous marginal uses its support when that
        support is finite. Otherwise, the bounds are the central ``confidence``
        probability interval.

        Args:
            *specs: One marginal per axis.
            confidence: Central probability used when a continuous support is infinite.
                Default: ``0.99``.
            axis_names: One name per axis. Default: ``mu0``, ``mu1``, and so on.
            evaluator: Callable, or a sequence of callables, stored for ``sample``.
                Default: ``None``.

        Returns:
            A hypercube with those marginals and the derived bounds.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If a derived upper bound is not strictly greater than the lower
                bound, or ``axis_names`` does not have one entry per marginal.
            TypeError: If a specification is not an interval, discrete, or continuous
                marginal.

        """
        lowers, uppers, marginals = [], [], []

        for spec in specs:
            lo, hi, marginal = _bounds_from_spec(spec, confidence)
            lowers.append(lo)
            uppers.append(hi)
            marginals.append(marginal)

        return cls(
            lower=jnp.asarray(lowers),
            upper=jnp.asarray(uppers),
            axis_names=tuple(axis_names) if axis_names else None,
            marginals=tuple(marginals),
            evaluator=evaluator,
        )

def __init__(
    self,
    lower: tuple[float, ...] | list[float] | Array,
    upper: tuple[float, ...] | list[float] | Array,
    *,
    axis_names: tuple[str, ...] | None = None,
    marginals: tuple[MarginalSpec, ...] | None = None,
    evaluator: Callable | Sequence[Callable] | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Store the bounds and one marginal per axis.

    Omitted marginals are uniform on each ``[lower, upper]`` interval. Omitted
    axis names are ``mu0``, ``mu1``, and so on.

    Args:
        lower: Lower bound of each axis.
        upper: Upper bound of each axis. Each entry must be strictly greater than
            the matching entry of ``lower``.
        axis_names: One name per axis. Default: ``mu0``, ``mu1``, and so on.
        marginals: One marginal per axis. Default: a uniform distribution on each
            bound interval.
        evaluator: Callable, or a sequence of callables, applied to the samples at
            the end of ``sample``. Default: ``None``.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the bounds differ in length, an upper bound is not strictly
            greater than the matching lower bound, or a name or marginal sequence
            does not have one entry per axis.

    """
    super().__init__()

    self.lower = jnp.asarray(lower, dtype=config.get_dtype())
    self.upper = jnp.asarray(upper, dtype=config.get_dtype())
    self.evaluator = evaluator
    self.evaluated_values = None

    if self.lower.shape != self.upper.shape:
        raise ValueError(
            f"lower and upper must have the same length, "
            f"got {self.lower.shape} and {self.upper.shape}.",
        )

    if jnp.any(self.upper <= self.lower):
        raise ValueError("Each upper bound must be strictly greater than lower.")

    k = int(self.lower.shape[0])
    self.spatial_dims = k
    self.dims = k
    self.times = None

    if axis_names is None:
        self.axis_names = tuple(f"mu{i}" for i in range(k))
    else:
        if len(axis_names) != k:
            raise ValueError(f"axis_names length must be {k}")
        self.axis_names = tuple(axis_names)

    if marginals is None:
        self.marginals = tuple(
            _uniform_on_interval(
                (float(self.lower[i]), float(self.upper[i])),
            )
            for i in range(k)
        )
    else:
        if len(marginals) != k:
            raise ValueError(f"marginals length must be {k}, got {len(marginals)}")
        self.marginals = tuple(marginals)

def draw(
    self,
    *,
    show_normals: bool = False,
    normal_scale: float = 1.0,
    fig: Figure | None = None,
    ax: Axes | None = None,
    show: bool = True,
) -> tuple[Figure, Axes]:
    """Draw the hypercube when it has at most three dimensions.

    Args:
        show_normals: Ignored.
        normal_scale: Ignored.
        fig: Figure to draw on. A new figure is created when omitted.
        ax: Existing axes. New axes are created when omitted.
        show: Display the figure before returning it. Default: ``True``.

    Returns:
        The Matplotlib figure and axes.

    Raises:
        TypeError: If the supplied axes does not match the hypercube dimension.

    """
    del show_normals, normal_scale

    if self.dims > THREE_DIMENSIONAL:
        config.LOGGER.warning(
            f"Cannot draw a {self.dims}D Hypercube. Only up to 3D is supported.",
        )
        if ax is None:
            if fig is None:
                fig = plt.figure()
            ax = fig.add_subplot(111)

        return cast(Figure, ax.get_figure(root=True)), ax

    if self.dims == 1:
        if ax is None:
            if fig is None:
                fig = plt.figure()
            ax = fig.add_subplot(111)
        elif isinstance(ax, Axes3D):
            raise TypeError("A 1D Hypercube requires a 2D axes.")

        ax.plot(
            [self.lower[0], self.upper[0]],
            [0.0, 0.0],
            color="black",
            marker="o",
        )
        ax.set_xlabel(self.axis_names[0])
        ax.set_yticks([])

    elif self.dims == TWO_DIMENSIONAL:
        if ax is None:
            if fig is None:
                fig = plt.figure()
            ax = fig.add_subplot(111)
        elif isinstance(ax, Axes3D):
            raise TypeError("A 2D Hypercube requires a 2D axes.")

        x0, y0 = self.lower
        x1, y1 = self.upper
        x = jnp.array([x0, x1, x1, x0, x0])
        y = jnp.array([y0, y0, y1, y1, y0])

        ax.plot(x, y, color="black", marker="o")
        ax.set_xlabel(self.axis_names[0])
        ax.set_ylabel(self.axis_names[1])
        ax.set_aspect("equal", adjustable="box")

    elif self.dims == THREE_DIMENSIONAL:
        if ax is None:
            if fig is None:
                fig = plt.figure()
            ax = fig.add_subplot(111, projection="3d")

        if not isinstance(ax, Axes3D):
            raise TypeError("A 3D Hypercube requires a 3D axes.")

        x0, y0, z0 = self.lower
        x1, y1, z1 = self.upper

        vertices = jnp.array(
            [
                [x0, y0, z0],
                [x1, y0, z0],
                [x1, y1, z0],
                [x0, y1, z0],
                [x0, y0, z1],
                [x1, y0, z1],
                [x1, y1, z1],
                [x0, y1, z1],
            ],
        )

        edges = (
            (0, 1),
            (1, 2),
            (2, 3),
            (3, 0),
            (4, 5),
            (5, 6),
            (6, 7),
            (7, 4),
            (0, 4),
            (1, 5),
            (2, 6),
            (3, 7),
        )

        for i, j in edges:
            edge = vertices[jnp.array([i, j])]
            ax.plot(edge[:, 0], edge[:, 1], edge[:, 2], color="black")

        ax.set_xlabel(self.axis_names[0])
        ax.set_ylabel(self.axis_names[1])
        ax.set_zlabel(self.axis_names[2])
        ax.set_box_aspect([1.0, 1.0, 1.0])

    if show:
        plt.show()

    assert ax is not None
    return cast(Figure, ax.get_figure(root=True)), ax

def estimate_nsamples(self, value: float) -> int:
    """Return how many points a uniform grid at this spacing would contain.

    Each axis uses at least two points. The count on an axis is the edge length
    divided by ``value``, rounded, and the counts are multiplied.

    Args:
        value: Spacing between grid points, in the same units as the bounds.

    Returns:
        The product of the per-axis counts.

    """
    edges = self.upper - self.lower
    per_axis = jnp.maximum(jnp.round(edges / value), 2)
    return int(jnp.prod(per_axis))

def evaluate(
    self,
    evaluator: SampleEvaluator | Sequence[SampleEvaluator],
    *,
    overwrite: bool = False,
) -> Array:
    """Apply one or more callables to the stored samples.

    Each callable is mapped over the sample rows. One callable returns that array.
    Several callables are stacked on a new leading axis. ``overwrite`` stores the
    result on ``evaluated_values``.

    Args:
        evaluator: One callable, or a sequence of callables. Each callable takes one
            sample row and returns an array.
        overwrite: Replace ``evaluated_values`` with the result. Default: ``False``.

    Returns:
        The mapped values, or a stack of those values when more than one callable
        was given.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``sample`` has not been called, or the sequence is empty.
        TypeError: If an entry in the sequence is not callable.

    """
    samples = self.samples
    if samples is None:
        raise ValueError("Shape must first be sampled prior to evaluation.")

    if isinstance(evaluator, Sequence):
        evaluators = tuple(evaluator)
    else:
        evaluators = (evaluator,)

    if len(evaluators) == 0:
        raise ValueError("evaluator sequence must contain at least one callable.")

    if not all(callable(fn) for fn in evaluators):
        raise TypeError("All evaluators must be callable.")
    values = [jnp.asarray(jax.vmap(fn)(samples), dtype=config.get_dtype()) for fn in evaluators]

    if len(values) == 1:
        out = values[0]
    else:
        out = jnp.stack(values, axis=0)

    if overwrite:
        self.evaluated_values = out
    return out

def loss(self, residuals: Array) -> Array:
    """Calculate the loss for all collocation points.

    Evaluation uses the bound [`pinnjax.Loss`][pinnjax.Loss].

    Args:
        residuals: Array of residual values for each collocation point.

    Returns:
        The loss for ``residuals``.

    Raises:
        InputError: If no [`pinnjax.Loss`][pinnjax.Loss] has been bound
            to this Shape.

    """
    loss_function = self.loss_function
    if loss_function is None:
        msg = "There is no loss function associated with this shape. Call .set_loss first."
        config.LOGGER.error(msg)
        raise config.InputError(msg)

    self.loss_val = loss_function(residuals)
    return self.loss_val

def residuals(self, ops: DifferentialOperators) -> Array:
    """Calculate the residual values for all collocation points.

def sample(
    self,
    method: SamplingMethod,
    sampling_values: float | Sequence[float | int] | None = None,
    *,
    overwrite: bool = False,
    descriptor_count: int = 32,
) -> tuple[Array, int]:
    """Draw collocation points, then run ``evaluator`` when one was stored.

    Sampling follows [`Shape.sample`][pinnjax.geometry.base.Shape.sample]. A stored evaluator
    is then applied with ``overwrite=True``, which replaces ``evaluated_values``.
    ``descriptor_count`` is ignored.

    Args:
        method: Sampler used to draw the points.
        sampling_values: Size passed to ``method``. ``None`` uses ``1000``.
        overwrite: Replace points that were already stored.
        descriptor_count: Descriptor sample count for an operator geometry.

    Returns:
        samples: Collocation points stored on this shape.
        n_points: Number of those points.

    """
    del descriptor_count
    self.samples, self.n_points = super().sample(
        method,
        sampling_values,
        overwrite=overwrite,
    )

    if self.evaluator is not None:
        self.evaluated_values = self.evaluate(self.evaluator, overwrite=True)

    return self.samples, self.n_points

def transform(self, unit_samples: Array) -> Array:
    """Map unit-cube coordinates onto the marginal for each axis.

    The last axis of ``unit_samples`` is one coordinate per dimension, in ``[0, 1]``.
    An interval marginal maps that coordinate linearly onto its interval. A discrete
    marginal picks a value by cutting ``[0, 1]`` into equal bins. A continuous
    marginal uses its percent-point function.

    Args:
        unit_samples: Coordinates in the unit cube, shaped ``(..., dims)``.

    Returns:
        Points in parameter space, with the same shape as ``unit_samples``.

    """
    u = jnp.asarray(unit_samples, dtype=config.get_dtype())
    u_np = np.asarray(u)

    cols = [_transform_axis(u_np[..., i], self.marginals[i]) for i in range(self.dims)]
    return jnp.asarray(np.stack(cols, axis=-1), dtype=config.get_dtype())

class SpatialGrid(Grid):
    """A prediction grid on a [`SpatialDomain`][pinnjax.SpatialDomain].

    Subclasses fill ``coordinates``. A time range is optional and is stored
    separately until ``_setup_temporal`` appends it.

    Attributes:
        AXIS_TO_IDX: ``"x"``, ``"y"``, and ``"z"`` mapped to ``0``, ``1``, and ``2``.
        domain: Spatial bounds this grid samples.
        spatial_dimensions: Number of spatial axes.
        has_time: Whether a time axis has been added. Default: ``False``.
        times: Sampled time values, once a time range is set.
        coordinates: Spatial coordinates. The last axis is one entry per spatial axis.
        spatiotemporal_coordinates: ``coordinates`` repeated over time, with time
            appended as the last coordinate.
        periodic: Drop the endpoint of each free axis when sampling. Default: ``False``.

    """

    AXIS_TO_IDX: ClassVar[Mapping[str, int]] = AXIS_TO_IDX

    domain: SpatialDomain
    spatial_dimensions: int
    has_time: bool = False
    times: Array
    coordinates: Array
    spatiotemporal_coordinates: Array
    periodic: bool = False

    def _build_spatiotemporal_coordinates(self) -> None:
        """Append a time coordinate to the spatial coordinates.

        The result has shape ``(num_times, *spatial_shape[:-1], spatial_dimensions + 1)``.

        Raises:
            pinnjax.InputError: If this grid has no time samples.

        """
        if not self.has_time or self.times is None:
            msg = "Cannot build spatiotemporal coordinates without time configuration"
            config.LOGGER.error(msg)
            raise config.InputError(msg)

        spatial_shape = self.coordinates.shape  # e.g., (200, 300, 3) for 2D grid

        # Create time mesh: broadcast times to match spatial dimensions
        # Add singleton dimensions for all spatial dims, then broadcast
        time_shape = (self.num_times,) + (1,) * (len(spatial_shape) - 1) + (1,)
        times_mesh = jnp.broadcast_to(
            self.times.reshape(time_shape),
            (self.num_times, *spatial_shape[:-1], 1),
        )

        # Create spatial mesh
        spatial_mesh = jnp.broadcast_to(
            self.coordinates[None, ...],
            (self.num_times, *spatial_shape),
        )

        # Concatenate: [...spatial_dims, time]
        self.spatiotemporal_coordinates = jnp.concatenate(
            [spatial_mesh, times_mesh],
            axis=-1,
        )

    def _setup_temporal(self, time_range: tuple[float, float], num_times: int) -> None:
        """Store a time range and build the spatiotemporal coordinates.

        ``times`` is ``num_times`` values from the start of the range through the end.

        Args:
            time_range: First and last time.
            num_times: Number of time samples, including both ends.

        """
        self.has_time = True
        self.time_range = time_range
        self.num_times = num_times
        self.times = jnp.linspace(time_range[0], time_range[1], num_times)
        self._build_spatiotemporal_coordinates()

    def _get_free_axes(
        self,
        fixed_coordinates: dict[str, float],
        expected_count: int,
    ) -> list[str]:
        """Return the spatial axes that are not fixed.

        Axes are taken from ``"x"``, ``"y"``, and ``"z"`` up to ``spatial_dimensions``.

        Args:
            fixed_coordinates: Axis name to the value held constant.
            expected_count: How many axes must remain free.

        Returns:
            The free axis names, in ``x``, ``y``, ``z`` order.

        Raises:
            pinnjax.InputError: If the number of free axes is not ``expected_count``.

        """
        coord_names = ["x", "y", "z"][: self.spatial_dimensions]
        free_axes = [ax for ax in coord_names if ax not in fixed_coordinates]

        if len(free_axes) != expected_count:
            msg = f"Need exactly {expected_count} free axes, got {len(free_axes)}: {free_axes}"
            config.LOGGER.error(msg)
            raise config.InputError(msg)
        return free_axes

    def _build_coordinates(
        self,
        free_axes: list[str],
        fixed_coordinates: dict[str, float],
        num_points: tuple[int, ...],
    ) -> Array:
        """Sample the free axes and fill the fixed axes with constants.

        Each free axis is a linspace from the domain minimum to the domain maximum.
        ``periodic`` drops the endpoint. One free axis stays a single range. Several
        free axes become a mesh with ``xy`` indexing.

        Args:
            free_axes: Axis names to sample, in the order of ``num_points``.
            fixed_coordinates: Axis name to the constant value.
            num_points: Sample count for each free axis, in the same order as ``free_axes``.

        Returns:
            Coordinates with the spatial axes stacked on the last dimension.

        """
        # Create ranges for free axes
        ranges = []
        for i, axis in enumerate(free_axes):
            idx = self.AXIS_TO_IDX[axis]
            ranges.append(
                jnp.linspace(
                    self.domain.min[idx],
                    self.domain.max[idx],
                    num_points[i],
                    endpoint=not self.periodic,
                ),
            )

        # Create meshgrid for free axes
        mesh = [ranges[0]] if len(ranges) == 1 else jnp.meshgrid(*ranges, indexing="xy")

        # Build full coordinate array
        coordinates = []
        for axis in ["x", "y", "z"][: self.spatial_dimensions]:
            if axis in fixed_coordinates:
                fixed_val = fixed_coordinates[axis]
                coordinates.append(jnp.full_like(mesh[0], fixed_val))
            else:
                axis_idx = free_axes.index(axis)
                coordinates.append(mesh[axis_idx])

        return jnp.stack(coordinates, axis=-1)

    def slice(
        self,
        fixed_coordinates: dict[str, float] | None = None,
        *,
        atol: float = 1e-9,
    ) -> SpatialComparisonGrid:
        """Return the grid points that sit on the requested fixed coordinates.

        The spatial coordinates are flattened to one row per point. With no fixed
        coordinates, every row is kept and the grid's own ``fixed_coordinates`` are
        passed through when that attribute exists. Each requested axis must be within
        ``atol`` of the given value. The comparison does not use a relative tolerance.

        Args:
            fixed_coordinates: Axis name to the value that row must match. Default: no
                constraint.
            atol: Absolute tolerance for each comparison. Default: ``1e-9``.

        Returns:
            A [`SpatialComparisonGrid`][pinnjax.SpatialComparisonGrid] of the matching rows.

        Raises:
            pinnjax.InputError: If an axis name is outside this grid's spatial axes.
            ValueError: If no row matches.

        """
        from .comparison import SpatialComparisonGrid

        fixed_coordinates = fixed_coordinates or {}

        coords_flat = self.coordinates.reshape(-1, self.spatial_dimensions)

        if not fixed_coordinates:
            return SpatialComparisonGrid(
                domain=self.domain,
                coords=coords_flat,
                fixed_coordinates=getattr(self, "fixed_coordinates", None),
            )

        valid_axes = set(["x", "y", "z"][: self.spatial_dimensions])
        bad = [k for k in fixed_coordinates if k not in valid_axes]
        if bad:
            msg = f"Invalid fixed axis/axes: {bad}. Valid: {sorted(valid_axes)}"
            config.LOGGER.error(msg)
            raise config.InputError(msg)

        mask = jnp.ones((coords_flat.shape[0],), dtype=bool)
        for axis, val in fixed_coordinates.items():
            idx = self.AXIS_TO_IDX[axis]
            mask = mask & jnp.isclose(
                coords_flat[:, idx],
                float(val),
                rtol=0.0,
                atol=atol,
            )

        if not bool(jnp.any(mask)):
            msg = f"Slice produced no points for {fixed_coordinates}."
            config.LOGGER.error(msg)
            raise ValueError(msg)

        sliced_coords = coords_flat[mask, :]

        return SpatialComparisonGrid(
            domain=self.domain,
            coords=sliced_coords,
            fixed_coordinates=fixed_coordinates,
        )

class SpatialComparisonGrid(SpatialGrid):
    """A Cartesian grid whose axes are the unique coordinates of a point set.

    The input rows are not stored as the mesh. Each column is reduced to its
    sorted unique values, and ``coordinates`` is the Cartesian product of those
    values. A fixed axis keeps only the unique value that matches the requested
    number.

    Attributes:
        domain: Spatial bounds passed in at construction.
        spatial_dimensions: Number of columns, taken from ``len(domain.min)``.
        fixed_coordinates: Axis name to the value held constant. Empty when omitted.
        column_values: Sorted unique values on each axis, in ``x``, ``y``, ``z`` order.
            A fixed axis holds one value.
        coordinates: Mesh of those column values. The last axis is one entry per
            spatial axis.

    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        domain: SpatialDomain,
        coords: Array,
        fixed_coordinates: dict[str, float] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Build the mesh from the unique value in each coordinate column.

        A fixed axis is kept only when one unique value lies within ``1e-9`` of the
        requested number. The stored value is the one from ``coords``, not the number
        that was requested. The comparison does not use a relative tolerance.

        Args:
            domain: Spatial bounds. ``len(domain.min)`` is the number of columns read
                from ``coords``.
            coords: Point rows, shaped ``(n, spatial_dimensions)``, in ``x``, ``y``, ``z``
                order.
            fixed_coordinates: Axis name to the value held constant. Default: no fixed axes.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If a fixed value is not present in that column.

        """
        super().__init__()
        self.domain = domain
        self.spatial_dimensions = len(domain.min)
        self.fixed_coordinates = fixed_coordinates or {}

        unique_per_column = [
            jnp.sort(jnp.unique(coords[:, i])) for i in range(self.spatial_dimensions)
        ]

        # Apply fixed coordinates by masking the uniques
        self.column_values = []
        for i in range(self.spatial_dimensions):
            axis_name = list(SpatialGrid.AXIS_TO_IDX.keys())[i]  # "x", "y", "z", ...
            if axis_name in self.fixed_coordinates:
                # Only keep the fixed value
                # (match by tolerance so model float matches CSV)
                fixed_val = float(self.fixed_coordinates[axis_name])
                uniques = unique_per_column[i]
                close = jnp.isclose(uniques, fixed_val, rtol=0.0, atol=1e-9)
                if not jnp.any(close):
                    msg = f"Fixed coordinate {axis_name}={fixed_val} not in column {i}"
                    config.LOGGER.error(msg)
                    raise ValueError(msg)
                # Use the CSV's value so scatter indexing matches
                self.column_values.append(jnp.array([uniques[jnp.argmax(close)]]))
            else:
                self.column_values.append(unique_per_column[i])

        # build the coordinate mesh
        if len(self.column_values) == 1:
            mesh = [self.column_values[0]]
        else:
            mesh = jnp.meshgrid(*self.column_values, indexing="xy")
        self.coordinates = jnp.stack(mesh, axis=-1)

    def shape(self) -> tuple[int, ...]:
        """Return the unique-value count on each spatial axis.

        The order is ``x``, ``y``, ``z``. This is not the shape of ``coordinates``.
        Two axes stored with ``xy`` indexing have mesh shape ``(ny, nx, 2)``, while
        this method returns ``(nx, ny)``. Time is not included.

        Returns:
            One count per spatial axis.

        """
        return tuple(int(v.size) for v in self.column_values)

    def indices_for(self, coords: Array) -> list[Array]:
        """Return the column index of each coordinate.

        Each column is located with a binary search on ``column_values``. The search
        returns an insertion index and does not check that the coordinate is present.

        Args:
            coords: Point rows, shaped ``(n, spatial_dimensions)``, in ``x``, ``y``, ``z``
                order.

        Returns:
            One index array per spatial axis, in ``x``, ``y``, ``z`` order.

        """
        n_spatial = self.coordinates.shape[-1]
        return [jnp.searchsorted(self.column_values[i], coords[:, i]) for i in range(n_spatial)]

    def add_time(
        self,
        times: Array,
        *,
        time_range: tuple[float, float] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Append these time samples to the mesh.

        ``times`` is flattened. ``time_range`` defaults to the first and last stored
        time after that flatten. The parent builder then repeats the spatial mesh once
        per time and appends time as the last coordinate.

        Args:
            times: Time values, one entry per time sample.
            time_range: First and last time to record. Default: the minimum and maximum
                of ``times``.

        """
        times = jnp.asarray(times, dtype=config.get_dtype()).reshape(-1)
        self.has_time = True
        self.times = times
        self.num_times = int(times.shape[0])
        self.time_range = time_range or (float(times.min()), float(times.max()))
        self._build_spatiotemporal_coordinates()

    def scatter(
        self,
        coords: Array,
        values: Array,
        *,
        require_full: bool = True,
    ) -> Array:
        """Place sample values onto the Cartesian mesh.

        ``coords`` uses ``x``, ``y``, ``z`` order. For two or more axes the mesh is
        stored with ``xy`` indexing, so the output shape is ``(ny, nx, ...)`` and the
        ``x`` and ``y`` indices are swapped to match. One axis keeps shape ``(nx,)``.

        ``require_full`` checks that the number of rows equals the number of mesh
        points. It does not check that every mesh point appears exactly once.

        Args:
            coords: Point rows, shaped ``(n, spatial_dimensions)``.
            values: One value per row of ``coords``.
            require_full: Reject a point set that is not the same length as the mesh.
                Default: ``True``.

        Returns:
            The values on the mesh.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If ``require_full`` is true and the row count is not the mesh size.

        """
        # coords: (n_samples, n_spatial) in (x, y, [z]) column order
        n_spatial = self.coordinates.shape[-1]

        # indices along each axis as per column_values order: [x, y, (z)]
        idxs = self.indices_for(coords)

        # meshgrid(indexing="xy") => grid shape is (ny, nx, [nz]), i.e. Y first, then X
        if n_spatial >= TWO_DIMENSIONAL:
            shp = (
                int(self.column_values[1].size),  # ny
                int(self.column_values[0].size),  # nx
                *(int(v.size) for v in self.column_values[2:]),
            )  # [nz, ...]
            idxs = [idxs[1], idxs[0], *idxs[2:]]  # swap X<->Y for XY indexing
        else:
            shp = (int(self.column_values[0].size),)

        if require_full and int(coords.shape[0]) != int(jnp.prod(jnp.array(shp))):
            config.LOGGER.info(f"{coords.shape[0]=}")
            config.LOGGER.info(f"{int(jnp.prod(jnp.array(shp)))=}")
            msg = "CSV does not form a full Cartesian grid."
            config.LOGGER.error(msg)
            raise ValueError(msg)

        out = jnp.empty(shp, dtype=values.dtype)
        return out.at[tuple(idxs)].set(values)

def __init__(
    self,
    domain: SpatialDomain,
    coords: Array,
    fixed_coordinates: dict[str, float] | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Build the mesh from the unique value in each coordinate column.

    A fixed axis is kept only when one unique value lies within ``1e-9`` of the
    requested number. The stored value is the one from ``coords``, not the number
    that was requested. The comparison does not use a relative tolerance.

    Args:
        domain: Spatial bounds. ``len(domain.min)`` is the number of columns read
            from ``coords``.
        coords: Point rows, shaped ``(n, spatial_dimensions)``, in ``x``, ``y``, ``z``
            order.
        fixed_coordinates: Axis name to the value held constant. Default: no fixed axes.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If a fixed value is not present in that column.

    """
    super().__init__()
    self.domain = domain
    self.spatial_dimensions = len(domain.min)
    self.fixed_coordinates = fixed_coordinates or {}

    unique_per_column = [
        jnp.sort(jnp.unique(coords[:, i])) for i in range(self.spatial_dimensions)
    ]

    # Apply fixed coordinates by masking the uniques
    self.column_values = []
    for i in range(self.spatial_dimensions):
        axis_name = list(SpatialGrid.AXIS_TO_IDX.keys())[i]  # "x", "y", "z", ...
        if axis_name in self.fixed_coordinates:
            # Only keep the fixed value
            # (match by tolerance so model float matches CSV)
            fixed_val = float(self.fixed_coordinates[axis_name])
            uniques = unique_per_column[i]
            close = jnp.isclose(uniques, fixed_val, rtol=0.0, atol=1e-9)
            if not jnp.any(close):
                msg = f"Fixed coordinate {axis_name}={fixed_val} not in column {i}"
                config.LOGGER.error(msg)
                raise ValueError(msg)
            # Use the CSV's value so scatter indexing matches
            self.column_values.append(jnp.array([uniques[jnp.argmax(close)]]))
        else:
            self.column_values.append(unique_per_column[i])

    # build the coordinate mesh
    if len(self.column_values) == 1:
        mesh = [self.column_values[0]]
    else:
        mesh = jnp.meshgrid(*self.column_values, indexing="xy")
    self.coordinates = jnp.stack(mesh, axis=-1)

def add_time(
    self,
    times: Array,
    *,
    time_range: tuple[float, float] | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Append these time samples to the mesh.

    ``times`` is flattened. ``time_range`` defaults to the first and last stored
    time after that flatten. The parent builder then repeats the spatial mesh once
    per time and appends time as the last coordinate.

    Args:
        times: Time values, one entry per time sample.
        time_range: First and last time to record. Default: the minimum and maximum
            of ``times``.

    """
    times = jnp.asarray(times, dtype=config.get_dtype()).reshape(-1)
    self.has_time = True

    self.num_times = int(times.shape[0])
    self.time_range = time_range or (float(times.min()), float(times.max()))
    self._build_spatiotemporal_coordinates()

def indices_for(self, coords: Array) -> list[Array]:
    """Return the column index of each coordinate.

    Each column is located with a binary search on ``column_values``. The search
    returns an insertion index and does not check that the coordinate is present.

    Args:
        coords: Point rows, shaped ``(n, spatial_dimensions)``, in ``x``, ``y``, ``z``
            order.

    Returns:
        One index array per spatial axis, in ``x``, ``y``, ``z`` order.

    """
    n_spatial = self.coordinates.shape[-1]
    return [jnp.searchsorted(self.column_values[i], coords[:, i]) for i in range(n_spatial)]

    if require_full and int(coords.shape[0]) != int(jnp.prod(jnp.array(shp))):

def shape(self) -> tuple[int, ...]:

def slice(
    self,
    fixed_coordinates: dict[str, float] | None = None,
    *,
    atol: float = 1e-9,
) -> SpatialComparisonGrid:
    """Return the grid points that sit on the requested fixed coordinates.

    The spatial coordinates are flattened to one row per point. With no fixed
    coordinates, every row is kept and the grid's own ``fixed_coordinates`` are
    passed through when that attribute exists. Each requested axis must be within
    ``atol`` of the given value. The comparison does not use a relative tolerance.

    Args:
        fixed_coordinates: Axis name to the value that row must match. Default: no
            constraint.
        atol: Absolute tolerance for each comparison. Default: ``1e-9``.

    Returns:
        A [`SpatialComparisonGrid`][pinnjax.SpatialComparisonGrid] of the matching rows.

    Raises:
        pinnjax.InputError: If an axis name is outside this grid's spatial axes.
        ValueError: If no row matches.

    """
    from .comparison import SpatialComparisonGrid

    fixed_coordinates = fixed_coordinates or {}

    coords_flat = self.coordinates.reshape(-1, self.spatial_dimensions)

    if not fixed_coordinates:
        return SpatialComparisonGrid(
            domain=self.domain,
            coords=coords_flat,
            fixed_coordinates=getattr(self, "fixed_coordinates", None),
        )

    valid_axes = set(["x", "y", "z"][: self.spatial_dimensions])
    bad = [k for k in fixed_coordinates if k not in valid_axes]
    if bad:
        msg = f"Invalid fixed axis/axes: {bad}. Valid: {sorted(valid_axes)}"
        config.LOGGER.error(msg)
        raise config.InputError(msg)

    mask = jnp.ones((coords_flat.shape[0],), dtype=bool)
    for axis, val in fixed_coordinates.items():
        idx = self.AXIS_TO_IDX[axis]
        mask = mask & jnp.isclose(
            coords_flat[:, idx],
            float(val),
            rtol=0.0,
            atol=atol,
        )

    if not bool(jnp.any(mask)):
        msg = f"Slice produced no points for {fixed_coordinates}."
        config.LOGGER.error(msg)
        raise ValueError(msg)

    sliced_coords = coords_flat[mask, :]

    return SpatialComparisonGrid(
        domain=self.domain,
        coords=sliced_coords,
        fixed_coordinates=fixed_coordinates,
    )

class LineGrid(SpatialGrid):
    """A grid with one varying axis and the other axes held constant.

    ``spatial_dimensions`` follows the domain. A line through a 3D domain still
    stores ``x``, ``y``, and ``z`` on each point. The two constant axes come from
    ``fixed_coordinates``.

    Attributes:
        domain: Spatial bounds being sampled.
        spatial_dimensions: Number of axes in the domain.
        periodic: Drop the endpoint of the varying axis. Default: ``False``.
        fixed_coordinates: Axis name to the constant value.
        num_points: Sample count for the varying axis, stored as a one-element tuple.
        free_axis: Name of the varying axis.
        free_axes: ``free_axis`` in a one-element list.
        coordinates: Sampled points. The last axis is one entry per domain axis.

    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        domain: SpatialDomain,
        fixed_coordinates: dict[str, float] | None = None,
        num_points: int = 100,
        axis: str | None = None,
        time_range: tuple[float, float] | None = None,
        num_times: int | None = None,
        *,
        periodic: bool = False,
    ) -> None:
        """Sample one axis of the domain.

        ``axis=None`` uses the single axis that is absent from ``fixed_coordinates``.
        A time axis is added only when both ``time_range`` and ``num_times`` are given.

        Args:
            domain: Spatial bounds to sample.
            fixed_coordinates: Axis name to the constant value. Default: no fixed axes.
            num_points: Number of samples on the varying axis. Default: ``100``.
            axis: Name of the varying axis. Default: the one axis that is not fixed.
            time_range: First and last time. Default: no time axis.
            num_times: Number of time samples, including both ends. Default: no time axis.
            periodic: Drop the endpoint of the varying axis. Default: ``False``.

        Raises:
            pinnjax.InputError: If ``axis`` is omitted and the number of unfixed axes
                is not one.

        """
        super().__init__()
        self.domain = domain
        self.spatial_dimensions = len(domain.min)

        self.periodic = periodic
        self.fixed_coordinates = fixed_coordinates or {}
        self.num_points = (num_points,)

        if axis is None:
            free_axes = self._get_free_axes(self.fixed_coordinates, expected_count=1)
            self.free_axis = free_axes[0]
        else:
            self.free_axis = axis

        self.free_axes = [self.free_axis]

        # Build spatial coordinates
        self.coordinates = self._build_coordinates(
            self.free_axes,
            self.fixed_coordinates,
            self.num_points,
        )

        # Setup temporal dimension if specified
        if time_range is not None and num_times is not None:
            self._setup_temporal(time_range, num_times)

def slice(
    self,
    fixed_coordinates: dict[str, float] | None = None,
    *,
    atol: float = 1e-9,
) -> SpatialComparisonGrid:
    """Return the grid points that sit on the requested fixed coordinates.

    The spatial coordinates are flattened to one row per point. With no fixed
    coordinates, every row is kept and the grid's own ``fixed_coordinates`` are
    passed through when that attribute exists. Each requested axis must be within
    ``atol`` of the given value. The comparison does not use a relative tolerance.

    Args:
        fixed_coordinates: Axis name to the value that row must match. Default: no
            constraint.
        atol: Absolute tolerance for each comparison. Default: ``1e-9``.

    Returns:
        A [`SpatialComparisonGrid`][pinnjax.SpatialComparisonGrid] of the matching rows.

    Raises:
        pinnjax.InputError: If an axis name is outside this grid's spatial axes.
        ValueError: If no row matches.

    """
    from .comparison import SpatialComparisonGrid

    fixed_coordinates = fixed_coordinates or {}

    coords_flat = self.coordinates.reshape(-1, self.spatial_dimensions)

    if not fixed_coordinates:
        return SpatialComparisonGrid(
            domain=self.domain,
            coords=coords_flat,
            fixed_coordinates=getattr(self, "fixed_coordinates", None),
        )

    valid_axes = set(["x", "y", "z"][: self.spatial_dimensions])
    bad = [k for k in fixed_coordinates if k not in valid_axes]
    if bad:
        msg = f"Invalid fixed axis/axes: {bad}. Valid: {sorted(valid_axes)}"
        config.LOGGER.error(msg)
        raise config.InputError(msg)

    mask = jnp.ones((coords_flat.shape[0],), dtype=bool)
    for axis, val in fixed_coordinates.items():
        idx = self.AXIS_TO_IDX[axis]
        mask = mask & jnp.isclose(
            coords_flat[:, idx],
            float(val),
            rtol=0.0,
            atol=atol,
        )

    if not bool(jnp.any(mask)):
        msg = f"Slice produced no points for {fixed_coordinates}."
        config.LOGGER.error(msg)
        raise ValueError(msg)

    sliced_coords = coords_flat[mask, :]

    return SpatialComparisonGrid(
        domain=self.domain,
        coords=sliced_coords,
        fixed_coordinates=fixed_coordinates,
    )

    """A grid that samples ``x``, ``y``, and ``z``.

    The domain must have three spatial axes. No axis is held constant.

    Attributes:
        domain: Spatial bounds being sampled.
        spatial_dimensions: Number of axes in the domain. This is ``3``.
        periodic: Drop the endpoint of each axis. Default: ``False``.
        fixed_coordinates: Empty. This grid does not fix an axis.
        num_points: Sample count for ``x``, ``y``, and ``z``.
        free_axes: ``["x", "y", "z"]``.
        coordinates: Sampled points. The last axis is ``x``, ``y``, ``z``.

    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        domain: SpatialDomain,
        num_points: tuple[int, int, int] = (100, 100, 100),
        time_range: tuple[float, float] | None = None,
        num_times: int | None = None,
        *,
        periodic: bool = False,
    ) -> None:
        """Sample all three axes of a 3D domain.

        A time axis is added only when both ``time_range`` and ``num_times`` are given.

        Args:
            domain: Spatial bounds to sample. Must have three axes.
            num_points: Sample count for ``x``, ``y``, and ``z``.
                Default: ``(100, 100, 100)``.
            time_range: First and last time. Default: no time axis.
            num_times: Number of time samples, including both ends. Default: no time axis.
            periodic: Drop the endpoint of each axis. Default: ``False``.

        Raises:
            pinnjax.InputError: If the domain does not have three spatial axes.

        """
        super().__init__()
        self.domain = domain
        self.spatial_dimensions = len(domain.min)

        self.periodic = periodic

        if self.spatial_dimensions != THREE_DIMENSIONAL:
            msg = "RectangularGrid3D requires 3D domain"
            config.LOGGER.error(msg)
            raise config.InputError(msg)

        self.num_points = num_points
        self.free_axes = ["x", "y", "z"]
        self.fixed_coordinates = {}

        # Build spatial coordinates
        self.coordinates = self._build_coordinates(
            self.free_axes,
            self.fixed_coordinates,
            self.num_points,
        )

        # Setup temporal dimension if specified
        if time_range is not None and num_times is not None:
            self._setup_temporal(time_range, num_times)

class MorrisMethod(Sensitivity):
    """Screen parameters with the Morris elementary-effects method.

    Each trajectory is a random walk on the unit hypercube ``[0, 1]``. One
    coordinate changes at each step, by ``+step_size`` or ``-step_size``.
    :meth:`to_real` maps those unit values back onto the ranges in the parameter
    space.

    A parameter space maps each name to ``(kind, bounds)``. ``kind`` is a
    :data:`~pinnjax.importance.types.ParamType`. ``bounds`` is a
    ``(low, high)`` pair for ``"continuous"`` and ``"log-cont"``, and a
    one-dimensional array of allowed values for ``"discrete"`` and ``"category"``.

    Attributes:
        step_size: Step length on the unit interval. At most ``0.5``.
        key: JAX random key. Sampling and trajectory generation replace it.
        trajectories: Walks from the last :meth:`generate_trajectories` call.
            ``None`` until that method runs.

    """

    trajectories: list[list[dict[str, jax.Array]]] | None

    def __init__(self, step_size: float = 0.25) -> None:
        """Store the step length and seed the random key.

        The key comes from :func:`pinnjax.config.get_seed`.

        Args:
            step_size: Step length on the unit interval. Default: ``0.25``.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If ``step_size`` is greater than ``0.5``.

        """
        if step_size <= 0.5:
            self.step_size = step_size
        else:
            msg = f"The step_size ({step_size}) is too LARGE for the Morris method."
            config.LOGGER.error(msg)
            raise ValueError(msg)

        key, _ = jax.random.split(jax.random.key(config.get_seed()))
        self.key = key

        self.trajectories = None

    def sample(
        self,
        parameter_space: dict[
            str,
            tuple[ParamType, ContinuousRange | DiscreteRange],
        ],
    ) -> dict[str, jax.Array]:
        """Draw one point in the unit hypercube.

        Each parameter receives one uniform value on ``[0, 1]``. The kinds and bounds
        in ``parameter_space`` are ignored. The draw replaces :attr:`key`.

        Args:
            parameter_space: Parameter name to ``(kind, bounds)``. Only the names are used.

        Returns:
            Parameter name to a scalar array on ``[0, 1]``.

        """
        # sample in [0, 1] space

        out: dict[str, jax.Array] = {}
        _keys = jax.random.split(self.key, len(parameter_space) + 1)
        self.key, *subkeys = _keys
        for (name, _), key in zip(parameter_space.items(), subkeys, strict=False):
            out[name] = jax.random.uniform(key, ())  # default between 0 and 1
        return out

    def _trajectory(
        self,
        parameter_space: dict[
            str,
            tuple[ParamType, ContinuousRange | DiscreteRange],
        ],
    ) -> list[dict[str, jax.Array]]:
        parameters = list(parameter_space.keys())

        self.key, (subkey) = jax.random.split(self.key, 2)
        permutations = jax.random.permutation(subkey, jnp.arange(len(parameters)))

        old = self.sample(parameter_space)
        trajectory: list[dict[str, jax.Array]] = [old]
        for perm in permutations:
            parameter = parameters[int(perm)]
            new = dict(old)
            new[parameter] = self._step(parameter, current_location=old)
            trajectory.append(new)
            old = new

        return trajectory

    def _determine_delta_sign(self, value: jax.Array) -> float:
        if value + self.step_size <= 1.0:
            return 1.0
        if value - self.step_size >= 0.0:
            return -1.0
        return -1.0 if value <= 0.5 else 1.0  # if this case triggers, the step_size is too large

    def _step(
        self,
        parameter: str,
        current_location: dict[str, jax.Array],
    ) -> jax.Array:
        p = current_location[parameter]
        _sign = self._determine_delta_sign(p)

        return p + (_sign * self.step_size)

    def generate_trajectories(
        self,
        parameter_space: dict[
            str,
            tuple[ParamType, ContinuousRange | DiscreteRange],
        ],
        n: int = 15,
    ) -> list[list[dict[str, jax.Array]]]:
        """Build elementary-effect trajectories and store them.

        Each trajectory starts at :meth:`sample` and then visits the parameters once,
        in random order. Each visit copies the previous point and moves that one
        parameter. The sign is positive when the step stays at most ``1``. Otherwise
        it is negative when the step stays at least ``0``. If neither step stays inside
        ``[0, 1]``, the sign is negative at values at most ``0.5`` and positive above
        that. A trajectory therefore has one more point than there are parameters.

        Args:
            parameter_space: Parameter name to ``(kind, bounds)``. Only the names are used.
            n: Number of trajectories. Default: ``15``.

        Returns:
            ``n`` trajectories. Each trajectory is a list of points, and each point maps
            a parameter name to a scalar array.

        """
        trajectories: list[list[dict[str, jax.Array]]] = []
        i = 0
        while i < n:
            trajectories.append(self._trajectory(parameter_space))
            i += 1
        self.trajectories = trajectories
        return self.trajectories

    def to_real(
        self,
        parameter_space: dict[
            str,
            tuple[ParamType, ContinuousRange | DiscreteRange],
        ],
    ) -> list[list[dict[str, jax.Array]]]:
        """Map the stored unit trajectories onto the parameter ranges.

        Args:
            parameter_space: Parameter name to ``(kind, bounds)``. Passed to
                :meth:`denormalize` for every coordinate.

        Returns:
            The stored trajectories, with each coordinate converted by :meth:`denormalize`.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If :meth:`generate_trajectories` has not been called.

        """
        trajectories = self.trajectories
        if trajectories is None:
            msg = "Call generate_trajectories() before to_real()."
            config.LOGGER.error(msg)
            raise ValueError(msg)

        real_trajectories: list[list[dict[str, jax.Array]]] = []
        for trajectory in trajectories:
            real_trajectory: list[dict[str, jax.Array]] = []
            for step in trajectory:
                _step: dict[str, jax.Array] = {}
                for name, value in step.items():
                    _step[name] = self.denormalize(name, value, parameter_space)
                real_trajectory.append(_step)
            real_trajectories.append(real_trajectory)
        return real_trajectories

    @staticmethod
    def normalize(value: jax.Array, low: jax.Array, high: jax.Array) -> jax.Array:
        """Map a value onto the unit interval.

        Args:
            value: Quantity to scale.
            low: Lower end of the original interval.
            high: Upper end of the original interval.

        Returns:
            ``(value - low) / (high - low)``.

        """
        return (value - low) / (high - low)

    @staticmethod
    def denormalize(
        name: str,
        norm_value: jax.Array,
        parameter_space: dict[
            str,
            tuple[ParamType, ContinuousRange | DiscreteRange],
        ],
    ) -> jax.Array:
        """Map one unit coordinate back onto its parameter range.

        ``"continuous"`` uses ``low + u * (high - low)``. ``"log-cont"`` uses the same
        fraction between ``log(low)`` and ``log(high)``, then exponentiates.
        ``"discrete"`` and ``"category"`` take index ``floor(u * n)``, clipped to the
        array, where ``n`` is the number of allowed values.

        Args:
            name: Parameter name in ``parameter_space``.
            norm_value: Coordinate on the unit interval.
            parameter_space: Parameter name to ``(kind, bounds)``.

        Returns:
            The coordinate on the original range or set of values.

        Raises:
            KeyError: If ``name`` is not in ``parameter_space``.
            TypeError: If a continuous kind does not have a ``(low, high)`` pair, or a
                discrete kind does not have an array of values.
            ValueError: If ``kind`` is not a known parameter type.

        """

        def _denormalize_continuous(
            _norm_value: jax.Array,
            low: jax.Array,
            high: jax.Array,
        ) -> jax.Array:
            return low + _norm_value * (high - low)

        def _denormalize_log_continuous(
            _norm_value: jax.Array,
            low: jax.Array,
            high: jax.Array,
        ) -> jax.Array:
            return jnp.exp(jnp.log(low) + _norm_value * (jnp.log(high) - jnp.log(low)))

        def _denormalize_discrete(
            _norm_value: jax.Array,
            values: jax.Array,
        ) -> jax.Array:
            n = int(values.shape[0])
            idx = jnp.floor(_norm_value * n).astype(jnp.int32)
            idx = jnp.clip(idx, 0, n - 1)
            return values[idx]

        def _denormalize_category(
            _norm_value: jax.Array,
            values: jax.Array,
        ) -> jax.Array:
            n = int(values.shape[0])
            idx = jnp.floor(_norm_value * n).astype(jnp.int32)
            idx = jnp.clip(idx, 0, n - 1)
            return values[idx]

        spec = parameter_space.get(name)
        if spec is None:
            msg = f"Unknown parameter: {name}"
            config.LOGGER.error(msg)
            raise KeyError(msg)
        ptype, bounds = spec

        match ptype.lower():
            case "continuous" | "log-cont":
                if not isinstance(bounds, tuple):
                    msg = f"{name} must have a (low, high) range."
                    config.LOGGER.error(msg)
                    raise TypeError(msg)
                low = jnp.asarray(bounds[0], dtype=config.get_dtype())
                high = jnp.asarray(bounds[1], dtype=config.get_dtype())
                if ptype.lower() == "continuous":
                    denorm = _denormalize_continuous(norm_value, low, high)
                else:
                    denorm = _denormalize_log_continuous(norm_value, low, high)
            case "discrete":
                if not isinstance(bounds, jax.Array):
                    msg = f"{name} must have an array of discrete values."
                    config.LOGGER.error(msg)
                    raise TypeError(msg)
                denorm = _denormalize_discrete(norm_value, bounds)
            case "category":
                if not isinstance(bounds, jax.Array):
                    msg = f"{name} must have an array of category values."
                    config.LOGGER.error(msg)
                    raise TypeError(msg)
                denorm = _denormalize_category(norm_value, bounds)
            case _:
                msg = f"Unknown parameter type: {ptype.lower()}"
                config.LOGGER.error(msg)
                raise ValueError(msg)

        return denorm

def __init__(self, step_size: float = 0.25) -> None:
    """Store the step length and seed the random key.

    The key comes from :func:`pinnjax.config.get_seed`.

    Args:
        step_size: Step length on the unit interval. Default: ``0.25``.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``step_size`` is greater than ``0.5``.

    """
    if step_size <= 0.5:
        self.step_size = step_size
    else:
        msg = f"The step_size ({step_size}) is too LARGE for the Morris method."
        config.LOGGER.error(msg)
        raise ValueError(msg)

    key, _ = jax.random.split(jax.random.key(config.get_seed()))
    self.key = key

    self.trajectories = None

def generate_trajectories(
    self,
    parameter_space: dict[
        str,
        tuple[ParamType, ContinuousRange | DiscreteRange],
    ],
    n: int = 15,
) -> list[list[dict[str, jax.Array]]]:
    """Build elementary-effect trajectories and store them.

    Each trajectory starts at :meth:`sample` and then visits the parameters once,
    in random order. Each visit copies the previous point and moves that one
    parameter. The sign is positive when the step stays at most ``1``. Otherwise
    it is negative when the step stays at least ``0``. If neither step stays inside
    ``[0, 1]``, the sign is negative at values at most ``0.5`` and positive above
    that. A trajectory therefore has one more point than there are parameters.

    Args:
        parameter_space: Parameter name to ``(kind, bounds)``. Only the names are used.
        n: Number of trajectories. Default: ``15``.

    Returns:
        ``n`` trajectories. Each trajectory is a list of points, and each point maps
        a parameter name to a scalar array.

    """
    trajectories: list[list[dict[str, jax.Array]]] = []
    i = 0
    while i < n:
        trajectories.append(self._trajectory(parameter_space))
        i += 1
    self.trajectories = trajectories
    return self.trajectories

def sample(
    self,
    parameter_space: dict[
        str,
        tuple[ParamType, ContinuousRange | DiscreteRange],
    ],
) -> dict[str, jax.Array]:
    """Draw one point in the unit hypercube.

    Each parameter receives one uniform value on ``[0, 1]``. The kinds and bounds
    in ``parameter_space`` are ignored. The draw replaces :attr:`key`.

    Args:
        parameter_space: Parameter name to ``(kind, bounds)``. Only the names are used.

    Returns:
        Parameter name to a scalar array on ``[0, 1]``.

    """
    # sample in [0, 1] space

    out: dict[str, jax.Array] = {}
    _keys = jax.random.split(self.key, len(parameter_space) + 1)
    self.key, *subkeys = _keys
    for (name, _), key in zip(parameter_space.items(), subkeys, strict=False):
        out[name] = jax.random.uniform(key, ())  # default between 0 and 1
    return out

def to_real(
    self,
    parameter_space: dict[
        str,
        tuple[ParamType, ContinuousRange | DiscreteRange],
    ],
) -> list[list[dict[str, jax.Array]]]:
    """Map the stored unit trajectories onto the parameter ranges.

    Args:
        parameter_space: Parameter name to ``(kind, bounds)``. Passed to
            :meth:`denormalize` for every coordinate.

    Returns:
        The stored trajectories, with each coordinate converted by :meth:`denormalize`.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If :meth:`generate_trajectories` has not been called.

    """
    trajectories = self.trajectories
    if trajectories is None:
        msg = "Call generate_trajectories() before to_real()."
        config.LOGGER.error(msg)
        raise ValueError(msg)

    real_trajectories: list[list[dict[str, jax.Array]]] = []
    for trajectory in trajectories:
        real_trajectory: list[dict[str, jax.Array]] = []
        for step in trajectory:
            _step: dict[str, jax.Array] = {}
            for name, value in step.items():
                _step[name] = self.denormalize(name, value, parameter_space)
            real_trajectory.append(_step)
        real_trajectories.append(real_trajectory)
    return real_trajectories
