def plot_prediction(
    prediction: jnp.ndarray,
    grid: SpatialGrid,
    *,
    sliced_axis: str | None = None,
    threshold: float | None = None,
    fig_size: tuple[float, float] | None = None,
    ax: Axes | None = None,
    cbar_ax: Axes | None = None,
    norm: mpl.colors.Normalize | None = None,
    cbar_ticks: jnp.ndarray | None = None,
    add_colorbar: bool = True,
    show: bool | None = True,
    save: bool | None = True,
    save_location: str | Path | None = None,
    save_name: str | None = "prediction",
    save_format: str = "pdf",
    dpi: int = 300,
    title: str | None = None,
    x_label: str | None = None,
    y_label: str | None = None,
    cbar_label: str | None = None,
    cmap: str | None = "turbo",
    sparse_interior: bool = True,
):
    """Plot a prediction defined on a SpatialGrid.

    A 2D field is drawn by [`plot_field`][pinnjax.plot.plot_field]. A 3D field
    is a scatter of the six boundary faces, unless ``sparse_interior`` is
    false, and the domain outline is added afterward. ``sliced_axis`` omitted
    uses one fixed grid coordinate, otherwise ``"z"``.

    Args:
        prediction: Predicted field.
        grid: [`SpatialGrid`][pinnjax.SpatialGrid] for the domain and labels.
        sliced_axis: Axis removed before a 2D plot.
        threshold: Upper clip.
        fig_size: Figure size in inches. When omitted, from the 2D grid, or
            unset for a 3D figure.
        ax: Existing axes.
        cbar_ax: Axes for the colorbar.
        norm: Color scale. When omitted, the plotted minimum and maximum.
        cbar_ticks: Colorbar tick locations. When omitted, five ticks.
        add_colorbar: Draw the colorbar.
        show: Display the figure.
        save: Write the figure to disk.
        save_location: Directory for the saved figure.
        save_name: File name.
        save_format: File format.
        dpi: Resolution used when saving.
        title: Axes title.
        x_label: Horizontal axis label. When omitted, the axis name and ``[m]``.
        y_label: Vertical axis label. When omitted, the axis name and ``[m]``.
        cbar_label: Colorbar label.
        cmap: Colormap name.
        sparse_interior: For a 3D field, draw only the boundary faces.

    Returns:
        The Matplotlib figure and axes. ``show`` false closes a 3D figure this
        function created.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the squeezed field is not 2D or 3D.

    """
    sliced_axis = _resolved_sliced_axis(
        grid,
        sliced_axis,
    )

    prediction = _squeeze_spatial_slice_for_image(
        prediction,
        grid,
        sliced_axis,
    )

    dim = prediction.ndim

    if dim == TWO_DIMENSIONAL:
        idx = AXIS_TO_IDX[sliced_axis or "z"]

        other_idxs = tuple(i for i in AXIS_TO_IDX.values() if i != idx)

        extent = (
            grid.domain.min[other_idxs[0]],
            grid.domain.max[other_idxs[0]],
            grid.domain.min[other_idxs[1]],
            grid.domain.max[other_idxs[1]],
        )

        fig_size = fig_size if fig_size is not None else _figsize_from_2d_grid(grid)

        x_label = x_label or IDX_TO_AXIS[other_idxs[0]] + " [m]"

        y_label = y_label or IDX_TO_AXIS[other_idxs[1]] + " [m]"

        return plot_field(
            prediction,
            extent=extent,
            threshold=threshold,
            fig_size=fig_size,
            ax=ax,
            cbar_ax=cbar_ax,
            norm=norm,
            cbar_ticks=cbar_ticks,
            add_colorbar=add_colorbar,
            show=show,
            save=save,
            save_location=save_location,
            save_name=save_name,
            save_format=save_format,
            dpi=dpi,
            title=title,
            x_label=x_label,
            y_label=y_label,
            cbar_label=cbar_label,
            cmap=cmap,
        )

    if dim != THREE_DIMENSIONAL:
        msg = f"Unsupported grid dimension: {dim}"
        config.LOGGER.error(msg)
        raise ValueError(msg)

    # TODO(@mjryande): Convert this to PyVista or another volumetric plotter.

    if threshold is not None:
        prediction = jnp.clip(
            prediction,
            None,
            threshold,
        )

    owns_figure = ax is None

    if ax is None:
        fig = plt.figure(
            figsize=fig_size,
        )
        ax = fig.add_subplot(
            111,
            projection="3d",
        )
    else:
        fig = ax.figure

    if norm is None:
        norm = mpl.colors.Normalize(
            vmin=float(jnp.min(prediction)),
            vmax=float(jnp.max(prediction)),
        )

    if sparse_interior:
        face = jnp.zeros(
            prediction.shape,
            dtype=bool,
        )

        face = face.at[0, :, :].set(True)
        face = face.at[-1, :, :].set(True)
        face = face.at[:, 0, :].set(True)
        face = face.at[:, -1, :].set(True)
        face = face.at[:, :, 0].set(True)
        face = face.at[:, :, -1].set(True)

        mask = face.ravel()

    else:
        mask = jnp.ones(
            prediction.shape,
            dtype=bool,
        ).ravel()

    x = grid.coordinates[..., 0].ravel()[mask]
    y = grid.coordinates[..., 1].ravel()[mask]
    z = grid.coordinates[..., 2].ravel()[mask]
    values = prediction.ravel()[mask]

    if not isinstance(ax, Axes3D):
        msg = "A 3D prediction requires a 3D axes."
        config.LOGGER.error(msg)
        raise TypeError(msg)

    surface = ax.scatter3D(
        x,
        y,
        z,
        c=values,
        norm=norm,
        cmap=cmap,
        rasterized=True,
        depthshade=False,
    )

    ax.set_xlim(
        float(grid.domain.min[0]),
        float(grid.domain.max[0]),
    )
    ax.set_ylim(
        float(grid.domain.min[1]),
        float(grid.domain.max[1]),
    )
    ax.set_zlim(
        float(grid.domain.min[2]),
        float(grid.domain.max[2]),
    )

    _force_limit_ticks(ax)

    if add_colorbar:
        if cbar_ticks is None:
            tick_min = surface.norm.vmin
            tick_max = surface.norm.vmax
            if tick_min is None or tick_max is None:
                msg = "The color scale needs a minimum and a maximum."
                config.LOGGER.error(msg)
                raise ValueError(msg)
            cbar_ticks = jnp.linspace(
                float(jnp.asarray(tick_min)),
                float(jnp.asarray(tick_max)),
                num=5,
            )

        fig.colorbar(
            surface,
            cax=cbar_ax,
            label=cbar_label,
            orientation="horizontal",
            pad=0.05,
            ticks=cbar_ticks,
            shrink=0.9,
        )

    if not isinstance(fig, Figure):
        msg = "A 3D prediction requires a Matplotlib figure."
        config.LOGGER.error(msg)
        raise TypeError(msg)

    fig, ax = grid.domain.draw(
        show=False,
        fig=fig,
        ax=ax,
    )

    if title is not None:
        ax.set_title(title)

    if save:
        from pinnjax.plot.saving import save_plot

        save_plot(
            fig,
            save_location=save_location,
            save_name=save_name,
            save_format=save_format,
            dpi=dpi,
        )

    if show:
        plt.show()
    elif owns_figure:
        plt.close(fig)

    return fig, ax

def plot_prediction_evolution(
    evolution: Array,
    grid: SpatialGrid,
    *,
    sliced_axis: str | None = None,
    threshold: float | None = None,
    fig_size: tuple[float, float] | None = None,
    fps: int | None = None,
    show: bool | None = True,
    time: bool | None = False,
    save: bool | None = False,
    save_location: str | Path | None = None,
    save_name: str | None = None,
    x_label: str | None = None,
    y_label: str | None = None,
    cbar_label: str | None = None,
    cmap: str | None = "turbo",
    dpi: int = 300,
) -> tuple[Figure, Axes, FuncAnimation]:
    """Animate a predicted field over time.

    The first axis is the frame. The color scale uses the minimum and maximum
    of the whole series. ``sliced_axis`` omitted uses one fixed grid
    coordinate, otherwise ``"z"``. A ``.gif`` name is written with Pillow. Any
    other suffix uses ffmpeg. ``show`` false closes the figure.

    Args:
        evolution: Frames shaped ``(num_times, nx, ny)``.
        grid: [`SpatialGrid`][pinnjax.SpatialGrid] with sampled times.
        sliced_axis: Unused axis for the extent labels.
        threshold: Upper clip.
        fig_size: Figure size in inches. When omitted, from the 2D grid.
        fps: Frames per second. ``None`` divides the frame count by the domain
            time span. The result is at least ``1``.
        show: Display the animation.
        time: Overlay ``grid.times`` in the upper left.
        save: Write the animation.
        save_location: Directory for the saved file. When omitted, the working
            directory.
        save_name: File name, including the suffix.
        x_label: Horizontal axis label. When omitted, the axis name and ``[m]``.
        y_label: Vertical axis label. When omitted, the axis name and ``[m]``.
        cbar_label: Colorbar label.
        cmap: Colormap name.
        dpi: Resolution used when saving.

    Returns:
        The Matplotlib figure, axes, and animation.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the grid has no ``times``.

    """
    if threshold is not None:
        evolution = jnp.clip(evolution, None, threshold)

    if not hasattr(grid, "times") or grid.times is None:
        msg = "Grid must have temporal information for evolution plots"
        config.LOGGER.error(msg)
        raise ValueError(msg)

    if fps is None:
        domain_times = grid.domain.times
        if domain_times is None:
            msg = "Grid must have temporal information for evolution plots"
            config.LOGGER.error(msg)
            raise ValueError(msg)
        span = float(jnp.asarray(domain_times.range()))
        fps = max(1, int(evolution.shape[0] / span))

    # Get global min/max for consistent colorbar
    vmin = float(jnp.min(evolution))
    vmax = float(jnp.max(evolution))
    norm = mpl.colors.Normalize(vmin=vmin, vmax=vmax)

    # Create figure and axis
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(
        figsize=fig_size if fig_size is not None else _figsize_from_2d_grid(grid),
        constrained_layout=True,
    )

    sliced_axis = _resolved_sliced_axis(
        grid,
        sliced_axis,
    )

    # Initial plot
    idx = AXIS_TO_IDX[sliced_axis or "z"]
    other_idxs = tuple(i for i in AXIS_TO_IDX.values() if i != idx)
    im = ax.imshow(
        evolution[0],
        origin="lower",
        aspect="equal",
        extent=(
            grid.domain.min[other_idxs[0]],
            grid.domain.max[other_idxs[0]],
            grid.domain.min[other_idxs[1]],
            grid.domain.max[other_idxs[1]],
        ),
        cmap=cmap,
        norm=norm,
    )

    # Colorbar
    ticks = jnp.linspace(vmin, vmax, num=5)
    cbar = fig.colorbar(
        im,
        label=cbar_label,
        orientation="horizontal",
        pad=0.04,
        fraction=0.24,
        ticks=ticks,
    )
    x_label = x_label or IDX_TO_AXIS[other_idxs[0]] + " [m]"
    y_label = y_label or IDX_TO_AXIS[other_idxs[1]] + " [m]"

    ax.set_xlabel(x_label)
    ax.set_ylabel(y_label)
    _force_limit_ticks(ax)
    _style_2d_axes(ax, cbar)

    # Time text
    if time:
        time_text = ax.text(
            0.02,
            0.98,
            "",
            transform=ax.transAxes,
            verticalalignment="top",
            fontsize=_TICK_FONTSIZE,
            bbox={"boxstyle": round, "pad": 0.3, "facecolor": "white", "alpha": 0.85},
        )

    def animate(frame: int):
        """Animation function."""
        im.set_data(evolution[frame])
        if time:
            time_text.set_text(f"t = {grid.times[frame]:.3f} s")
            return [im, time_text]
        return [im]

    # Resolve constrained layout once before animation
    fig.canvas.draw()
    fig.set_layout_engine("none")

    # Create animation
    anim = FuncAnimation(
        fig,
        animate,
        frames=len(evolution),
        interval=1000 / fps,
        blit=True,
        repeat=True,
    )

    # Stop animation timer before the canvas is destroyed
    def on_close(_):
        if anim.event_source is not None:
            anim.event_source.stop()

    fig.canvas.mpl_connect("close_event", on_close)

    if save:
        # Resolve output path
        out_dir = Path(save_location) if save_location else Path.cwd()
        out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        out_path = out_dir / (save_name or "ani.gif")

        ext = out_path.suffix.lower()
        if ext == ".gif":
            writer = PillowWriter(fps=fps, bitrate=-1)
            anim.save(out_path, writer=writer, dpi=min(150, dpi))
        else:
            writer = FFMpegWriter(fps=fps, extra_args=["-vcodec", "libx264"])
            anim.save(out_path, writer=writer, dpi=dpi)

    if show:
        plt.show()
    else:
        if anim.event_source is not None:
            anim.event_source.stop()
        plt.close(fig)

    return fig, ax, anim

def plot_field(
    field: jnp.ndarray,
    *,
    extent: tuple[float, float, float, float] | None = None,
    threshold: float | None = None,
    fig_size: tuple[float, float] | None = None,
    ax: Axes | None = None,
    cbar_ax: Axes | None = None,
    norm: mpl.colors.Normalize | None = None,
    cbar_ticks: jnp.ndarray | None = None,
    add_colorbar: bool = True,
    show: bool | None = True,
    save: bool | None = False,
    save_location: str | Path | None = None,
    save_name: str | None = "field",
    save_format: str = "pdf",
    dpi: int = 300,
    title: str | None = None,
    x_label: str | None = None,
    y_label: str | None = None,
    cbar_label: str | None = None,
    cmap: str | None = "turbo",
):
    """Plot a two-dimensional scalar field.

    The image uses a lower origin and an equal aspect. ``threshold`` is an
    upper clip. An omitted color scale runs from the field minimum to its
    maximum, with five colorbar ticks. ``show`` false closes a figure this
    function created.

    Args:
        field: Array of shape ``(H, W)``.
        extent: ``(left, right, bottom, top)``.
        threshold: Upper clip.
        fig_size: Figure size in inches.
        ax: Existing axes.
        cbar_ax: Axes for the colorbar.
        norm: Color scale. When omitted, the field minimum and maximum.
        cbar_ticks: Colorbar tick locations. When omitted, five ticks.
        add_colorbar: Draw the colorbar.
        show: Display the figure.
        save: Write the figure to disk.
        save_location: Directory for the saved figure.
        save_name: File name.
        save_format: File format.
        dpi: Resolution used when saving.
        title: Axes title.
        x_label: Horizontal axis label.
        y_label: Vertical axis label.
        cbar_label: Colorbar label.
        cmap: Colormap name.

    Returns:
        The Matplotlib figure and axes.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``field`` is not two-dimensional.

    """
    field = jnp.asarray(field)

    if field.ndim != 2:
        raise ValueError(
            f"plot_field requires a two-dimensional scalar field. Got shape {field.shape}.",
        )

    if threshold is not None:
        field = jnp.clip(field, None, threshold)

    owns_figure = ax is None

    if ax is None:
        fig, ax = plt.subplots(
            figsize=fig_size,
            constrained_layout=True,
        )
    else:
        fig = ax.figure

    if norm is None:
        norm = mpl.colors.Normalize(
            vmin=float(jnp.min(field)),
            vmax=float(jnp.max(field)),
        )

    image = ax.imshow(
        field,
        origin="lower",
        aspect="equal",
        extent=extent,
        cmap=cmap,
        norm=norm,
    )

    cbar = None

    if add_colorbar:
        if cbar_ticks is None:
            vmin = image.norm.vmin
            vmax = image.norm.vmax
            if vmin is None or vmax is None:
                msg = "The color scale needs a minimum and a maximum."
                config.LOGGER.error(msg)
                raise ValueError(msg)
            cbar_ticks = jnp.linspace(
                float(jnp.asarray(vmin)),
                float(jnp.asarray(vmax)),
                num=5,
            )

        cbar = fig.colorbar(
            image,
            cax=cbar_ax,
            label=cbar_label,
            orientation="horizontal",
            pad=0.04,
            fraction=0.24,
            ticks=cbar_ticks,
        )

    if title is not None:
        ax.set_title(title)

    if x_label is not None:
        ax.set_xlabel(x_label)

    if y_label is not None:
        ax.set_ylabel(y_label)

    ax.grid(
        False,
        which="both",
        axis="both",
    )

    _force_limit_ticks(ax)
    _style_2d_axes(ax, cbar)

    if save:
        from pinnjax.plot.saving import save_plot

        save_plot(
            fig,
            save_location=save_location,
            save_name=save_name,
            save_format=save_format,
            dpi=dpi,
        )

    if show:
        plt.show()
    elif owns_figure and isinstance(fig, Figure):
        plt.close(fig)

    return fig, ax

def plot_model_prediction(
    model,
    inputs: Array,
    *,
    sample: int = 0,
    channel: int | None = 0,
    prediction_transformation: Callable[
        [Array, Array],
        Array,
    ]
    | None = None,
    extent: tuple[
        float,
        float,
        float,
        float,
    ]
    | None = None,
    threshold: float | None = None,
    fig_size: tuple[float, float] | None = None,
    ax: Axes | None = None,
    cbar_ax: Axes | None = None,
    norm: mpl.colors.Normalize | None = None,
    cbar_ticks: jnp.ndarray | None = None,
    add_colorbar: bool = True,
    show: bool | None = True,
    save: bool | None = False,
    save_location: str | Path | None = None,
    save_name: str | None = "prediction",
    save_format: str = "pdf",
    dpi: int = 300,
    title: str | None = None,
    x_label: str | None = None,
    y_label: str | None = None,
    cbar_label: str | None = None,
    cmap: str | None = "turbo",
):
    """Predict one sample with a model and plot one output field.

    The model is called with ``inputs[sample]``. A ``(H, W)`` result is the
    field. A ``(C, H, W)`` result uses ``channel``. One channel and an omitted
    ``channel`` select channel 0. The field is drawn by
    [`plot_field`][pinnjax.plot.plot_field].

    Args:
        model: Callable model. It receives one sample.
        inputs: Batch of model inputs. The first axis is the sample.
        sample: Sample index.
        channel: Output channel. ``None`` or ``0`` for a ``(H, W)`` result.
        prediction_transformation: Called as ``(sample, prediction)`` before
            the field is selected.
        extent: ``(left, right, bottom, top)`` passed to the image.
        threshold: Upper clip applied by [`plot_field`][pinnjax.plot.plot_field].
        fig_size: Figure size in inches.
        ax: Existing axes.
        cbar_ax: Axes for the colorbar.
        norm: Color scale. When omitted, the field minimum and maximum.
        cbar_ticks: Colorbar tick locations. When omitted, five ticks.
        add_colorbar: Draw the colorbar.
        show: Display the figure.
        save: Write the figure to disk.
        save_location: Directory for the saved figure.
        save_name: File name.
        save_format: File format.

        y_label: Vertical axis label.

    Returns:

    Raises:

            ``None`` or ``0``.

        ValueError: If the result is not ``(H, W)`` or ``(C, H, W)``.

    """
    if not 0 <= sample < inputs.shape[0]:
        raise IndexError(f"sample={sample} is invalid for {inputs.shape[0]} samples.")

    model_input = inputs[sample]
    prediction = model(model_input)

    if prediction_transformation is not None:
        prediction = prediction_transformation(
            model_input,
            prediction,
        )

    prediction = jnp.asarray(prediction)

    if prediction.ndim == 2:
        if channel not in (None, 0):
            raise ValueError(
                "channel can only be None or 0 for "
                "a two-dimensional prediction. "
                f"Got channel={channel}.",
            )

        field = prediction

    elif prediction.ndim == 3:
        if channel is None:
            if prediction.shape[0] != 1:
                raise ValueError(
                    "A channel must be specified for "
                    "a multi-channel prediction. "
                    f"Got shape {prediction.shape}.",
                )

            channel = 0

        if not 0 <= channel < prediction.shape[0]:
            raise IndexError(
                f"channel={channel} is invalid for prediction shape {prediction.shape}.",
            )

        field = prediction[channel]

    else:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Expected model output with shape (H, W) or (C, H, W). Got {prediction.shape}.",
        )

    return plot_field(
        field,
        extent=extent,
        threshold=threshold,
        fig_size=fig_size,
        ax=ax,
        cbar_ax=cbar_ax,
        norm=norm,
        cbar_ticks=cbar_ticks,
        add_colorbar=add_colorbar,
        show=show,
        save=save,
        save_location=save_location,
        save_name=save_name,
        save_format=save_format,
        dpi=dpi,
        title=title,
        x_label=x_label,
        y_label=y_label,
        cbar_label=cbar_label,
        cmap=cmap,
    )

def save_plot(
    plot,
    save_location: str | Path | None = None,
    save_name: str | None = None,
    save_format: str = "pdf",
    dpi: int = 300,
    bbox_inches: str | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Save a Matplotlib figure or a PyVista plotter.

    An axes object saves its figure. A file name with a suffix selects the
    format. Otherwise, ``save_format`` is used, and the suffix is added.
    PyVista writes ``svg``, ``eps``, ``ps``, ``pdf``, and ``tex`` as vector
    graphics. Other formats are screenshots. A raster PyVista plot is shown
    before the screenshot when it has not been shown and is not already
    off-screen. The directory is created when it does not exist.

    Args:
        plot: A Matplotlib ``Axes`` or ``Figure``, or a PyVista ``Plotter``.
        save_location: Directory for the file. Default: the working directory.
        save_name: File name. Default: ``plot`` plus ``save_format``.
        save_format: Format used when ``save_name`` has no suffix. Default:
            ``"pdf"``.
        dpi: Matplotlib resolution. A PyVista screenshot uses this as a scale
            against 96 dpi, at least ``1``. Default: ``300``.
        bbox_inches: Bounding box passed to Matplotlib. Unused for PyVista.
            Default: ``None``.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``plot`` is not a Matplotlib axes or figure, and not a
            PyVista plotter.

    """
    from matplotlib.axes import Axes
    from matplotlib.figure import Figure
    from pyvista import Plotter

    DEFAULT_NAME: str = "plot"

    backend = (
        "matplotlib"
        if isinstance(plot, (Axes, Figure))
        else "pyvista"
        if isinstance(plot, Plotter)
        else None
    )

    save_name = save_name or f"{DEFAULT_NAME}.{save_format}"
    match backend:
        case "matplotlib":
            out_dir = Path(save_location) if save_location else Path.cwd()
            out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

            out_path = out_dir / save_name
            ext = out_path.suffix.lower()
            fmt = ext.lstrip(".") if ext else save_format.lstrip(".")

            if not ext:
                out_path = out_path.with_suffix(f".{fmt}")

            figure = plot.figure if isinstance(plot, Axes) else plot
            figure.savefig(out_path, bbox_inches=bbox_inches, format=fmt, dpi=dpi)
        case "pyvista":
            out_dir = Path(save_location) if save_location else Path.cwd()
            out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            out_path = out_dir / save_name
            ext = out_path.suffix.lower()
            fmt = (
                ext.lstrip(".")
                if ext
                else (save_format.lstrip(".") if isinstance(save_format, str) else "pdf")
            )

            if not ext:
                out_path = out_path.with_suffix(f".{fmt}")

            plot.enable_anti_aliasing("ssaa")
            if fmt in {"svg", "eps", "ps", "pdf", "tex"}:
                plot.save_graphic(out_path)
            else:
                if plot._first_time and not plot.off_screen:
                    plot.show(
                        interactive=False,
                        auto_close=False,
                    )
                plot.screenshot(
                    out_path,
                    scale=max(1, round(dpi / 96)),
                )

        case _:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Invalid 'backend'. Must be {get_args(PlottingBackend)}. Got {backend}.",
            )

def value_over_time_plot(
    spatial_points: Iterable[tuple | list] | tuple | list,
    model: NeuralNetwork | None = None,
    truth: pathlib.Path | str | None = None,
    *,
    point_type: str = "percentage",  # 'percentage' or 'coordinate'
    domain: SpatialDomain | None = None,
    time: Time | Iterable | None = None,
    csv_coordinate_column_order: Iterable | None = None,
    csv_truth_column: int = -1,
    fig_size: tuple | None = (10, 5),
    title: str | None = None,
    x_axis_label: str | None = "Time [s]",
    y_axis_label: str | None = None,
    legend: bool = True,
    show_points: bool = True,
    show: bool = True,
    save: bool | None = False,
    save_location: str | pathlib.Path | None = None,
    save_name: str | None = "value_over_time",
    save_format: str = "pdf",
    dpi: int = 300,
) -> tuple[Figure, Axes] | tuple[Figure, Axes, Figure, Axes]:
    """Plot a field at fixed points over time.

    ``"percentage"`` places each point at the domain width on that axis times
    the fraction, measured from zero. ``"coordinate"`` uses the points as
    given. A [`Time`][pinnjax.Time] is sampled from its minimum to its
    maximum. An omitted time uses the domain time range, or the times in the
    truth file when a model is evaluated. Truth samples are snapped to the
    nearest CSV row. The point figure treats the points as 3D. A coordinate
    shared by every point is dropped and the other two axes are drawn instead.

    Args:
        spatial_points: One point per series.
        model: [`NeuralNetwork`][pinnjax.model.NeuralNetwork] evaluated at
            each point and time.
        truth: CSV path. The selected column is the value. The last remaining
            column is time.
        point_type: ``"percentage"`` or ``"coordinate"``.
        domain: [`SpatialDomain`][pinnjax.SpatialDomain]. Required for
            percentages.
        time: A [`Time`][pinnjax.Time], or times to sample. When omitted, the
            domain time range is used.
        csv_coordinate_column_order: Column order for the CSV coordinates.
        csv_truth_column: Value column.
        fig_size: Series figure size in inches.
        title: Title.
        x_axis_label: Horizontal label.
        y_axis_label: Vertical label.
        legend: Draw the legend.
        show_points: Also draw where the points sit.
        show: Display the figures.
        save: Write the figures.
        save_location: Directory for the saved files.
        save_name: Series file name.
        save_format: File format.
        dpi: Resolution used when saving.

    Returns:
        The series figure and axes. When ``show_points`` is true, the
        point-location figure and axes follow them. ``show`` false closes
        the figures.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If neither ``model`` nor ``truth`` is set.
        ValueError: If percentages are requested without a domain, or the
            domain has no time range.
        ValueError: If ``time`` or ``point_type`` is not one of the supported
            values, or a coordinate lies outside the domain.
        ValueError: If the CSV coordinate count does not match the model input
            width, or the model has no topology.
        TypeError: If ``truth`` is not a path or string.
        ValueError: If ``truth`` is not a CSV file.

    """
    import numpy as np

    # TODO(@mjryande): Parts of this only work in 3D (x, y, z)
    if model is None and truth is None:
        msg = "Neither a model or truth has be provided."
        config.LOGGER.error(msg)
        raise ValueError(msg)

    if domain is None and point_type.casefold() == "percentage":
        msg = "When using point_type = 'percentage, a domain must be provided."
        config.LOGGER.error(msg)
        raise ValueError(msg)

    if time is not None:
        if isinstance(time, Time):
            time = jnp.linspace(time.min, time.max, int(time.range() / time.step))
        elif isinstance(time, Iterable):
            time = jnp.asarray(time)
        else:
            msg = f"Invalid time type: {type(time)}."
            config.LOGGER.error(msg)
            raise ValueError(msg)
    elif domain is not None:
        domain_times = domain.times
        if domain_times is None:
            msg = "The domain has no time range."
            config.LOGGER.error(msg)
            raise ValueError(msg)
        time = jnp.linspace(
            float(jnp.asarray(domain_times.min)),
            float(jnp.asarray(domain_times.max)),
            int(
                float(jnp.asarray(domain_times.range())) / float(jnp.asarray(domain_times.step)),
            ),
        )

    spatial_points = jnp.asarray(spatial_points)
    match point_type.casefold():
        case "percentage":
            if domain is None:
                msg = "When using point_type = 'percentage, a domain must be provided."
                config.LOGGER.error(msg)
                raise ValueError(msg)
            percentages = [
                _percentage_to_point(domain, spatial_points[row])
                for row in range(spatial_points.shape[0])
            ]
            spatial_points = jnp.stack(percentages)
        case "coordinate":
            if domain is not None:
                for row in range(spatial_points.shape[0]):
                    if not _verify_domain(domain, spatial_points[row]):
                        msg = f"Selected Coordinate: {spatial_points[row]} is not in the Domain."
                        config.LOGGER.error(msg)
                        raise ValueError(msg)
            else:
                config.LOGGER.warning(
                    "Coordinates not guaranteed to be in the Domain.",
                )
            spatial_points = jnp.stack(spatial_points)
        case _:
            msg = f"Invalid point_type: {point_type}. Use either 'percentage' or 'coordinate'"
            config.LOGGER.error(msg)
            raise ValueError(msg)

    truth_times = None
    truth_values_at_points = None
    if truth is not None:
        if isinstance(truth, (str, pathlib.Path)):
            truth = pathlib.Path(truth)
            if truth.suffix.lower() != ".csv":
                msg = f"Expected a CSV file, got {truth.suffix}."
                config.LOGGER.error(msg)
                raise ValueError(msg)
            truth_np = pl.read_csv(truth).to_numpy().astype(float, copy=False)

            coordinates = np.delete(truth_np, csv_truth_column, axis=1)
            if csv_coordinate_column_order is not None:
                coordinates = coordinates[:, list(csv_coordinate_column_order)]

            truth_values = truth_np[:, csv_truth_column]
        else:
            msg = f"Invalid truth type: {type(truth)}. Use pathlib.Path or str (CSV)."
            config.LOGGER.error(msg)
            raise TypeError(msg)

        if model is not None:
            topology = cast("tuple[int, ...] | None", getattr(model, "topology", None))
            if topology is None:
                msg = "The model has no topology."
                config.LOGGER.error(msg)
                raise ValueError(msg)
            if coordinates.shape[1] != topology[0]:
                msg = (
                    f"Truth coordinates [Columns: {coordinates.shape[1]}] is not"
                    f" consistent with prediction topology [Columns:"
                    f" {topology[0]}]"
                )
                config.LOGGER.error(msg)
                raise ValueError(msg)

        truth_times = np.unique(coordinates[:, -1])

        spatial_points_np = np.asarray(spatial_points).copy()

        spatial_coordinates_at_t0 = coordinates[
            np.isclose(coordinates[:, -1], truth_times[0], rtol=0.0, atol=1e-12),
            :-1,
        ]
        tree = KDTree(spatial_coordinates_at_t0)
        for idx, point in enumerate(spatial_points_np):
            spatial_points_np[idx] = spatial_coordinates_at_t0[_nearest_neighbor_index(tree, point)]

        spatial_points = jnp.asarray(spatial_points_np)

        spatial_temporal_points = [
            np.hstack(
                [
                    np.tile(
                        pt[None, :],
                        (truth_times.size, 1),
                    ),
                    truth_times[:, None],
                ],
            )
            for pt in spatial_points_np
        ]

        tree = KDTree(coordinates)
        truth_values_at_points = [
            truth_values[np.array([_nearest_neighbor_index(tree, pt_row) for pt_row in pts])]
            for pts in spatial_temporal_points
        ]

    predictions = None
    if model is not None:
        if time is None and truth is not None:
            time = jnp.asarray(truth_times)
        if time is None:
            msg = "A time range is required to evaluate the model."
            config.LOGGER.error(msg)
            raise ValueError(msg)
        spatial_temporal_points = [
            jnp.hstack(
                [
                    jnp.tile(
                        pt[None, :],
                        (time.size, 1),
                    ),  # repeat spatial point for each time
                    time[:, None],  # append times
                ],
            )
            for pt in spatial_points
        ]

        predictions = []
        for points in spatial_temporal_points:
            _prediction = jax.vmap(model)(points)
            predictions.append(_prediction.reshape(points.shape[:-1]))

    # ----Plotting-----
    if show_points:
        # check if the points share an axis.
        axes = list(zip(*spatial_points, strict=False))
        shared_axes = [
            i for i, axis_values in enumerate(axes) if len({float(v) for v in axis_values}) == 1
        ]

        if not shared_axes:
            fig1 = plt.figure(constrained_layout=True)
            ax1 = fig1.add_subplot(111, projection="3d")
            _style(ax1)
            for i in range(len(spatial_points)):
                x, y, z = spatial_points[i]

                ax1.scatter(x, y, z)
                ax1.text(x, y, z, f"P{i + 1}", fontsize=14)

            if domain is not None:
                fig1, ax1 = domain.draw(show=False, fig=fig1, ax=ax1)

            if save:
                from pinnjax.plot.saving import save_plot

                save_plot(
                    fig1,
                    save_location=save_location,
                    save_name="representative_point_locations",
                    save_format=save_format,
                    dpi=dpi,
                )

        else:
            units = None
            all_axis = [0, 1, 2]
            for idx in shared_axes:  # plots each shared axis as a separate plot.
                other_axis = [ax for ax in all_axis if ax != idx]
                fig1, ax1 = plt.subplots(
                    constrained_layout=True,
                )
                _style(ax1)
                reduced_points = [list(p[:idx]) + list(p[idx + 1 :]) for p in spatial_points]
                for i, (x, y) in enumerate(reduced_points):
                    ax1.scatter(x, y)
                    ax1.annotate(f"P{i + 1}", (x, y), fontsize=14)

                if domain is not None:
                    _mins = tuple(domain.min[:idx] + domain.min[idx + 1 :])
                    _maxs = tuple(domain.max[:idx] + domain.max[idx + 1 :])
                    units = getattr(domain, "UNITS", {}).get("min", None)

                    xs = jnp.linspace(_mins[0], _maxs[0], num=5)
                    ys = jnp.linspace(_mins[1], _maxs[1], num=5)
                    ax1.set_xticks(xs)
                    ax1.set_yticks(ys)

                ax1.set_xlabel(
                    str(IDX_TO_AXIS[other_axis[0]]) + (f" [{units}]" if units is not None else ""),
                )
                ax1.set_ylabel(
                    str(IDX_TO_AXIS[other_axis[1]]) + (f" [{units}]" if units is not None else ""),
                )

                ax1.set_aspect("equal", adjustable="box")

                if save:
                    from pinnjax.plot.saving import save_plot

                    save_plot(
                        fig1,
                        save_location=save_location,
                        save_name=(
                            f"representative_point_locations_"
                            f"{IDX_TO_AXIS[other_axis[0]]}-"
                            f"{IDX_TO_AXIS[other_axis[1]]}"
                        ),
                        save_format=save_format,
                        dpi=dpi,
                    )

    # Main Plot.
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=fig_size)
    _style(ax)

    colors = cycle(_style_colors())

    for idx, _ in enumerate(spatial_points):
        color = next(colors)
        if model is not None:
            if time is None or predictions is None:
                msg = "A time range is required to evaluate the model."
                config.LOGGER.error(msg)
                raise ValueError(msg)
            ax.plot(
                time,
                predictions[idx],
                color=color,
                label=f"P{idx + 1}-PINN",
            )
        if truth is not None:
            fig_width = fig_size[0] if fig_size is not None else 10
            max_marker_points = int(6.0 * fig_width)

            if truth_times is None or truth_values_at_points is None:
                msg = "Truth values were not loaded."
                config.LOGGER.error(msg)
                raise ValueError(msg)
            if truth_times.size <= max_marker_points:
                ax.scatter(
                    truth_times,
                    truth_values_at_points[idx],
                    color=color,
                    edgecolors="black",
                    marker="o",
                    linewidths=0.25,
                    s=12,
                    label=f"P{idx + 1}-GT",
                )
            else:
                ax.plot(
                    truth_times,
                    truth_values_at_points[idx],
                    color=color,
                    linestyle="--",
                    linewidth=1.25,
                    label=f"P{idx + 1}-GT",
                )

    if x_axis_label:
        ax.set_xlabel(x_axis_label, fontsize=15)
    if y_axis_label:
        ax.set_ylabel(y_axis_label, fontsize=15)

    if title:
        plt.title(title)

    if legend:
        ax.legend(fontsize=14, markerscale=1.0)

    ax.grid(
        color="grey",
        axis="both",
        linestyle="-",
        alpha=0.2,
        zorder=0,
        linewidth=0.75,
    )
    ax.xaxis.set_tick_params(labelsize=14)
    ax.yaxis.set_tick_params(labelsize=14)

    if save:
        from pinnjax.plot.saving import save_plot

        save_plot(
            fig,
            save_location=save_location,
            save_name=save_name,
            save_format=save_format,
            dpi=dpi,
        )

    if show:
        plt.show()
    else:
        plt.close(fig)
        if show_points:
            plt.close(fig1)

    if show_points:
        return fig, ax, fig1, ax1

    return fig, ax

def value_along_path_plot(
    time_instances: Iterable | float,
    path: Path,
    *,
    model: NeuralNetwork | None = None,
    truth: pathlib.Path | str | None = None,
    domain: SpatialDomain | None = None,
    times: Time | None = None,
    csv_coordinate_column_order: Iterable | None = None,
    csv_truth_column: int = -1,
    fig_size: tuple | None = (10, 5),
    title: str | None = None,
    x_axis_label: str | None = None,
    y_axis_label: str | None = None,
    legend: bool = True,
    show: bool = True,
    save: bool | None = False,
    save_location: str | pathlib.Path | None = None,
    save_name: str | None = "value_along_path",
    save_format: str = "pdf",
    dpi: int = 300,
) -> tuple[Figure, Axes]:
    """Plot a field along a path at selected times.

    A domain supplies the times at which the path is sampled. ``times`` is
    used when no domain is given. The horizontal axis is the sample index,
    not distance along the path. Each selected time is one curve. A model is
    a line. Truth is markers snapped to the nearest CSV row. ``show`` false
    closes the figure.

    Args:
        time_instances: Times to draw. One time or a sequence.
        path: [`Path`][pinnjax.Path] sampled at the travel times.
        model: [`NeuralNetwork`][pinnjax.model.NeuralNetwork].
        truth: CSV path. The selected column is the value. The last remaining
            column is time.
        domain: [`SpatialDomain`][pinnjax.SpatialDomain] whose time range is
            sampled.
        times: [`Time`][pinnjax.Time] used when ``domain`` is omitted.
        csv_coordinate_column_order: Column order for the CSV coordinates.
        csv_truth_column: Value column.
        fig_size: Figure size in inches.
        title: Title.
        x_axis_label: Horizontal label.
        y_axis_label: Vertical label.
        legend: Draw one entry per time.
        show: Display the figure.
        save: Write the figure.
        save_location: Directory for the saved file.
        save_name: File name.
        save_format: File format.
        dpi: Resolution used when saving.

    Returns:
        The Matplotlib figure and axes.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If neither ``model`` nor ``truth`` is set.
        ValueError: If neither ``domain`` nor ``times`` is set.
        TypeError: If ``times`` is not a [`Time`][pinnjax.Time].
        ValueError: If the CSV coordinate count does not match the model input
            width.
        TypeError: If ``truth`` is not a path or string.
        ValueError: If ``truth`` is not a CSV file.

    """
    time_instances = jnp.asarray(time_instances)

    if model is None and truth is None:
        msg = "Neither a model or truth has be provided."
        config.LOGGER.error(msg)
        raise ValueError(msg)

    if domain is not None:
        domain_times = domain.times
        if not isinstance(domain, Domain) or domain_times is None:
            msg = "The domain has no time range."
            config.LOGGER.error(msg)
            raise TypeError(msg)
        travel_times = jnp.linspace(
            float(jnp.asarray(domain_times.min)),
            float(jnp.asarray(domain_times.max)),
            int(
                float(jnp.asarray(domain_times.range())) / float(jnp.asarray(domain_times.step)),
            ),
        )
    elif times is not None:
        if isinstance(times, Time):
            travel_times = jnp.linspace(
                times.min,
                times.max,
                int(times.range() / times.step),
            )
        else:
            msg = "'domain' should be type: pinnjax.Domain."
            config.LOGGER.error(msg)
            raise TypeError(msg)
    else:
        msg = "Neither a Domain or Time object has been provided."
        config.LOGGER.error(msg)
        raise ValueError(msg)

    path_locations = path.eval(travel_times)

    if truth is not None:
        if isinstance(truth, (str, pathlib.Path)):
            truth_path = pathlib.Path(truth)
            if truth_path.suffix.lower() != ".csv":
                msg = f"Expected a CSV file, got {truth_path.suffix}"
                config.LOGGER.error(msg)
                raise ValueError(msg)
            truth_np = pl.read_csv(truth_path).to_numpy().astype(float)
            coordinates = jnp.array(
                jnp.delete(truth_np, csv_truth_column, axis=1),
                copy=False,
            )
            if csv_coordinate_column_order is not None:
                coordinates = jnp.array(
                    coordinates[:, csv_coordinate_column_order],
                    copy=False,
                )
            else:
                coordinates = jnp.array(coordinates, copy=False)
            truth_values = jnp.array(truth_np[:, csv_truth_column], copy=False)
        else:
            msg = f"Invalid truth type: {type(truth)}. Use pathlib.Path or str (CSV)."
            config.LOGGER.error(msg)
            raise TypeError(msg)

        if model is not None:
            topology = cast("tuple[int, ...] | None", getattr(model, "topology", None))
            if topology is None:
                msg = "The model has no topology."
                config.LOGGER.error(msg)
                raise ValueError(msg)
            if coordinates.shape[1] != topology[0]:
                msg = (
                    f"Truth coordinates [Columns: {coordinates.shape[1]}] is not "
                    f"consistent with prediction topology [Columns: "
                    f"{topology[0]}] "
                )
                config.LOGGER.error(msg)
                raise ValueError(msg)

        truth_times = jnp.unique(jnp.array(coordinates[:, -1], copy=False))

        tree = KDTree(truth_times[:, None])
        for idx, _time in enumerate(time_instances):
            time_instances = time_instances.at[idx].set(
                truth_times.at[_nearest_neighbor_index(tree, _time)].get(),
            )
        time_instances = jnp.unique(time_instances)

        spatial_coordinates_at_t0 = coordinates[
            jnp.isclose(coordinates[:, -1], truth_times[0], rtol=0.0, atol=1e-12),
            :-1,
        ]

        tree = KDTree(spatial_coordinates_at_t0)
        for idx, point in enumerate(path_locations):
            path_locations = path_locations.at[idx].set(
                spatial_coordinates_at_t0.at[_nearest_neighbor_index(tree, point)].get(),
            )

        path_locations = jnp.unique(path_locations, axis=0)

        spatial_temporal_points = [
            jnp.hstack([path_locations, jnp.full((path_locations.shape[0], 1), ti)])
            for ti in time_instances
        ]

        tree = KDTree(coordinates)
        truth_values_at_points = [
            truth_values[jnp.array([_nearest_neighbor_index(tree, pt_row) for pt_row in pts])]
            for pts in spatial_temporal_points
        ]

    predictions = None
    if model is not None:
        spatial_temporal_points = [
            jnp.hstack([path_locations, jnp.full((path_locations.shape[0], 1), ti)])
            for ti in time_instances
        ]

        predictions = []
        for points in spatial_temporal_points:
            _prediction = jax.vmap(model)(points)
            predictions.append(_prediction.reshape(points.shape[:-1]))

    # --Plotting--
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=fig_size)
    _style(ax)

    colors = cycle(_style_colors())
    legend_labels = []
    legend_handles = []
    for idx, _time in enumerate(time_instances):
        # TODO(@mjryande): Reconsider x-axis (distance somehow)
        #    euclidean distance between points (?)
        color = next(colors)
        if model is not None:
            if predictions is None:
                msg = "Model predictions were not computed."
                config.LOGGER.error(msg)
                raise ValueError(msg)
            ax.plot(range(len(predictions[idx])), predictions[idx], color=color)
        if truth is not None:
            scatter = ax.scatter(
                range(len(truth_values_at_points[idx])),
                truth_values_at_points[idx],
                edgecolors="black",
                marker="o",
                linewidths=0.25,
                s=12,
                color=color,
            )
        else:
            scatter = ax.scatter(
                [],
                [],  # empty data -> used only as a legend proxy
                facecolors=color,
                edgecolors="black",
                marker="o",
                linewidths=0.25,
                s=36,
                zorder=3,
            )
        legend_labels.append(f"t={_time:.2f}s")
        legend_handles.append(scatter)

    if x_axis_label:
        ax.set_xlabel(x_axis_label, fontsize=15)
    if y_axis_label:
        ax.set_ylabel(y_axis_label, fontsize=15)

    if title:
        plt.title(title)

    if legend and legend_handles:
        ax.legend(
            handles=legend_handles,
            labels=legend_labels,
            fontsize=14,
            markerscale=1.0,
        )

    ax.grid(
        color="grey",
        axis="both",
        linestyle="-",
        alpha=0.2,
        zorder=0,
        linewidth=0.75,
    )
    ax.xaxis.set_tick_params(labelsize=14)
    ax.yaxis.set_tick_params(labelsize=14)

    if save:
        from pinnjax.plot.saving import save_plot

        save_plot(
            fig,
            save_location=save_location,
            save_name=save_name,
            save_format=save_format,
            dpi=dpi,
        )

    if show:
        plt.show()
    else:
        plt.close()

    return fig, ax

def plot_loss(
    loss: dict,
    *,
    mode: str = "class",  # ["class", "type"]
    title: str | None = None,
    best_epoch: int | None = None,
    show_grid: bool = True,
    show: bool = True,
    save: bool = False,
    save_location: Path | str | None = None,
    save_name: str | None = None,
    save_format: str = "pdf",
    dpi: int = 300,
) -> tuple[Figure, Axes]:
    """Plot the class or type loss histories.

    The horizontal axis is the one-based step in each series, on a logarithmic
    vertical scale. ``best_epoch`` draws a dashed vertical line. When that
    position is within ``0.35`` of a tick step of an existing tick, the epoch
    is annotated instead of added as a tick. ``show`` false closes the figure
    after it is built.

    Args:
        loss: Histories keyed by ``"class"`` and ``"type"``. Each value maps a
            label to a series.
        mode: ``"class"`` or ``"type"``.
        title: Axes title.
        best_epoch: Epoch to mark.
        show_grid: Draw the axes grid.
        show: Display the figure before returning it.
        save: Write the figure to disk.
        save_location: Directory for the saved figure.
        save_name: File name without the extension. When omitted, the file is
            ``loss_plot_`` plus ``mode``.
        save_format: File extension.
        dpi: Resolution used when saving.

    Returns:
        The Matplotlib figure and axes.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``mode`` is not ``"class"`` or ``"type"``, or that
            entry has no series.
        KeyError: If ``loss`` has no entry for ``mode``.

    """
    if mode not in ("class", "type"):
        msg = f"mode must be 'class' or 'type'. Inputted mode: {mode}"
        config.LOGGER.error(msg)
        raise ValueError(msg)

    fig, ax = plt.subplots()

    _style(ax)

    for label, _loss in loss[mode].items():
        ax.semilogy(range(1, len(_loss) + 1), _loss, label=label)

    if best_epoch is not None:
        ax.axvline(best_epoch, color="k", linestyle="--")

        xticks = jnp.asarray(ax.get_xticks())
        step = jnp.median(jnp.diff(xticks)) if len(xticks) >= 2 else 1.0

        too_close = jnp.any(jnp.abs(xticks - best_epoch) < 0.35 * step)

        if not too_close:
            ax.set_xticks(jnp.sort(jnp.append(xticks, best_epoch)))
        else:
            ax.annotate(
                f"{best_epoch}",
                xy=(best_epoch, 1),
                xycoords=("data", "axes fraction"),
                xytext=(0, 4),
                textcoords="offset points",
                ha="center",
                va="bottom",
                fontsize=9,
                clip_on=False,
            )

    ax.set_xlabel("Epoch")
    ax.set_ylabel("Loss")

    # sometimes the best_epoch line changes the xlim
    max_epoch = max(len(v) for v in loss[mode].values())
    pad = 0.02 * max_epoch  # just slight padding for aesthetics
    ax.set_xlim(1 - pad, max_epoch + pad)

    if title is not None:
        ax.set_title(title)

    ax.grid(show_grid)
    ax.legend()

    if save:
        from pinnjax.plot.saving import save_plot

        save_plot(
            fig,
            save_location=save_location,
            save_name=save_name or f"loss_plot_{mode}",
            save_format=save_format,
            dpi=dpi,
        )

    if show:
        plt.show()
    else:
        plt.close()

    return fig, ax

def plot_evaluation(
    evaluation_dictionary: dict,
    *,
    normalize: bool = False,
    scale: Literal["linear", "semilogy", "semilogx", "loglog"] = "linear",
    best_epoch: int | None = None,
    title: str | None = None,
    show_grid: bool = True,
    show: bool = True,
    save: bool = True,
    save_location: str | Path | None = None,
    save_name: str | None = "evaluation_plot",
    save_format: str = "pdf",
    dpi: int = 300,
) -> tuple[Figure, Axes]:
    """Plot each series in an evaluation dictionary.

    ``"Epochs"`` is the horizontal axis when that entry exists. Repeated epoch
    numbers are stitched so a restarted run keeps increasing. Otherwise the
    axis is the one-based iteration. ``normalize`` scales each series to its
    own minimum and maximum. A constant series is left unchanged. The vertical
    label is ``"Loss"``.

    Args:
        evaluation_dictionary: Metric histories. ``"Epochs"`` is optional.
            Every other entry is a series.
        normalize: Scale each series to the unit interval.
        scale: ``"linear"``, ``"semilogy"``, ``"semilogx"``, or ``"loglog"``.
        best_epoch: Draw a dashed vertical line at this epoch. When that
            position is within ``0.35`` of a tick step of an existing tick, the
            epoch is annotated instead of added as a tick.
        title: Axes title.
        show_grid: Draw the axes grid.
        show: Display the figure before returning it.
        save: Write the figure to disk.
        save_location: Directory for the saved figure.
        save_name: File name without the extension.
        save_format: File extension.
        dpi: Resolution used when saving.

    Returns:
        The Matplotlib figure and axes.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If there is no series other than ``"Epochs"``.

    """

    def _stitch_epochs(_epochs: Sequence[int | float]) -> list[float]:
        out: list[float] = []
        offset = 0.0
        prev: float | None = None
        for e in _epochs:
            e = float(e)
            if prev is not None and e < prev:  # reset detected
                offset += prev
            out.append(e + offset)
            prev = e
        return out

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 4))

    plot_fn_name = "plot" if scale == "linear" else scale
    plot_fn = getattr(ax, plot_fn_name)

    _style(ax)

    series = [(label, v) for label, v in evaluation_dictionary.items() if label != "Epochs"]
    if not series:
        msg = "evaluation_dictionary contains no series to plot."
        config.LOGGER.error(msg)
        raise ValueError(msg)

    # CHANGED: use stitched epochs if provided, else fall back to evaluation steps
    epochs_raw = evaluation_dictionary.get("Epochs")
    if epochs_raw is not None:
        epochs = _stitch_epochs(epochs_raw)
        x_all = epochs
        xlabel = "Epochs"
    else:
        max_len = max(len(v) for _, v in series)
        x_all = list(range(1, max_len + 1))
        xlabel = "Iterations"

    for label, _loss in series:
        y = _loss
        if normalize:
            lo, hi = min(_loss), max(_loss)
            y = [(x - lo) / (hi - lo) if hi > lo else x for x in _loss]

        x = x_all[: len(_loss)]
        plot_fn(x, y, label=label)

    if best_epoch is not None:
        ax.axvline(best_epoch, color="k", linestyle="--")

        xticks = jnp.asarray(ax.get_xticks())
        step = jnp.median(jnp.diff(xticks)) if len(xticks) >= 2 else 1.0

        too_close = jnp.any(jnp.abs(xticks - best_epoch) < 0.35 * step)

        if not too_close:
            ax.set_xticks(jnp.sort(jnp.append(xticks, best_epoch)))
        else:
            ax.annotate(
                f"{best_epoch}",
                xy=(best_epoch, 1),
                xycoords=("data", "axes fraction"),
                xytext=(0, 4),
                textcoords="offset points",
                ha="center",
                va="bottom",
                fontsize=9,
                clip_on=False,
            )

    ax.set_xlabel(xlabel)
    ax.set_ylabel("Loss")
    if title is not None:
        ax.set_title(title)

    if x_all:
        xmin, xmax = float(min(x_all)), float(max(x_all))
        pad = 0.02 * (xmax - xmin if xmax > xmin else 1.0)
        ax.set_xlim(xmin - pad, xmax + pad)

    ax.grid(show_grid)
    ax.legend()

    if save:
        from pinnjax.plot.saving import save_plot

        save_plot(
            fig,
            save_location=save_location,
            save_name=save_name or "evaluation_plot",
            save_format=save_format,
            dpi=dpi,
        )

    if show:
        plt.show()

    return fig, ax

def predict(
    model: NeuralNetwork,
    grid: SpatialGrid,
    time: float | None = None,
    output_index: int | None = 0,
) -> Array:
    """Predict model output on a spatial grid at one time.

    The grid is flattened. A scalar time is appended when ``time`` is set.
    The [`NeuralNetwork`][pinnjax.NeuralNetwork] is evaluated with ``vmap``,
    and the result is reshaped to the spatial grid. A multi-column output
    uses ``output_index``. A single output column is reshaped as it is.

    Args:
        model: [`NeuralNetwork`][pinnjax.NeuralNetwork] to evaluate.
        grid: [`SpatialGrid`][pinnjax.SpatialGrid] of spatial coordinates.
        time: Scalar time appended to every point. Default: spatial
            coordinates only.
        output_index: Column kept when the network returns more than one
            value per point. Default: ``0``.

    Returns:
        The prediction, shaped like the spatial grid without the coordinate
            axis.

    """
    spatial_mesh = grid.coordinates
    spatial_dimensions = spatial_mesh.shape[-1]

    if time is not None:
        t = jnp.full(spatial_mesh[..., :1].shape, jnp.asarray(time))
        _mesh = jnp.concatenate([spatial_mesh, t], axis=-1).reshape(
            -1,
            spatial_dimensions + 1,
        )
    else:
        _mesh = spatial_mesh.reshape(-1, spatial_dimensions)

    _prediction = _predict_flat(model, _mesh)

    prediction_2d = 2
    if _prediction.ndim == prediction_2d and _prediction.shape[1] != 1:
        _prediction = _prediction[:, output_index]

    return _prediction.reshape(spatial_mesh.shape[:-1])

def predict_at_times(
    model: NeuralNetwork,
    grid: SpatialGrid,
    times: Array,
) -> Array:
    """Predict model outputs on a spatial grid at each requested time.

    Every time is appended to the spatial coordinates and evaluated in one
    batch. A multi-column output keeps column 0. A single output column is
    reshaped as it is.

    Args:
        model: [`NeuralNetwork`][pinnjax.NeuralNetwork] to evaluate.
        grid: [`SpatialGrid`][pinnjax.SpatialGrid] of spatial coordinates.
        times: One time per frame.

    Returns:
        Predictions of shape ``(n_times, *spatial_shape)``, in the same order
        as ``times``.

    """
    times_arr = jnp.atleast_1d(jnp.asarray(times))
    spatial = grid.coordinates
    spatial_shape = spatial.shape[:-1]
    flat = spatial.reshape(-1, spatial.shape[-1])
    n_times = times_arr.shape[0]
    n_points = flat.shape[0]
    spatial_dims = flat.shape[-1]
    repeated = jnp.broadcast_to(flat, (n_times, n_points, spatial_dims))
    time_column = jnp.broadcast_to(times_arr[:, None, None], (n_times, n_points, 1))
    points = jnp.concatenate([repeated, time_column], axis=-1).reshape(-1, spatial_dims + 1)
    predictions = jnp.asarray(vmap(model)(points))
    if predictions.ndim == 2 and predictions.shape[1] != 1:
        predictions = predictions[:, 0]
    return predictions.reshape(n_times, *spatial_shape)

def predict_evolution(model: NeuralNetwork, grid: SpatialGrid) -> Array:
    """Predict the field over the full time range of a grid.

    Evaluates the [`NeuralNetwork`][pinnjax.NeuralNetwork] on the
    spatiotemporal coordinates already stored on the
    [`SpatialGrid`][pinnjax.SpatialGrid]. The grid must define a time range.

    Args:
        model: [`NeuralNetwork`][pinnjax.NeuralNetwork] to evaluate.
        grid: [`SpatialGrid`][pinnjax.SpatialGrid] with a time range
            (``has_time`` is true).

    Returns:
        Predictions of shape ``(num_times, *spatial_shape)``.

    Raises:
        pinnjax.InputError: If the grid has no time range.

    """
    if not grid.has_time:
        msg = "Grid must have time_range and num_times for evolution prediction"
        config.LOGGER.error(msg)
        raise config.InputError(msg)

    coords_flat = grid.spatiotemporal_coordinates.reshape(
        -1,
        grid.spatial_dimensions + 1,
    )
    predictions: Array = jnp.asarray(vmap(model)(coords_flat))
    spatial_shape = grid.coordinates.shape[:-1]
    return predictions.reshape(grid.num_times, *spatial_shape)

def run_prediction(
    model: NeuralNetwork,
    domain: SpatialDomain,
    *,
    fixed_coordinates: dict[str, float] | None = None,
    num_points: tuple[int, int] = DEFAULT_GRID_NUM_POINTS,
    num_times: int = DEFAULT_GRID_NUM_TIMES,
) -> tuple[Array, RectangularGrid2D]:
    """Run an evolution prediction on a 2D slice.

    Builds a [`RectangularGrid2D`][pinnjax.RectangularGrid2D] over
    ``domain.times`` and evaluates
    [`predict_evolution`][pinnjax.predict_evolution]. An omitted slice holds
    ``z`` at the domain maximum. ``num_points`` is ``(nx, ny)`` along the free
    axes. The stored field is ``(num_times, ny, nx)``.

    Args:
        model: [`NeuralNetwork`][pinnjax.NeuralNetwork] to evaluate.
        domain: [`SpatialDomain`][pinnjax.SpatialDomain] with a positive time
            range.
        fixed_coordinates: Axis name to the constant value. When omitted,
            ``z`` is held at ``domain.max[2]``.
        num_points: Sample counts ``(nx, ny)`` for the free axes.
        num_times: Number of times, including both ends.

    Returns:
        The predictions, shaped ``(num_times, ny, nx)``, and the grid.

    Raises:
        TypeError: If ``domain`` is not a
            [`SpatialDomain`][pinnjax.SpatialDomain].
        ValueError: If ``domain`` has no time range, or the range is not
            positive.
        pinnjax.InputError: If the fixed axes do not leave two free axes.

    """
    if not isinstance(domain, SpatialDomain):
        raise TypeError(
            "run_prediction requires a SpatialDomain (evolution uses domain.times). "
            f"Got {type(domain).__name__}.",
        )
    if domain.times is None:
        raise ValueError("SpatialDomain has no times; cannot run evolution prediction.")
    t_min, t_max = float(domain.times.min), float(domain.times.max)
    if t_max <= t_min:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Domain time range is non-positive (min={t_min}, max={t_max}). "
            "Evolution prediction would be constant (e.g. initial condition only).",
        )
    time_range = (t_min, t_max)
    if fixed_coordinates is None:
        fixed_coordinates = {"z": float(domain.max[2])}
    grid = RectangularGrid2D(
        domain=domain,
        fixed_coordinates=fixed_coordinates,
        num_points=num_points,
        time_range=time_range,
        num_times=num_times,
    )
    predictions = predict_evolution(model, grid)
    return predictions, grid

def run_prediction_at_time(
    model: NeuralNetwork,
    domain: SpatialDomain | None = None,
    time: float = 0.0,
    *,
    fixed_coordinates: dict[str, float] | None = None,
    num_points: tuple[int, int] = DEFAULT_GRID_NUM_POINTS,
) -> tuple[Array, RectangularGrid2D]:
    """Predict a 2D slice at one time.

    Builds a [`RectangularGrid2D`][pinnjax.RectangularGrid2D] and evaluates
    [`predict`][pinnjax.predict.base.predict]. An omitted domain uses ``model.domain``.
    An omitted slice holds ``z`` at the domain maximum. ``num_points`` is
    ``(nx, ny)`` along the free axes. The stored field is ``(ny, nx)``.

    Args:
        model: [`NeuralNetwork`][pinnjax.NeuralNetwork] to evaluate.
        domain: [`SpatialDomain`][pinnjax.SpatialDomain]. When omitted,
            ``model.domain`` is used.
        time: Time of the snapshot.
        fixed_coordinates: Axis name to the constant value. When omitted,
            ``z`` is held at ``domain.max[2]``.
        num_points: Sample counts ``(nx, ny)`` for the free axes.

    Returns:
        The prediction, shaped ``(ny, nx)``, and the spatial grid.

    Raises:
        TypeError: If neither ``domain`` nor ``model.domain`` is set, or the
            domain is not a [`SpatialDomain`][pinnjax.SpatialDomain].

    """
    resolved = domain if domain is not None else model.domain
    if resolved is None:
        raise TypeError(
            "run_prediction_at_time requires domain or model.domain to be set.",
        )
    domain = _as_spatial_domain(resolved, context="run_prediction_at_time")
    if fixed_coordinates is None:
        fixed_coordinates = {"z": float(domain.max[2])}
    grid = RectangularGrid2D(
        domain=domain,
        fixed_coordinates=fixed_coordinates,
        num_points=num_points,
    )
    prediction = predict(model, grid, time=float(time))
    return prediction, grid

def from_stl(
    to: FileType,
    file: str | Path,
    *,
    folder: str | Path | None = None,
    name: str | None = None,
    verbose: bool = False,
) -> None:
    """Convert an STL file or directory to a smaller mesh file.

    ``"hdf5"`` writes ``float32`` points and ``uint32`` faces to a
    gzip-compressed ``.h5`` file. ``"npz"`` writes those arrays to a compressed
    ``.npz`` archive. ``"ply"`` writes a binary PLY mesh. A directory is
    searched recursively for ``.stl`` files and written in numeric filename
    order. ``verbose`` logs that progress.

    Args:
        to: ``"hdf5"``, ``"ply"``, or ``"npz"``.
        file: STL file, or a directory of STL files.
        folder: Output directory. A directory input keeps each file's relative
            folder. When omitted, the source file's folder.
        name: Output file name. A different suffix warns and is replaced.
            Only the file name is kept. When omitted, the source stem plus the
            format suffix.
        verbose: Log directory progress.

    Returns:
        ``None``.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``name`` is set while ``file`` is a directory.
        ValueError: If ``file`` is not an STL file.
        ValueError: If ``to`` is not ``"hdf5"``, ``"ply"``, or ``"npz"``.

    """
    file = Path(file)

    if file.is_dir():
        if name is not None:
            raise ValueError("'name' cannot be used when converting a directory.")

        stl_files = sorted(
            (path for path in file.rglob("*") if path.is_file() and path.suffix.lower() == ".stl"),
            key=lambda path: [
                int(part) if part.isdigit() else part.lower()
                for part in re.split(r"(\d+)", str(path.relative_to(file)))
            ],
        )
        total = len(stl_files)
        for index, stl_file in enumerate(stl_files, start=1):
            if folder is None:
                output_folder = None
            else:
                relative_folder = stl_file.parent.relative_to(file)
                output_folder = Path(folder) / relative_folder

            from_stl(
                to,
                stl_file,
                folder=output_folder,
            )

            if verbose:
                width = len(str(total))
                percent = index / total * 100

                config.LOGGER.info(f"[{index:>{width}}/{total}] {percent:5.1f}% {stl_file.name}")

        return

    if file.suffix.lower() != ".stl":
        raise ValueError(f"Expected an STL file, got {file.suffix!r}")

    mesh = trimesh.load_mesh(file)

    points = np.asarray(mesh.vertices, dtype=np.float32)
    faces = np.asarray(mesh.faces, dtype=np.uint32)

    suffixes = {
        "npz": ".npz",
        "hdf5": ".h5",
        "ply": ".ply",
    }
    suffix = suffixes[to]

    output_folder = Path(folder) if folder is not None else file.parent
    output_folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    if name is None:
        output_name = file.stem + suffix
    else:
        output_name = Path(name)

        if output_name.suffix:
            if output_name.suffix.lower() != suffix:
                warnings.warn(
                    f"Expected suffix {suffix!r}, got {output_name.suffix!r}. Replacing it.",
                    stacklevel=2,
                )

            output_name = output_name.with_suffix(suffix)
        else:
            output_name = output_name.with_suffix(suffix)

        output_name = output_name.name

    output_path = output_folder / output_name

    match to:
        case "npz":
            npz_path = cast("str", output_path)

            np.savez_compressed(
                npz_path,
                points=points,
                faces=faces,
            )

        case "hdf5":
            import h5py

            with h5py.File(output_path, "w") as f:
                f.create_dataset(
                    "points",
                    data=points,
                    compression="gzip",
                    shuffle=True,
                )
                f.create_dataset(
                    "faces",
                    data=faces,
                    compression="gzip",
                    shuffle=True,
                )

        case "ply":
            mesh.export(
                output_path,
                file_type="ply",
                encoding="binary",
            )

        case _:
            raise ValueError(
                f"File type must be in FileType {get_args(FileType)}. Got '{to}'.",
            )

def scan_images_nchw(
    images,
    height_channel: int = 0,
    channel_count: int | None = None,
):
    """Return scan tensors as ``(N, C, H, W)``.

    ``(H, W)`` becomes one single-channel image. A 4D array is kept as
    ``(N, C, H, W)``. A 3D array is one multichannel crop or a batch of
    single-channel maps. ``(6, 31, 155)`` can be six maps or one six-channel
    crop. ``channel_count`` resolves it: a first axis equal to that count is
    channels, and any other first axis is a batch. Scan metadata records the
    count as ``channel_count``. Without it, the first axis is channels when
    it is greater than ``height_channel``, at most 16, and smaller than both
    spatial axes, which must each be at least 16. That guess warns.

    Notes:
        N = batch size / number of samples
        C = number of channels
        H = image height
        W = image width

    Args:
        images: Array-like scan images.
        height_channel: Channel index used when a 3D shape is guessed.
            Default: ``0``.
        channel_count: Number of channels in one crop. Default: guess from
            the shape.

    Returns:
        ``(N, C, H, W)`` array.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``images`` is not rank 2, 3, or 4.

    """
    arr: np.ndarray = np.asarray(images)
    channel = int(height_channel)
    if arr.ndim == 2:
        return arr[None, None, ...]
    if arr.ndim == 4:
        return arr
    if arr.ndim != 3:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Expected (H, W), (N, H, W), (C, H, W) or (N, C, H, W); got shape {arr.shape}.",
        )
    if channel_count is not None:
        if arr.shape[0] == int(channel_count):
            return arr[None, ...]
        return arr[:, None, ...]
    if _looks_like_channel_stack(tuple(arr.shape), channel):
        warnings.warn(
            f"Reading shape {arr.shape} as one crop with {arr.shape[0]} "
            "channels. A batch of that many single-channel height maps has "
            "the same shape; pass channel_count to disambiguate.",
            stacklevel=2,
        )
        return arr[None, ...]
    return arr[:, None, ...]

def height_maps_from_scan(
    images,
    height_channel: int = 0,
    channel_count: int | None = None,
):
    """Return ``(N, H, W)`` height from a scan tensor.

    Images are arranged with
    [`scan_images_nchw`][pinnjax.scan_images_nchw]. ``height_channel`` selects
    the returned channel. Default ``0`` is the relative-height channel in the
    scan metadata. A mask or gradient channel is returned only when its index
    is selected.

    Args:
        images: Array-like scan images. Accepts ``(H, W)``, ``(N, H, W)``,
            ``(C, H, W)``, or ``(N, C, H, W)``.
        height_channel: Channel read as height. Default: ``0``.
        channel_count: Number of channels in one crop. Default: guess from
            the shape.

    Returns:
        Height maps shaped ``(N, H, W)``.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``images`` is not rank 2, 3, or 4, or
            ``height_channel`` is outside the channel axis.

    """
    nchw = scan_images_nchw(images, height_channel, channel_count)
    channel = int(height_channel)
    if not 0 <= channel < nchw.shape[1]:
        raise ValueError(
            f"height_channel={channel} is invalid for tensor shape {nchw.shape}.",
        )
    return nchw[:, channel]

class UniformSampler(SamplingMethod):
    """Uniform-grid samples mapped onto a [`Shape`][pinnjax.geometry.base.Shape].

    - `mode` determines how `sampling_value` is interpreted:
    - `"grid_resolution"` is based on [`estimate_nsamples()`][pinnjax.geometry.base.Shape.estimate_nsamples].
        - This value is then reduced based on the dimensionality of the sample space.
    - `"density"` is based on the measured length, area, or volume of the associated [`Shape`][pinnjax.geometry.base.Shape].

    """

    def __init__(  # noqa: D107
        self,
        sampling_value: float = 0.1,
        *,
        mode: SpatialSampleMode = "grid_resolution",
        multiplier: float = 1.0,
    ) -> None:
        self.sampling_value = sampling_value
        self.mode = mode
        self.multiplier = multiplier

    def __call__(
        self,
        shape: Shape,
        sampling_value: float | None = None,
    ) -> Array:
        """Draw a uniform grid and map it onto the shape.

        Args:
            shape: [`Shape`][pinnjax.Shape] to sample.
            sampling_value: Value interpreted by ``mode``.

        Returns:
            Points shaped ``(n_samples, dims)``.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If `multiplier` or `sampling_value` is less than or equal to 0.
            TypeError: If ``mode`` is not one of the two spatial sampling modes.

        """
        if sampling_value is None:
            sampling_value = self.sampling_value

        if sampling_value <= 0:
            msg = f"`sampling_value` must be positive. Got {sampling_value}."
            config.LOGGER.error(msg)
            raise ValueError(msg)

        if self.multiplier <= 0:
            msg = f"`multiplier` must be positive. Got {self.multiplier}."
            config.LOGGER.error(msg)
            raise ValueError(msg)

        mode = self.mode.lower()
        if mode not in ("grid_resolution", "density"):
            msg = f"Invalid 'mode': {self.mode}."
            config.LOGGER.error(msg)
            raise TypeError(msg)

        grid_dims = len(shape.grid_shape(1.0))
        if isinstance(shape.times, Time):
            grid_dims -= 1

        if mode == "grid_resolution":
            resolution = sampling_value
            if grid_dims > 0:
                resolution /= self.multiplier ** (1 / grid_dims)
        else:
            if grid_dims > 0:
                resolution = (sampling_value * self.multiplier) ** (-1 / grid_dims)
            else:
                resolution = 1.0

        if isinstance(shape, Triangle):
            return self._triangle_grid(shape, resolution)

        grid_shape = tuple(max(n, 1) for n in shape.grid_shape(resolution))

        if grid_shape:
            axes = [(jnp.arange(n, dtype=config.get_dtype()) + 0.5) / n for n in grid_shape]
            mesh = jnp.meshgrid(*axes, indexing="ij")
            unit_samples = jnp.stack([axis.reshape(-1) for axis in mesh], axis=-1)
        else:
            unit_samples = jnp.empty((1, 0), dtype=config.get_dtype())

        samples = shape.transform(unit_samples)

        return jnp.asarray(samples, dtype=config.get_dtype())

    def _triangle_grid(self, shape: Triangle, resolution: float) -> Array:
        """Create a uniform triangular lattice inside a triangle."""
        area = float(shape.measure())
        target_samples = max(1, round(area / resolution**2))

        n = max(1, round((float(jnp.sqrt(1 + 8 * target_samples)) - 1) / 2))

        points = []

        for i in range(n):
            for j in range(n - i):
                u = (i + 1 / 3) / n
                v = (j + 1 / 3) / n

                point = shape.a + u * (shape.b - shape.a) + v * (shape.c - shape.a)
                points.append(point)

        spatial = jnp.stack(points)

        if shape.single_time is not None:
            time = jnp.full(
                (spatial.shape[0], 1),
                shape.single_time,
                dtype=config.get_dtype(),
            )
            return jnp.concatenate([spatial, time], axis=1)

        if shape.times is not None:
            n_time = max(1, round(float((shape.tmax - shape.tmin) / shape.tstep)))
            unit_time = (jnp.arange(n_time, dtype=config.get_dtype()) + 0.5) / n_time
            time = shape.tmin + unit_time * (shape.tmax - shape.tmin)

            n_space = spatial.shape[0]
            spatial = jnp.repeat(spatial, n_time, axis=0)
            time = jnp.tile(time, n_space)[:, None]

            return jnp.concatenate([spatial, time], axis=1)

        return jnp.asarray(spatial, dtype=config.get_dtype())
